decision_maker: Executive Director Resources & Partnerships (Stephan Van Arendsen)
purpose:
To authorise the award of a £0.020m
grant from the from the Pride in Place funding provision within the
Knowsley Community Fund to AFC Knowsley CIC to allow the club to
undertake works to complete grounds improvements at Lord Derby
Memorial Playing Fields that would help them achieve Step 6 ground
grading in football for the coming season.
content:
To authorise the award of a £0.020m
grant from the from the Pride in Place funding provision within the
Knowsley Community Fund to AFC Knowsley CIC to allow the club to
undertake works to complete grounds improvements at Lord Derby
Memorial Playing Fields that would help them achieve Step 6 ground
grading in football for the coming season.
 

That the Executive
Director (Resources and Partnerships), in consultation with the
Leader of the Council:
 
a)   
Approve an early allocation of £0.020m from the Pride in
Place funding provision within the Knowsley Community Fund, ahead
of formal Cabinet approval of the full Fund allocation, to AFC
Knowsley CIC to support the delivery of ground improvements at Lord
Derby Memorial Playing Fields.
 
b)   
Note the requirement to address the criteria stipulated within the
Pride in Place Grant Funding Programme; and
 
c)   
Authorise the Head of Legal Services to enter any necessary legal
agreements.
 

Works on the grounds of Lord Derby Memorial
Playing Fields to achieve Step 6 football standards are already
underway, though have yet to be completed. These works need to be
completed by the 30 September 2026 for the club to be eligible to
be part of Step 6 football competitions.  Although a suite of external funding applications
are currently applied for and awaiting
approval, this leaves a short-term cash flow issue for the Club, if
this deadline is to be met.  Therefore,
there is a need to support the sustainability of the club to cover
this short-term cash flow issue and ensure continued function of
the site for the benefit of the community.
 
If no action was to be taken at this time, the
club would be unable to reach Step 6 standard, which will then
create issues of sustainability for their operations at the
site.  As a result, a key outdoor sports
asset serving the locality would be at risk of being lost.

decision_maker: Head of Housing and Property (Barry Fawcett)
purpose:
The purpose of this report is to seek
approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 7.7.1
(Schedule 1), for the award of contract to arc4 Ltd to undertake
the Knowsley Strategic Housing Market Assessment, to run
from 12 October 2026, to 31 March
2027.  The Knowsley Strategic Housing
Market Assessment will be a key part of the evidence base to
develop the Council’s new Housing Strategy and Local Plan;
and will also support the development of other housing and planning
policies / strategies / initiatives.
 
The reason for the decision is that a
compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 7, and the winning bidder has been
identified as providing the most advantageous offer to the
Council.
content:
The purpose of this report is to seek
approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 7.7.1
(Schedule 1), for the award of contract to arc4 Ltd to undertake
the Knowsley Strategic Housing Market Assessment, to run
from 12 October 2026, to 31 March
2027.  The Knowsley Strategic Housing
Market Assessment will be a key part of the evidence base to
develop the Council’s new Housing Strategy and Local Plan;
and will also support the development of other housing and planning
policies / strategies / initiatives.
 
The reason for the decision is that a
compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 7, and the winning bidder has been
identified as providing the most advantageous offer to the
Council.
 

That the Head of Housing
and Property is recommended, in accordance with Contract Procedure
Rule 7.7.1 (Schedule 1), to: -
 
(i)   
approve the award of a contract to arc4 Ltd to undertake the
Knowsley Strategic Housing Market Assessment from 12 October 2026
to 31 March 2027, including options to extend for further periods
of time up to the completion of the project.
(ii)  
authorise the Procurement Team to make the necessary arrangements
for the issue of the relevant contract documentation after conclusion of the call-in
period / standstill period.
 

Deliver in house: This option was considered
and rejected because there is insufficient specific expertise or
resource within the Council to deliver this work.  The Council’s Local Plan will be subject to
consultation and external examination. 
The appointment of a specialist consultancy / organisation to
produce a Strategic Housing Market Assessments for the Council will
support robustness and soundness of evidence base for the
development of both the new Housing Strategy and new Local
Plan.  The Local Plan will also be
subject to consultation and an external examination and the skills,
knowledge and experience a specialist organisation will provide
through the work being undertaken (including future support where
necessary), will support the Council in delivering a compliant plan
to meet Knowsley’s needs and respond to potential
challenges.

content:
The purpose of this report is to seek
approval, in accordance with The Public Contact Regulations 2015,
Regulation 33 (8), to awarded to e2e-assure Ltd for the protective
monitoring and 24/7 Security Operations Centre (SOC) from
21st November 2026 to 20th November 2029, including the
option to extend for a further 12-month period, to 20th November
2030.
 
The reason for the decision is that a
compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in accordance
with The Public Contact Regulations 2015, Regulation 33 (8), using
the Government Commercial Agency, G-Cloud 14 Framework. The
provider which has been identified as part of the call off process
has been evaluated and is considered to provide an offer which is
acceptable to the Council in accordance with the councils
specification.
 

(i)            
That, in accordance with The Public Contact Regulations 2015,
Regulation 33 (8), a call off contract be awarded to e2e-assure
Ltd. for the protective monitoring and 24/7 Security Operations
Centre (SOC) from 21st November 2026 to 20th November
2029, including the option to extend for a further 12-month period,
to 20th November 2030.
(ii)           
 
Procurement Team
be authorised to make the necessary arrangements for the issue of
the relevant contract documentation after conclusion of the call-in
period

The availability of a skilled Security
Operations Centre (SOC) team with an in-depth understanding of our
environment ensures that security events are assessed, triaged, and
responded to promptly and effectively. This reduces response times,
enables more accurate decision-making, and strengthens the
organisation's overall security posture and resilience. In the
current cyber security landscape, where threat actors operate
continuously and attacks such as ransomware, business email
compromise, and exploitation of newly disclosed vulnerabilities can
occur at any time, the ability to detect and respond to threats on
a 24/7 basis is increasingly critical. Delays in identifying and
containing incidents can significantly increase the potential
impact on services, data, and operational continuity.
 
Furthermore, the supplier's 24/7 operating
model provides continuous monitoring and incident response
capabilities, ensuring that potential threats are identified and
managed regardless of the time or day. This supports compliance
obligations, incident management requirements, and business
continuity objectives, while reducing the likelihood of security
incidents escalating into major service disruptions. Collectively,
these benefits were key factors in identifying the supplier as
offering the most advantageous solution, delivering enhanced risk
mitigation, operational effectiveness, and assurance that the
organisation remains protected against an evolving and increasingly
sophisticated cyber threat landscape.

decision_maker: Chief Executive (James Duncan)
purpose:
The proposed staffing restructure will
strengthen domestic abuse services, improve support pathways for
victims and survivors, and enhance early intervention for children
affected by domestic abuse.
The report seeks approval to:
 

Establish two Principal Officer
posts within the Community Safety (Domestic Abuse) Service
(Grade P, SCP 40–41) (Appendix A). These posts will provide
additional management capacity and oversight within the team,
ensuring the specialist in-house service can effectively respond to
residents experiencing domestic abuse, while maintaining compliance
with HR, operational and escalation procedures.
Approve the assimilation of
existing Senior Practitioners (Grade M, SCP 34–35) into
the new Principal Officer roles.

 
Whilst the Principal Officer posts are new
posts, elements of the role build on responsibilities currently
undertaken within the Senior Practitioner function and new
responsibilities to support the Operational Service Manager and
therefore meet the criteria for assimilation. This will also create
future development opportunities within the service and support
recruitment at entry level moving forward.
 
The Principal Officers will continue to
provide additional capacity to support service development,
oversight of complex and high-risk cases, and implementation of the
Knowsley Domestic Abuse Review Recommendations 2024 and forthcoming
Domestic Abuse Strategy. The revised structure will also strengthen
succession planning, support staff retention, and provide a
long-term career progression pathway for every member of the
Domestic Abuse Service, both now and in the future.

strengthen domestic abuse services, improve support pathways for
victims and survivors, and enhance early intervention for children
affected by domestic abuse.
The report seeks approval to:
 

Establish two Principal Officer
posts within the Community Safety (Domestic Abuse) Service
(Grade P, SCP 40–41) (Appendix A). These posts will provide
additional management capacity and oversight within the team,
ensuring the specialist in-house service can effectively respond to
residents experiencing domestic abuse, while maintaining compliance
with HR, operational and escalation procedures.
Approve the assimilation of
existing Senior Practitioners (Grade M, SCP 34–35) into
the new Principal Officer roles.

 
Whilst the Principal Officer posts are new
posts, elements of the role build on responsibilities currently
undertaken within the Senior Practitioner function and new
responsibilities to support the Operational Service Manager and
therefore meet the criteria for assimilation. This will also create
future development opportunities within the service and support
recruitment at entry level moving forward.
 
The Principal Officers will continue to
provide additional capacity to support service development,
oversight of complex and high-risk cases, and implementation of the
Knowsley Domestic Abuse Review Recommendations 2024 and forthcoming
Domestic Abuse Strategy. The revised structure will also strengthen
succession planning, support staff retention, and provide a
long-term career progression pathway for every member of the
Domestic Abuse Service, both now and in the future.
 

The Assistant Chief Executive
in consultation with Executive Director (Resources and
Partnerships) approves:
 

The disestablishment
of a Senior Practitioner post (Grade M);
The disestablishment
of the Team Manager post (Grade P);
The establishment of
two Principal Officer posts (Grade P);
and
The assimilation of
the two Senior Practitioner Grade M postholders into the newly
established Principal Officer posts.

 

Maintain the existing structure, this has been
discounted as this would be less effective to meet longer term
service needs and demands of the service.

breaks from caring for carers of disabled children; and to support

It would also have negative impact on the

Deliver in house:
This option was considered and rejected
because there is no current capacity within the Council to provide
this service. Whilst the Council does have its own internal respite
offer, this would not provide adequate support to meet the demand
for short breaks.

decision_maker: Executive Director Children & Young People (Mark Mirfin) & Executive Director Resources & Partnerships (Stephan Van Arendsen)
purpose:
The Council has a statutory duty to secure suitable
home to school transport for eligible children and young
people.
 
The Council has established a framework of providers
for Travel Support Services and undertaken procurement during 2026
to establish new contracts across 15 lots.
 
Due to unforeseen issues arising during the
implementation of new contractual arrangements for the provision of
home to school transport services, there is an immediate risk to
the continuity of transport provision from 2 September 2026 in
relation to lot 4 [part]. At the present time, these matters are still being
resolved and a longer-term solution is
being progressed.
 
In order to ensure that eligible children and young
people are able to access education and that the Council can
continue to discharge its statutory responsibilities, it is
necessary to put in place interim transport arrangements from the
start of the academic year.
 
Council officers have therefore identified suitable
providers that were able to mobilise services at short notice and
provide continuity of transport provision whilst the outstanding
contractual and operational matters are resolved.
 
Approval is therefore sought, in accordance with the
emergency provisions set out in Contract Procedure Rule 9.1.3
(Schedule 1), to award contracts for the period of 2 September 2026
to 31 December 2026. The estimated value of the temporary contract
is £0.042m.
 
Officers within the Whole Life Commissioning Team and
Travel Support Team reviewed the costs for the urgent provision
period submitted by providers compared to the costs submitted
during procurement.  Although there
are small variances they are considered reasonable for the
delivery of the contract for the period.  The cost of the provision will be met from the
approved Home to School Transport budget.
 
The temporary arrangement will ensure continuity of
service, minimise disruption to children, young people and
families, and provide sufficient time for the Council to establish
longer-term arrangements.
 
An Equality Impact Assessment
has been undertaken and no adverse
equality impacts have been identified arising from the proposed
decision.
 
A further report will be
brought forward should any additional approvals be required in
relation to longer-term arrangements. 
The decisions made here will also be reported to a future Cabinet
meeting.

decision_maker: Director Corporate Support (Justin Thompson) and Director Of Education and Inclusion (Chris Price)
purpose:
The purpose of this report is to seek
permission, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2
(e))for an exemption from Contract Procedure Rules 6 and 7 to award
a contract without competition to St Helens and Knowsley Community
College for the delivery of a Study Programme for young people aged
16 and over.
 
This exemption is justified as the
requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e) are met as
follows:
 
e.       Any other
exceptional circumstances.
 
The following circumstances are considered
exceptional justifying the awarding of a contract without
competition.  The DfE agreed
funding for this programme to be delivered in July 2026 leaving no
time to complete the procurement process and give the college
notice before the start of the academic year. We have to apply for
the funding annually and it is not guaranteed. Last year the
contract was awarded to Knowsley Community College but due to the
delay of going through the procurement process the course did not
start until January 2026 (rather than September 2025). Usually, the
DfE deadline for awarding funding is in April which would still
leave a relatively short period of time to complete the procurement
process for a September start date. This year the deadline was even
later (30 June 2026) and therefore there was no time to go through
the procurement process before the start of the academic year. If a
full competitive process were to be applied on this occasion, then
we would not be able to deliver the study programme during academic
year 2026/2027 and therefore the Council would lose funding from
the DfE. Once we lose this funding, we will not be able to acquire
it again. The study programme is an important part of the
Council’s strategy for reducing NEET in the Borough so we
would not want to risk losing funding for it going forward.

By Director
(Corporate Support):
 
(i)             
That an exemption from Contract Procedure Rules 6 and 7 be granted,
in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e), to permit the
award of a contract without competition for the delivery of a Study
Programme for young people aged 16 and over.
 
By Director
(Education and Inclusion):
 
(ii)       That a contract be
awarded without competition to St Helens and Knowsley Community
College 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027 for the delivery of a
Study Programme for young people aged 16 and over
 
(iii)      That the Procurement Team
be authorised to make the necessary arrangements for the issue of
the relevant contract documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected because the Council would lose the funding from the DfE
going forward and it is important that we do not lose this
funding.
 
Deliver in house: This option was considered
and rejected due to the Council not having the staff in place who
could deliver the programme.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): The
timescales for the procurement process would mean that the Council
would not actually be able to deliver the study programme during
the academic year 2026/2027 and therefore would lose the funding to

applied for annually and is not guaranteed.  Usually, the funding is applied for in April each
year but this year it was moved back by the DfE to 30 June 2026.
Therefore, once the Council received confirmation in July that the
study programme could go ahead there was not sufficient time to
start a full competitive process.

purpose:

with regulations 6(6) and 10 of the Health Care Services (Provider
Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 is to:
 

(i)       identify the most
suitable provider for the
delivery of the Knowsley 0 – 19(25) Healthy Child
Service; and

 

(ii)      seek approval to issue a notice of intention to award that contract, and,
subject to the decision not being called-in and the standstill
period concluding without an unresolved challenge, for that
contract to be awarded.
 
The
justification for this decision, as required by relevant
regulations, is that the Council is satisfied that:
 


•             
Direct award processes A or B cannot be
applied to this service.


•             
Direct award process C or the
Competitive process would also not be appropriate for this service,
in the circumstances.
 
A
compliant Most Suitable Provider process has therefore been

content:
The purpose of the report, in accordance
with regulations 6(6) and 10 of the Health Care Services (Provider
Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 is to:
 

(i)       identify the most
suitable provider for the
delivery of the Knowsley 0 – 19(25) Healthy Child
Service; and

 

(ii)      seek approval to issue a notice of intention to award that contract, and,
subject to the decision not being called-in and the standstill
period concluding without an unresolved challenge, for that
contract to be awarded.
 
The
justification for this decision, as required by relevant
regulations, is that the Council is satisfied that:
 


•             
Direct award processes A or B cannot be
applied to this service.


•             
Direct award process C or the
Competitive process would also not be appropriate for this service,
in the circumstances.
 
A
compliant Most Suitable Provider process has therefore been
conducted in accordance with the relevant regulations and approval
of its outcome is now being sought.
 


The Director (Corporate Support) and the
Executive Director (Health and Adult Social Care)
agreed:-

 


(i)          
That, in accordance with regulations 6(6)
and 10 of the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime)
Regulations 2023:

 

(a)        Wirral
Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust be identified as the
Most Suitable Provider for the provision of the Knowsley 0 –
19(25) Healthy Child Service ;
 

(b)        Subject to
this decision not being called-in within three working days of
being published, an Intent to Award Notice, as set out in Appendix
A to the report, be issued for publication on the UK e-notification
service, indicating the Council’s proposed award of the
contract to Wirral Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust,
for the period 1 February 2027 to 31 January 2032 with the option
to extend the contract up to a maximum of three 12 month periods
(until 31 January 2035); and
 

(ii)  That,
subject to the subsequent standstill period concluding without an
unresolved challenge, the contract be awarded, and the Procurement
Team authorised to issue the relevant contract award documentation,
including publishing a contract award notice, based on the
information already set out in the draft intent to award notice
(Appendix A) on the UK e-notification service. 

 


Do Nothing: This option was rejected because the Council has a
legal obligation and a statutory public health duty to commission
or provide the Healthy Child Programme, as many elements of the
programme are mandated services, including the universal health
visiting service, five health and development reviews (antenatal,
new birth, 6-8-week, 9-12 month and 2-2 ½ years), and the
National Child Measurement Programme (NCMP). A lack of services
could lead to harm or missed safeguarding risks. It is therefore
essential that there is a 0-19(25) Healthy Child Service in
place.

 

Deliver in
house: This option was
considered and rejected because the 0-19(25) Healthy Child Service
is a highly specialist service, providing clinical support to
residents. The Council does not have the clinical infrastructure or
governance to ensure compliance with healthcare standards at this
time. There are also national shortages of both health visitors and
school nurses, and the Council may struggle to recruit and align
with NHS pay structures.
     
Alternative Provider Selection Regime
Processes:
Direct
Award Process A – This was
rejected as the existing providers are not the only providers that
can deliver the services.
 

Direct Award Process B
– This was rejected as
patients are not offered a choice of provider and team when
accessing these services within the Borough, and the number of
providers is restricted by the Council.
 
Direct Award Process C
- This was rejected as there have been considerable
changes to the specification / contracting value since the current
contract was awarded.
 

Competitive Process
-A competitive process is time-consuming
and could risk a gap in service provision. The 0-19(25) Healthy Child Service is a highly
specialist service, providing clinical support to residents. Many
private providersdo not have the
clinical infrastructure or governance to ensure compliance with
healthcare standards. There are also national shortages of both
health visitors and school nurses; non-NHS Trusts may struggle to
recruit and align with NHS pay structures.
topline: The Executive Directors have decided to award the contract for the Knowsley 0 – 19(25) Healthy Child Service to Wirral Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust.

purpose:
This report seeks
approval to introduce a borough-wide Public Spaces Protection Order
(PSPO) for smoking and vaping in designated areas across Knowsley
for a three-year period.
content:
This report seeks
approval to introduce a borough-wide Public Spaces Protection Order
(PSPO) for smoking and vaping in designated areas across Knowsley
for a three-year period.

The Head of Community Safety in
consultation with the Cabinet Member Communities and
Neighbourhoods, considering the statutory consultation exercise is
recommended to:
 

      
i.        
Approve a three-year borough wide Public Space
Protection Order (Smoking and Vaping) in designated smoke and vape
free zones where children, young people and non-smokers are present
or are reasonably expected to be present to include:
 

a)   
A person must not smoke or vape within any
designated smoke and vape free zone or within 2 meters of any
entrance, exit, or access point to an enclosed public space or
workplace including: 

·    
Playgrounds and Environmental Centres in parks
(including entrances, play equipment areas and associated
seating)

·    
School grounds including the immediate vicinity of
school gates and entrances; 

·    
Youth Centres

·    
Leisure Centres (including main entrances and
forecourts);

·    
Children’s Centres and family
hubs; 

·    
Libraries (external entrances and forecourts open
to the public). This does not include Halewood and Prescot
Libraries;

·    
Shakespeare North Playhouse (external areas under
Council management open to the public).
 

b)   
A person must, when requested by an Authorised
Officer, extinguish any lit smoking material and/or cease vaping
and comply with any reasonable instruction given.
 

Not implementing a borough-wide
PSPO. After under-taking evidence review and statutory consultation
process to was deemed that both support and need were high to
implement a PSPO for smoking and vaping in designated areas across Knowsley for a three-year
period.
topline: The Head of Community Safety has decided to introduce a borough-wide Public Spaces Protection Order for smoking and vaping in designated areas across Knowsley for a three-year period.

purpose:
The purpose of this

Rule 9.4.2(1) to approve the extension of the current contracts
with Askews and Holts Library Services Ltd for the supply of Adult
Books (Lot 1), and Peters Ltd for the supply of Children’s
Books (Lot 2), for a further period of 24 months, from 1 August
2026 to 31 July 2028, in accordance with the terms of the original
contracts.
 
The reason for the
decision is that the original procurement was undertaken through a
compliant process in 2023, led by Rotherham Metropolitan Borough
Council via a mini competition under an ESPO framework agreement.
Rotherham MBC entered into the call-off contracts on behalf of
participating authorities, including those within the Yorkshire and
North West regions, thereby enabling access to the contracts
without the need for separate procurement exercises.
 
The ESPO framework is
a compliant procurement route, and the call-off arrangements were
established in accordance with public procurement regulations.
Rotherham MBC has coordinated with participating authorities and
has formally agreed the extension of the call-off contracts with
the appointed suppliers for the period 1 August 2026 to 31 July
2028.
 
The proposed extension
is expressly provided for within the original contract terms and
remains within the scope and conditions of the initial procurement.
It therefore represents a lawful contract modification and a
compliant route to maintaining service provision.
 
Each participating
authority is required to obtain its own internal approval under its
Contract Procedure Rules. This report seeks that approval to ensure
continued use of the arrangement.
 
The extension will
ensure continuity of service delivery and is considered to
represent value for money to the Council.

e.         Any
other exceptional circumstances.

exceptional justifying the awarding of a contract without

Governance laws.  This leaves the
Council vulnerable to receiving a monetary penalty from the

content:
The purpose of this report is to seek
permission, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e)
for an exemption from Contract Procedure Rules 6 and 7 to award a
contract without competition for refurbishment works on the
Council’s Records Storage Facility.
 
This exemption is justified as the
requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2(e) are met as
follows:
 
e.         Any
other exceptional circumstances.
 
The following circumstances are considered
exceptional justifying the awarding of a contract without
competition due to the current condition of the storage facility
leaving the Council at risk of becoming in breach of Information
Governance laws.  This leaves the
Council vulnerable to receiving a monetary penalty from the
regulator and facing reputational exposure. Considering this, and
the niche market available to complete the works within limited
timescales to prevent further damage to records, it is considered
appropriate to seek an exemption to permit a direct award.
 


(i)         That the
Executive Director (Resources and Partnerships) grants an exemption
from Contract Procedure Rules 6 and 7, in accordance with Contract
Procedure Rule 9.2.2(e) to permit the award of a contract without
competition for refurbishment works to the Council’s Records
Storage Facility;
 

(ii)        that the
Assistant Chief Executive awards a contract, without competition,
to Techbuild Ltd for refurbishment
works to the Council’s Records Storage Facility, from the
date of the decision to the completion of the works; and
 

(iii)      
that the Assistant Chief Executive, authorises the Procurement
Team  to make
the necessary arrangements for the issue of the relevant contract
documentation.
 

The following 3 alternative options were
considered:-
 
Do Nothing: This
option was considered and rejected due to the urgency in which
these works need to be completed.
 
Deliver in house: This
option was considered and rejected because this requirement cannot
be undertaken within Council resources due to the specialist nature
of the works. 
 
Seek Competition
(Quotation / Tender):  On this occasion
a competitive exercise is not possible due to the urgency of the
works which need to be completed. To prevent further damage to
records, the work needs to be completed in the drier months of the
year, before winter. The current state of the containers leaves the
Council in breach of information governance legislation which may
result in a penalty by the regulator and leaves the Council
vulnerable to reputational exposure. Following extensive engagement
with various suppliers over the last 18 months to ascertain options
and costs, it is clear there is an absence of a market for this
work with only Techbuild Ltd identified
as being able to offer this service.
topline: The Assistant Chief Executive and Executive Director Resources & Partnerships have decided to award a contract without competition for urgent refurbishment works on the Council's Records Storage Facility.

content:
To seek approval for the award of a Private
Rent Rescue Scheme grant to Livv
Housing Group to enable the purchase of a residential property
under the scheme.  The grant provided to enable the property
purchase will allow the existing household to continue to live at
the property as a tenant of Livv
Housing Group therefore preventing homelessness and supporting the
Council’s Homelessness and Rough Sleeping Strategy 2025-30
whilst also increasing affordable housing provision in the Borough
through the investment of section 106 commuted sums designated for
this purpose.  
 

The Executive Director (Place) in consultation
with the Cabinet Member for Regeneration and Economic Development
hereby:
 
(i)            
Approves the award of a Private Rent Rescue Scheme grant detailed
in Appendix B to Livv Housing Group for the acquisition of a
residential property on the main terms and conditions referred to
in Appendix A.
 
(ii)           
Authorises the Head of Legal Services to prepare and complete the
necessary legal documentation.
 

Do not purchase the property – this was
rejected. The current owner is intent on selling the property and
because of this has issued a Section 21 Notice seeking possession
of the property.  This means the tenants and their family are
threatened with homelessness.  Not purchasing the property
would result in the current tenants and their family becoming
homeless leaving the Council with further duties to fulfil under
homelessness legislation.  This could include the need to use
temporary accommodation and secure long term permanent
accommodation at a time when the Council is experiencing
significant pressures around homelessness and the availability of
housing to meet housing needs.    Not purchasing the
property would also be a missed opportunity to provide additional
affordable housing in the Borough now and for the future using
Section 106 affordable housing commuted sums secured for this
purpose, whilst also levering in investment from Registered
Provider partners to support the delivery of additional affordable
housing.

content:
To seek authorisation to enter
into a Grant Funding Agreement with Liverpool City Region Combined
Authority relating to the additional highway maintenance funding
for 2026/27.


The Executive Director (Place) and the Executive
Director (Resources & Partnerships) in consultation with the
Cabinet Member for Regeneration and Economic Development and the
Cabinet Member for Resources;

 

a)          
Approve the acceptance of an external grant funding
from Liverpool City Region Combined Authority with a value of
£0.977m.

 

b)          
Agree to the Council entering into a Grant Funding
Agreement with the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority, in
relation to highways maintenance.
 

c)           
Authorise the Head of Legal Services to finalise the
terms of the Grant Funding Agreement referenced in paragraph (b)
above.
 

d)          
Approve the inclusion of £0.977m to the
2026/27 Highways Capital Delivery programme.
 

Not entering into the Grant
Funding Agreement was considered and rejected as this would be a
missed opportunity to use external funding to improve the condition
of the highway network.
 
The condition of all roads in
the Borough was assessed when selecting the schemes. To inform
where and how the funding should be spent, criteria from several
data sources (including current condition, road categorisation,
work type, insurance claims, number of enquiries, reactive
maintenance spend over previous years, size of scheme, and
geographical grouping) are considered when identifying the proposed
works. This process achieves optimum benefits in terms of lifecycle
planning, improved accountability and stewardship of the asset,
better value for money, and improved customer service.
topline: The Executive Director Place and Executive Director Resources & Partnerships have decided to enter into a Grant Funding Agreement with Liverpool City Region Combined Authority for additional highway maintenance funding.

This exemption is justified as the
requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2(e)in relation to
exceptional circumstances are met as follows:
 

These exceptional circumstances mean

The Integrated Care Board (ICB) – NHS Cheshire

to be completed.  This was then paused
following the announcement by the ICB to continue with the

In light of this

transition in line with the ICB’s regional commissioning

Support Service
 
By Executive
Director (Health and Adult Social Care) and Executive Director
(Children and Young People):

currently working with and the need for the service to support
individuals with behaviour that challenges, and to prevent them

Deliver in house:

This option was considered and rejected due to
specialist skills and training required to deliver this service,
training and resources that could not be put in place internally

decision_maker: Executive Director Health and Social Care (Jenny Rollinson)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2.(1) to modify the contract with
KeyRing for the Community Network
Support Scheme as provided for within the existing contract at
clause B1.2 by extending the provision to 30 June 2027.
content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2.(1) to modify the contract with
KeyRing for the Community Network
Support Scheme as provided for within the existing contract at
clause B1.2 by extending the provision to 30 June 2027.
 

(i)   
That, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(1), the
contract with KeyRing for the Community
Network Support Scheme be modified by extending the term as
provided for within the existing contract at clause B1.2 from 1
July 2026 to 30 June 2027.
 
(ii)  
That the Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant
contract modification documentation.
 

ANY ALTERNATIVE
OPTIONS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED:
 

Do Nothing:
If the Council were to take no action and
allow the Community Network Support Scheme contract to expire on 30
June 2026, the service would cease with no alternative preventative
provision in place.
 
The scheme currently supports up to 30
individuals who, without this low?level intervention, would be at
high risk of escalation into statutory Adult Social Care. Evidence
from local commissioning experience indicates that once individuals
present with increased or unmet needs, an average community?based
care package from alternative provision would cost approximately
£400 per person per week.
 
If all 30 individuals required alternative
statutory support, this would equate to:

£400 per
person per week (on average)
£20,800 per
week for 30 people
£624,000
per annum (based on 52 weeks)

 
By comparison, the cost of extending the
KeyRing contract for the same period is
£123,200 per annum.
 
This demonstrates that failure to extend the
contract could expose the Council to over £500,000 of
additional annual costs (£624,000 compared to
£123,200), excluding any further costs associated with crisis
responses, hospital admissions, safeguarding interventions,
homelessness presentations, or supported accommodation
placements.
 
In addition to the direct financial impact,
the withdrawal of the service would remove an established
early?intervention pathway that actively prevents escalation.
Individuals currently supported to sustain tenancies, manage daily
living, and maintain social connections may experience
deterioration in mental health and independence, leading to
increased demand for Care Act assessments, ongoing commissioned
support packages, and unplanned interventions.
 
The do?nothing option therefore presents a
clear risk of false economy. While it would achieve a short?term
saving by ending the contract, this is likely to be significantly
outweighed by the higher costs of statutory Adult Social Care
provision and increased system demand. It would also undermine the
Council’s preventative commissioning approach and financial
sustainability objectives.
 
For these reasons, the option to do nothing
and not extend the contract was considered and rejected.
 

Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
Seeking competition through a quotation or
tender exercise was considered but discounted at this stage. The
current service is performing well, is meeting its core objectives,
and is delivering demonstrable preventative outcomes for
individuals who would otherwise be at high risk of escalation into
statutory Adult Social Care.
 
The proposed contract extension is expressly
provided for within the existing contract and does not represent a
material change to the scope, nature or value of the service. As
such, undertaking a new procurement exercise at this point would
offer limited additional benefit and would risk destabilising a
well?embedded and effective service that vulnerable individuals
rely upon for continuity of support.
 
Undertaking a competitive procurement would
also introduce avoidable service and delivery risks. Mobilisation
of a new provider, or potential service change arising from a
re?tender, could lead to disruption for service users, loss of
established relationships, and reduced engagement, all of which
increase the likelihood of unmet need and escalation into
higher?cost support.
 
In addition, this extension period represents
the final available extension under the contract and is intended to
provide stability while commissioners undertake a wider review of
community?based support services, including alignment with existing
mental health floating support services and emerging reablement
models. Prematurely tendering the service ahead of this strategic
review could result in fragmented commissioning and would risk
locking the Council into contractual arrangements that are not
aligned with future service design.
 
For these reasons, seeking competition at this
time was considered neither proportionate nor in the best interests
of service users or the Council and was therefore rejected.
topline: The Executive Director Health and Social Care has decided to extend the contract with KeyRing for the Community Network Support Scheme until June 2027.

By Executive
Director (Resources and Partnerships):
(i)       That permission be
granted for a contract to be awarded directly, in accordance with
Contract Procedure Rule 9.1.8, to reserve nursing care placements
to support rapid discharge from hospital within Knowsley.
 
By Executive
Director (Health and Adult Social Care):
 
(ii)       That a contract be
awarded without competition to St Helens and Knowsley Caring
Association to reserve ten nursing care placements for Knowsley
Local Authority, to facilitate safe rapid discharge of Knowsley
residents from hospital for the period 25 June 2026 to 24 June
2029.
 
(iii)      That the Procurement Team
be authorised to make the necessary arrangements for the issue of
the relevant contract documentation.
 


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected
because the Council has a statutory duty to ensure a diverse,
sustainable high quality adult social care market, which includes
ensuring sufficient supply of care home provision locally. There is
lack of capacity for general nursing placements in Knowsley and
this is adversely impacting those Knowsley residents in hospital
who have been identified as either requiring a fast-track admission
into a nursing placement or for residents identified as being
medically optimised as they may not be able to find a nursing
placement in borough.
 

Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
On this occasion a successful competitive
exercise was not considered feasible. The Whole Life Commissioning
Team manages the local market position, engages with providers and
are aware of the current availability in the
market. A soft market test undertaken in April 2026
demonstrated that there has been no interest from any
organisations other than the proposed provider who are able to
provide this service presently.
topline: The Executive Directors have decided to award a contract to reserve nursing care placements for Knowsley Local Authority without competition.

decision_maker: Executive Director Health and Social Care (Jenny Rollinson)
purpose:

seek approval to direct award a contract to Northern Healthcare to
deliver Supported Accommodation at Helena’s House, Huyton,
Knowsley for three years with the options of extending up to 24
months.
content:
The purpose of the report is to
seek approval to direct award a contract to Northern Healthcare to
deliver Supported Accommodation at Helena’s House, Huyton,
Knowsley for three years with the options of extending up to 24
months.
 

The Executive Director (Health
and Adult Social Care) is recommended to;
 
a)   
Agree that a contract can be awarded without
competition to Northern Healthcare to deliver Supported
Accommodation at Helena House, Huyton, Knowsley, for three years
beginning Autum 2026 with the option of extending up to 24
months.
b)   
Delegates authority to the Head of Whole Life
Commissioning to award the contract once a start date is
confirmed.
c)   
Authorise the Complex Brokerage Team to make the
necessary arrangements for the issue of the relevant
documentation.
 


Do Nothing:
The option to decommission the care and
support at Helena House was rejected as failure to commission this
scheme will perpetuate a reactive, crisis-led system, increasing
safeguarding risks and placing continued strain on acute and
emergency services.
 

Without this provision, Knowsley
will remain over-reliant on reactive, high-cost crisis responses
(hospital admissions, emergency placements, hotel use).
Lack of local provision increases
safeguarding risks, as people are placed far from oversight,
family, and familiar services.
It creates a “revolving
door” cycle of hospital discharge - breakdown -
readmission.
topline: The Executive Director Health and Social Care has decided to award a contract to Northern Healthcare for Supported Accommodation at Helena's House in Huyton, Knowsley.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The
Knowsley Community Fund will impact all wards of the
Borough.
content:
The
Knowsley Community Fund will impact all wards of the
Borough.
 

         
The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive
Director (Resources and Partnerships) which provided an update on
the Knowsley Community Fund (Round 2 – 2026/27).
 
Councillor G Morgan, Leader of the Council, reported that the
Knowsley Council Plan had a clear vision of supporting
Knowsley’s people and communities to thrive and this had been
underpinned by an ethos of Stronger Communities with a clear focus
on supporting and helping people overcome
inequality. 
 
Councillor Morgan indicated that the Council had established an
annual community grant programme offering grants to Voluntary,
Community, Faith and Social Enterprise Sector organisations in the
Borough. In this respect, those community grants provided much
needed and valuable support to those organisations by enabling them
to design and deliver programmes and activities that positively
impacted Knowsley’s residents and communities. 
 
Councillor Morgan highlighted that, since 2022, between both the
former Stronger Communities Fund and the current Knowsley Community
Fund, £1.8m had been invested in Voluntary, Community, Faith
and Social Enterprise Sector organisations, enabling them to deliver diverse programmes of interventions and
activities. Councillor Morgan indicated that
between 2022 and 2024, over 28,000 residents were supported by
activities delivered utilising this funding, which was also
supported by over 1,000 volunteers who gave up their time to help
deliver community- led projects. Councillor Morgan acknowledged the
invaluable contributions of the community organisations and the
volunteers who supported them.
 
Councillor Morgan reported that the Knowsley Community Fund
would continue to support the Council Plan priorities and, in
particular, the Knowsley Community Fund would focus on the
priorities of encouraging growth that benefits everyone, ensuring
our communities and town centres can flourish and delivering
targeted support to encourage fairness and opportunity for those
residents facing the biggest challenges; 
 
Councillor Morgan indicated that for
the 2026-2027 funding period only, the
Knowsley Community Fund would also fund small capital
projects that supported
community spaces
with a particular focus on improving
sports facilities and securing equipment for sport and physical
activity.
 
Councillor Morgan indicated that the
Knowsley Community Fund would make £730,000
available for community organisations to apply for, which ensures
that the Council could continue to provide
much needed financial support to Knowsley’s voluntary and
community sector for another year, enabling the Council’s
social partners to deliver support to residents across the Borough.
Councillor Morgan acknowledged the continued
support and essential role that Knowsley’s voluntary,
community, faith, and social enterprise sector provided across
Knowsley’s communities, playing a vital role in helping
Knowsley’s people and communities to thrive. 
 
           
RESOLVED – That:-
 

(i)            
the launch of the £0.730m Knowsley Community
Fund 2026/2027 be agreed; and

 

(ii)       
the Guidance Note for the proposed Knowsley
Community Fund 2026/2027 as attached at Appendix A to this report
be agreed.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to launch the £0.730m Knowsley Community Fund for 2026/2027 to provide financial support to voluntary and community sector organizations in the Borough.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:

content:
The report proposes capital expenditure over

The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive
Director (Resources and Partnerships), which explained how the Council’s capital resources
were spent during 2025/26.

 

Councillor Mrs J Lonergan, Cabinet Member
for Resources, reported that the Capital Programme in 2025/26
invested in a wide range of schemes including improvements to
highways across the Borough, disabled facilities and adaptations to
residents’ properties, new mainstream and special school
places and improvements to highways and Town Centres. In this
respect, Councillor Lonergan indicated that the final level of
Capital Programme expenditure for 2025/26 had been
£47.380m. 

 

Councillor Lonergan indicated that the
Council’s total Capital Programme for the next three years
had been £77.110m, of which £66.373m is scheduled to be
spent in 2026/27 and demonstrated the
Council’s continued commitment to investing in the future of
the Borough. 

 

RESOLVED – That:-

 

(a)           
the final outturn position for the
2025/26 Capital Programme as set out in section 4 of this report be
agreed;

 

(b)           
the new three-year Capital Programme of
£77.110m in total as set out in paragraph 4.6 of this report
be approved; and,

 

(c)           
the treasury management
prudential indicators as presented in section 6 of this report be
noted.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a capital expenditure of over £1m for various schemes in the Borough.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The report will approve the allocation of resources and
will therefore need to be a key decision.
content:
The report will approve the allocation of resources and
will therefore need to be a key decision.
 

           
The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive Director
(Resources and Partnerships) which detailed how the Council’s revenue budget was spent
during 2025/26.  

 
Councillor Mrs J Lonergan, Cabinet
Member for Resources, reported that In March 2025, the Council set
a balanced budget for 2025/26 without the need for cuts in
frontline services or a reduction in jobs and the Council was also
made significant new investment in priority areas
aligned to the Council Plan
priorities and the needs of the Borough’s communities. In
this respect, the budget had funded net spending of £217 million on Council
services, as detailed in section 4 of the report.
 
Councillor Lonergan reported that at the end of
2025/26 the Council achieved a balanced overall final position
against its 2025/26 revenue budget. 
However, within the overall position there had been a number of
significant deficits against service budgets which had been offset
by one-off resources which the Council had set aside to manage
unbudgeted service pressures. In this respect, the Council was
reporting a deficit on service budgets of £7.547m, which
represented 3.6% of total service budgets. Councillor Lonergan
highlighted that the service deficit was mainly due to  continued pressures in Children’s Social
Care and Home to School Transport, in addition to an increased
shortfall in Adult Social Care, as highlighted in section 5 of the
report.
 
Councillor Lonergan indicated that
each year service budgets were set to reflect forecasts from
service mangers of future levels of demand and costs, and the
budget that would be needed to address these.  In this respect, Councillor Lonergan highlighted
that based on the forecasts, the 2025/26 budget therefore included additional
investment of £22m, of which £10.5m was in social care
and the final deficit for the year was after this additional
investment, which reflected the difficulty of making accurate
forecasts and the continued severity of growth in demand and
costs. 

 
Councillor Lonergan reported that the
Council’s financial strategy included actions to mitigate the
ongoing impact of the challenges faced by the Council, with a range
of measures to ensure that managers across the Council maintained
robust financial management and remained committed to reducing
budget pressures. In this respect, the Council also ensured that,
where possible, it set aside one-off resources to manage the risk
of unfunded in-year budget pressures. Councillor Lonergan indicated
that the 2025/26 pressures were reflected in the budget estimates
for 2026/27 and would continue to be monitored closely with a
further report being brought to Cabinet in July to provide an
update on the 2026/27 budget monitoring position.

 
Councillor Lonergan also highlighted that the report summarised
the year-end position on the Dedicated Schools Grant and outlined
how Government reforms would affect the financial impact of the
growing financial deficit.

 

RESOLVED - That:-
 

(i)           
the final 2025/26 budget monitoring position for the
Council as set out in this report be noted; and,
 

(ii)           
the allocation of one-off resources to fund the
2025/26 deficit as set out in section 4 of this report be
endorsed.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the allocation of resources to fund the Council's 2025/26 deficit in service budgets.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To approve revision of the Council’s Housing
Enforcement and Housing Civil Penalties policies to incorporate the
provisions of the Renter’s Rights Act 2025
 
This is a key decision since it has the potential to impact
throughout the Borough.
content:
To approve revision of the Council’s Housing
Enforcement and Housing Civil Penalties policies to incorporate the
provisions of the Renter’s Rights Act 2025
 
This is a key decision since it has the potential to impact
throughout the Borough.
 

           
The Cabinet considered the report of the Head of
Safety, Resilience and Community Protection, which sought approval
of a revised Housing Enforcement Policy and Housing Civil Penalties
Policy, which was required to reflect changes to the legislative
framework which have been brought about by the Renters’
Rights Act 2025 (“The Act”). 
 

Councillor G Morgan, Leader of the Council, reported
that the Housing Enforcement Policy would
inform the approach of the Council and its officers to
enforcing legislation that is aimed at improving housing conditions
throughout Knowsley and to protect the health and well-being of
residents across all tenures. In this respect, Councillor Morgan
highlighted that the Housing Civil Penalties Policy set out the
Council’s approach to the use of civil penalties for various
housing related offences as an alternative to prosecution and
described the principles and processes that would be adopted by
council officers in determining when such penalties should be used
and the calculation of the financial amount of each
penalty.
 
Councillor Morgan reported that both policies had been revised
to reflect changes to the legislative framework which have been
brought about by the Renters’ Rights Act 2025, which included
the creation of new offences designed to protect tenants and to
regulate the activity of landlords and letting agents, implementing
a statutory duty to enforce landlord legislation, and increasing
the maximum amount of civil penalties from £30,000 to
£40,000.
 
           
Councillor Morgan indicated that, subject to approval, the policies
would be administered by officers of the Environmental Health and
Community Protection Service and any income received from
enforcement of the policies would be retained by the Council and
used to support enforcement activities in this area.
 
Councillor Morgan indicated that the adoption of both policies
would ensure that all actions taken by Council officers would be
transparent and consistent and that all decisions were robust in
the event of challenges and/or appeals and it would  also ensure that the Council met its statutory
obligations under the Renters’ Rights Act 2025 and would
contribute to the Knowsley Council Plan 2025-2030 by facilitating
access to good quality housing and supporting local people to live
healthy lives.
 

           
RESOLVED – That:-

 

(i)         the
revised policies (as attached at Appendix A and Appendix B to this
report) be approved; and

 

(ii)        the Executive
Director (Place), in consultation with the Cabinet Member
(Communities and Neighbourhoods), be authorised to approve future
amendments to the policies when the further provisions of the Act
are implemented.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the revision of the Council's Housing Enforcement and Housing Civil Penalties policies to incorporate the provisions of the Renter's Rights Act 2025.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Financially significant and affects two or more
wards.
content:
Financially significant and affects two or more
wards.
 

           
The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive Director
(Children and Young People), which provided an update on the development of Knowsley’s Local Special
Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Reform Plan (“the
Plan”), which must be submitted to the Department for
Education by 19 June 2026 as part of the national SEND reform
programme. 
 

Councillor S Donnelly, Cabinet Member for Children
and Young People, reported that the Plan set out how the local area
partnership would deliver sustainable improvement in outcomes for
children and young people with SEND, strengthen inclusion, and
establish a more resilient and financially sustainable local
system.

 

Councillor Donnelly highlighted that the Department
for Education’s approval of the Plan would be based on
confidence in this approach and would be a pre?condition for access
to the High Needs Stability Grant, through which central government
would fund 90% of the Council’s cumulative High Needs Block
(Dedicated Schools Grant) deficit accrued to 31 March
2026.

 

Councillor Donnelly reported that Knowsley’s
cumulative deficit as at 31 March 2026 had been £43.788m,
which highlighted a potential grant support of approximately
£39.4m, subject to approval of the Plan.

 

Councillor Donnelly indicated that the Plan was
attached at Appendix A of the report and approval was sought to
delegate authority to the Chief Executive, the Executive Director
(Resources and Partnerships), and the Executive Director (Children and Young People), in consultation
with the Cabinet Member (Children and Young
People), to approve and submit the final
Local SEND Reform Plan to the Department for Education.

 

RESOLVED – That:-

 

(i)         the
requirement for Knowsley Council, working with its local area
partners, to develop and submit a draft Local SEND Reform Plan to
the Department for Education by 19 June 2026 be noted;

 

(ii)        the progress
made to date in developing the Plan, including the ongoing
programme of partnership engagement and the commissioning of
specialist support to support completion of the Plan be
noted;

 

(iii)       the draft Plan as
set out at Appendix A be noted; and

 

(iv)       the delegation of
authority to the Chief Executive, the Executive Director (Resources
and Partnerships), and the Executive Director (Children and Young
People), in consultation with the Cabinet Member (Children and
Young People), to approve and submit the final Plan by 19 June 2026
be approved.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to delegate authority for the submission of Knowsley's Local SEND Reform Plan by 19 June 2026.

in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation

(e) where the
modifications, irrespective of their value, are not substantial

(b) 
introduce additional conditions that would have influenced the

content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation
72(1)(e) to modify four Adult Social Care contracts, as detailed in
appendix A, to have their fee rates increased to levels that allow
for the Real Living Wage to be passed onto their care staff, and
have their terms amended to stipulate that providers pay their care
staff at Real Living Wage for the remainder of the 2026/27
financial year.
 
This modification is justified as the
requirements of Public Contract Regulations 2015 Regulation
72(1)(e) are met as follows:
 
72. (1) Contracts and framework agreements may
be modified without a new procurement procedure in accordance with
this Part in any of the following cases:—
 
(e) where the
modifications, irrespective of their value, are not substantial
within the meaning of paragraph (8)
 
In this instance, the proposed modifications
do not
 
(a) 
render the contracts materially different in character
 
(b) 
introduce additional conditions that would have influenced the
conduct or outcomes of the original tender processes
 
(c) 
change the economic balance of the contracts in favour of the
contractors
 
(d) 
extend the scope of the contracts considerably
 
(e) 
involve new contractors replacing those originally awarded
contracts.
 

 
(i)            
That, in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015,
Regulation 72(1)(e), four Adult Social Care contracts as detailed
in appendix A, be modified by price to have their fees rates
increased to levels that allow for the Real Living Wage to be
passed onto their care staff, and have their terms amended to
stipulate that providers pay their care staff at Real Living Wage
with effect from the date of this decision for the remainder of the
2026/27 financial year;
 
(ii)           
That all fee rates payable by the Council are amended through
contract modifications, and that one-off payments be made to
providers of an amount equal to what they would have been due had
their respective contracts been modified with effect from 1 April
2026; and
 
(iii)          
That the Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant
contract modification documentation.
 


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected
because the Council wants to ensure that the Real Living Wage is
passed onto front line staff who are supporting the delivery of
care and support to some of the most vulnerable people in our
community.  Without the modifications to
the contracts, the Council cannot ensure full compliance with this
stipulation is fully complied with.
 

Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
Each of the contracts under this modification
have been tendered for as part of a fair and competitive
process.  As each contract expires, they
will be re-tendered as per the Council procurement rules at that
time.  This modification seeks to ensure
that all current contracts can ensure the providers are paid fee
rates that allow them to pay the Real Living Wage to their
staff.  All contracts are performing at
a satisfactory standard and there was deemed no need to complete a
competitive exercise for this reason at this time.
topline: The Executive Director Resources & Partnerships and Executive Director Health and Social Care have decided to modify Adult Social Care contracts to increase fee rates for the Real Living Wage.

respite opportunities for unpaid adult carers.   
 
This modification is justified as the
requirements of Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation
72(1)(e) are met in that the modification is not considered to be
substantial within the meaning of Regulation 72(8) as follows:
 


•

initially concluded;


•               
It does not introduce conditions which, had they been part of the
initial procurement procedure would have allowed for the admission
of other bidders, the acceptance of another tender other than the
one originally accepted or attracted additional participants in the
original procedure;


•               
It does not change the economic balance of the contract in favour
of the contractor; 


•               
It does not extend the scope of the contract considerably; and


•               
It does not involve a new contractor replace the original recipient
of the contract award.

The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015,
Regulation72(1)(e) to modify the contract with N-Compass for the
unpaid carer service to allow N-Compass to pilot unconventional
respite opportunities for unpaid adult carers.   
 
This modification is justified as the
requirements of Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation
72(1)(e) are met in that the modification is not considered to be
substantial within the meaning of Regulation 72(8) as follows:
 


•               
It does not render the contract materially different from the one
initially concluded;


•               
It does not introduce conditions which, had they been part of the
initial procurement procedure would have allowed for the admission
of other bidders, the acceptance of another tender other than the
one originally accepted or attracted additional participants in the
original procedure;


•               
It does not change the economic balance of the contract in favour
of the contractor; 


•               
It does not extend the scope of the contract considerably; and


•               
It does not involve a new contractor replace the original recipient
of the contract award.
 

(i)            
That, in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015,
Regulation 72(1)(e),
the contract with
N-Compass for the unpaid carer service be modified by amending the
pricing and scope from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 to allow
NCompass to pilot unconventional respite opportunities for unpaid
adult carers; and 
 
(ii)           
That the Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant
contract modification documentation.
 


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected due to
the high demand for respite services within the Borough and the
need to ensure all Accelerated Reform Funding was spent by the
Council before April 2026. 
 

Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): 
This option was considered and rejected due to
the current unpaid carer provider being in a good position to
facilitate the use of this funding and provide a multitude of
options for carers and the clause in the funding stating that funds
must committed and spent by the Council by 31 March 2026, but can
continue to be used by the provider until March 2027, it is not
possible to undertake a fully compliant tender exercise at this
time.
 

Deliver in house: 
This option was considered and rejected due to
the service needing expertise, skills and resources to deliver a
Care Quality Commission compliant service, which could not be
undertaken within Council’s existing resources.
topline: The Executive Directors have decided to approve the modification of the contract with N-Compass to pilot unconventional respite opportunities for unpaid adult carers.

To seek approval for the purchase of the

accommodation for homeless households owed a
statutory duty.
 

The Director (Corporate Support) hereby:
 
(i)            
Approves the purchase of a residential property listed in Appendix
A of the report on the main terms and conditions referred to in
this report.
 
(ii)           
Authorise the Head of Legal Service to prepare and complete the
necessary legal documentation.
 

Do not purchase the property – this was
rejected because it would mean having to rely
on leasing of dispersed accommodation to meet
temporary accommodation demand
which would reduce the number of affordable
rented properties that are available for
households who require them.

accommodation demand – this was
rejected. It is accepted that the Council will
continue to need to use hotel provision due to

considerable cost to the Council and therefore it is
necessary to reduce, as far as possible, the
level of reliance on this type of provision
because the cost of using it leads to
significant subsidy loss to the Council.

13.—(1) Subject to paragraph (3), a contract

Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023,
Regulation 13(1)(a).
 
13.—(1) Subject to paragraph (3), a contract
or framework agreement for relevant health care services may be

content:
The purpose of this report is
to seek permission, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule
9.2.2 (e)) for an exemption from Contract
Procedure Rule 6, to award a contract without competition* to
Learning Pool [for the procurement of content and licenses for
E-Learning Packages.
 
This exemption is justified as
the requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e) are met as
follows:
 
e.       Any
other exceptional circumstances.
 
The following circumstances are
considered exceptional justifying the awarding of a contract
without competition.  Whilst other
suppliers can provide similar products, Learning Pool is the only
provider who can provide the number of courses/catalogues, with the
variety of subject matters, the e-learning authoring tool and the
practicality of using our own LMS (Learning Management System)
compliant with the content i.e. SCORM 1.2/2004 files

By
Executive Director (Resources and Partnerships):
 

(i)       
That an exemption from Contract Procedure Rule 6be
granted, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2(e), to
permit the award of acontract without competition for the
procurement of content and licenses for e-learning
packages.
 
By
Head of Workforce:
 

(i)        
That a contract be awarded without competition* to
Learning Pool for the provision of content and licenses for
authoring tools for e-learning packages from 1 April 2026 to 31
March 2029 with the option to extend the contract for two further
12-month periods to 31st March 2031; and
 
(ii)     That the
Procurement Team be authorised to make the necessary arrangements
for the issue of the relevant contract documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was
considered and rejected This option was considered and rejected
because the Service would become out of contract with the current
supplier and would lose access to a tailored suite of packages that
have been built up over the previous 15 years. This option would
create significant legal risk, as many of the training courses
available via the system are legal requirements.
 
Deliver in house: This option
was considered and rejected due to the expense of procuring an
E-Learning Authoring tool and building all subsequent e-learning
packages in addition to the resource required to do
this.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation /
Tender): Initial benchmarking was completed but it was deemed this
option would not be considered as there are currently no other
suppliers that would be able to supply the current suite of
packages which Knowsley Council utilise as well as authoring tool
and the bespoke courses that have been built up over a number of
years to meet particular needs.  As we
currently use Oracle HCM as our Learning Management system, the
compatibility with current Oracle HCM (26A) is not compliant with
majority of the providers delivery methods i.e. SCORM connectors
and cannot be used within the system. 
The use of SCORM connectors also means additional costs for
authoring copyrighted e-learning modules provided by alternative
providers.  As part of the existing
contract with Learning Pool we are
allowed full access to all catalogues and able to include Knowsley
details, links etc, with no additional cost. Given the needs of the
organisation, the most suitable provider available at present is
Learning Pool. 
 
Award via a Framework -
Whilst there is a potential route to market via
agreement of a four-year maximum contract to Learning Pool
available via the Crown Commercial Services G-Cloud 14 Framework,
this option has been considered and rejected.  This is because Learning Pool have agreed to a
fixed price for the next three years (with a fixed price for two
further potential 12-month extensions). 
In addition, with the proposed agreement with Learning Pool to
cover a period up to a total of five years, this will continue to
grant Knowsley unlimited access to all e-learning packages at no
additional cost.
topline: The Executive Director Resources And Partnerships and the Head Of Workforce have decided to award a contract without competition to Learning Pool for E-Learning Packages procurement.

content:
To approve the acceptance and utilisation of a
£0.075m grant from Veolia Environmental Trust to deliver the
Knowsley Village Recreation Ground ‘
Play Area Improvement Project’ and include this
project within the Capital Programme for 2026/27 for the
Environmental Sustainability Service. 
To also approve the proposed consultation with the public and key
stakeholders on the Park Master Plan and Activity Plan for
infrastructure/landscaping and activity/service development at
Knowsley Village Recreation Ground.
 

That the Executive Director
(Resources and Partnerships) in consultation with the Cabinet
Member for Communities and Neighbourhoods agree
to: -
 
a)   
Note, in accordance with the Council’s
Financial Procedure Rules, the acceptance of £0.075m of
external grant funding from Veolia Environmental
Trust;
 
b)   
Approve the utilisation of £0.075m of grant
funding on the Knowsley Village Recreation Ground ‘Play Area
Improvement Project’;
 
c)   
Approve the agreement to secure the funding from
Veolia Environment Trust with a Contributing Third-Party Payment of
£0.008m, funded on a 50/50 basis between Knowsley Town
Council and the Environmental Sustainability
Service;
 
d)   
Approve the inclusion of the Knowsley Village
Recreation Ground ‘Play Area Improvement Project’ in
the Environmental Sustainability Service 2026/27 Capital Programme;
and
 
e)   
Proceed in consulting with the community and key stakeholders on a
wider Park Improvement Master Plan and Activity Plan for Knowsley
Village Recreation Ground.
 

Do Nothing: Knowsley Village Recreation
Ground currently is in a poor condition and not functioning
effectively as the primary parkland space for the Knowsley Village
Community.  Local
residents have already expressed concern about the site
through consultation work delivered independently by the Friends
Group for the site.  To do nothing would
result in the Council not meeting obligations to provide high
quality public open space for this community and also generate reputational damage given the
current public momentum around the site to see change happen.
 
Delivery of Play Area Improvements:
identified as a key priority for enhancement by the community, the
Council has successfully secured a grant offer of £0.075m
from Veolia Environmental Trust.  If
this offer is not accepted and play area improvements not
delivered, this will mean loss of this sum of money to the Borough,
as well as significant reputational damage to both Knowsley Council
and Knowsley Town Council, who are leaseholders of the site and
active partners.
 
Consultation Delivery: building on the
excellent work of the Friends Group in consulting the community
about the site, it is prudent for the Council to deliver a further
phase of consultation focusing specifically on proposals for
improvement to the site.  This exercise
would help to provide the evidence for future inward investment
through external grant finance and would also support the targets
of the adopted Green Space Action Plan for Knowsley, which
highlights this site as a priority for delivery of a Master Plan in
the actions for 2026/27.
topline: The Executive Director Resources & Partnerships has decided to approve a £0.075m grant from Veolia Environmental Trust for the Knowsley Village Recreation Ground 'Play Area Improvement Project'.

Do
Nothing: 
This option was considered and rejected
because the contract is strategically relevant to the Council as it
helps to meet demand for low level daily living aids and,
therefore, reduces demand for the Council’s occupational
therapy services. Without this service waiting lists for the
occupational therapy service are likely to increase, creating
longer delays to people receiving support that prevents the need
for more expensive long-term care.  
 
Seek Competition
(Tender): 
This option was considered and rejected as
there were concerns that a retender would not result in any better
value being offered. The proposed cost of the service has been
evaluated and confirmed as offering good value to the Council.
 
Deliver in
house: 
This option was considered and rejected
because although the Council has the relevant skills and knowledge
to do this; it does not have capacity to deliver this service.
Furthermore, there is added value to an external organisation, such
as a Registered Provider of Social Housing, providing this type of
service in the borough which the Council would struggle to achieve
on its own.
