decision_maker: Director of Family Help and Children Social Care (Joanne Parry)
purpose:
The purpose of this report is to inform the
Assistant Executive Director of Children Services regarding the
Step Up to Social Care Program cohort nine and the implications for
Knowsley MBC.
content:
The purpose of this report is to inform the
Assistant Executive Director of Children Services regarding the
Step Up to Social Care Program cohort nine and the implications for
Knowsley MBC.
 

To endorse the contract between Wirral Borough Council,
acting as Lead Authority and Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council
as partner within the Learn Together Partnership and subsequently
the Step Up to Social Work cohort nine program. Due to the
continued success of the Step Up to Social Work program we have
previously decided to increase the number of student placements
from two to four and have continued with 4 this year.
 

As part of the Children’s
Social Care Workforce Sufficiency Programme, it was agreed that
increasing the number of student placements and opportunities
within Knowsley would support the long?term recruitment of Social
Workers into the organisation. In January 2023, it was decided that
Knowsley would increase its student placement numbers from two to
four. This decision was informed by the strong track record of
retaining Step Up to Social Work students within the council. Two
alternative options were considered. The first was to continue
offering only two student placements; however, it was felt that an
increase could be supported across the service and would better
align with the ambitions of the Workforce Sufficiency Programme.
The second option was to withdraw from the programme entirely, but
this would have undermined the service’s ongoing recruitment
and retention initiatives.
 
Last year, Knowsley
successfully supported four student placements, demonstrating the
service’s capacity and commitment to developing future Social
Workers. The positive outcomes and feedback from this cohort
reinforced the value of expanding placement opportunities. As a
result, the council has continued with four placements again this
year, further strengthening the long?term workforce pipeline.

The running of the course at Edge Hill University has been widely
praised both from the DfE and Ofsted, calling it a
‘model’ for other Universities to replicate nationally.
We are fortunate this this standard of delivery exists within the
region. Given the decline of student placements from BA/MA routes,
withdrawing from the Step Up to Social Work programme was not a
viable option or needing consideration. This shortfall is being
mitigated through both increased Step-Up placements and the SW
Apprenticeship programme.

decision_maker: Executive Director Resources & Partnerships (Stephan Van Arendsen) & Director Development & Infrastructure (Tony Clark)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (7) to modify the
contract with NECO Mechanical and Electrical Consulting Engineers
for Huyton Multi Storey Car Park.
content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (7) to modify the
contract with NECO Mechanical and Electrical Consulting Engineers
for Huyton Multi Storey Car Park.
 


(i)     
That in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule
9.4.2.(7), the contract with NECO Mechanical and Electrical
Consulting Engineers for Mechanical and Electrical Advisory
Services for Huyton Multi Storey Car Park be modified by amending
the pricing and scope to include additional car parking decks,
envelope treatments and services; and

 (ii)  That the Procurement Team be authorised to issue
the relevant contract modification documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected as this will not assist the Council in delivering its
long-term vision for Huyton Village Centre, for which Huyton Multi
Storey Car Park is a key component. In a do-nothing scenario,
opportunity to improve infrastructure in line with accessibility
goals, would be limited and the current car park would continue to
negatively impact the visual amenity of the town centre.
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): Seeking
competition for a new tender process is not considered feasible as
the existing contract is performing effectively. Initiating a
separate procurement exercise would likely result in significant
delays and additional costs ultimately impacting project
delivery.
topline: The Executive Director Resources & Partnerships and Director Development & Infrastructure have decided to modify the contract with NECO Mechanical and Electrical Consulting Engineers for Huyton Multi Storey Car Park.

purpose:
The purpose of the report is,
in accordance with regulations 13(1)(a) of the Health Care Services
(Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 to:
 

(i)            
modify the
terms of the Specialist Stop Smoking
Service contract with City Health Care

B1by extending the term from 1 April 2026 to 31 March
2028;
 

(ii)           
seek
approval to issue an award notice.
 
The justification for this
decision, as required by relevant regulations, is that the Council is satisfied that:
 

·      
the modification is clearly and unambiguously
provided for in the contract

·      
the modification has been assessed under Regulation
13, which governs when healthcare contracts may be modified during
their term without triggering a new procurement process.

·      
the modification is necessary to ensure continuity
of a critical health service, avoiding disruption that would
negatively impact patient outcomes.
content:
The purpose of the report is,
in accordance with regulations 13(1)(a) of the Health Care Services
(Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 to:
 

(i)            
modify the
terms of the Specialist Stop Smoking
Service contract with City Health Care
Partnerships as provided for within the existing contract at clause
B1by extending the term from 1 April 2026 to 31 March
2028;
 

(ii)           
seek
approval to issue an award notice.
 
The justification for this
decision, as required by relevant regulations, is that the Council is satisfied that:
 

·      
the modification is clearly and unambiguously
provided for in the contract

·      
the modification has been assessed under Regulation
13, which governs when healthcare contracts may be modified during
their term without triggering a new procurement process.

·      
the modification is necessary to ensure continuity
of a critical health service, avoiding disruption that would
negatively impact patient outcomes.
 


(i)   
That, in accordance with regulation 13(1)(a) of the Health Care
Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations
2023,the contract with City Health
Care Partnerships (CHCP) for the Specialist Stop Smoking Service
contract be modified by extending the term as provided for within
the existing contract at clause B1from 1 April 2026 to 31 March
2028.
 

(ii)  
That, in
accordance with regulation 13(4) of the Health Care
Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, a
transparency notice, as set out in Appendix B to the
report, be issued for publication on the UK
e-notification service, indicating the modification of the
Specialist Stop Smoking Service Contract from 1 April 2026 to 31
March 2028; and 
 

(iii)  That the Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant
contract award documentation.
 

Do
Nothing:
This option was considered and
rejected because this would leave Knowsley without a
specialist Stop Smoking Service. The consequences of this would
include poorer health outcomes for residents and increase pressure
on primary, secondary, and acute care services. It also risks
continuity of the service supporting delivery of The All
Together Smokefree Knowsley Strategic Action Plan
2024-2027 and access to its associated supplementary
funding.
 

Deliver in house:
This option was rejected as the
service provider is performing well and there is provision within
the current budget to trigger the available
extension.
 

Award a New Contract:
This option has been rejected
as the extension of the existing provision, is justified and
ensures continuity of care and avoids the risk of disruption to
treatment pathways, quit attempts, and behavioural support. A new
contract award at this time would introduce mobilisation risks,
including potential gaps in service delivery, loss of experienced
specialist staff, and reduced engagement with service
users.
topline: The Assistant Chief Executive and Executive Director Health & Social Care have decided to extend the Specialist Stop Smoking Service contract with City Health Care Partnerships until 2028.

purpose:
The purpose of this report is to seek approval
to award an honorarium arrangement to reflect additional
responsibilities, to ensure the management of the Children Centres
and Family Hubs is effective and sustainable.  The additional responsibilities will focus on the
management of the operational Start for Life / Early Years team who
deliver the Start for Life and Beyond offer across the borough and
support the strategic development and implementation of the offer
to Knowsley families.  This will be
aligned to the requirements of the ‘Giving Every Child the
Best Start in Life’ strategy which was released by the

content:
The purpose of this report is to seek approval
to award an honorarium arrangement to reflect additional
responsibilities, to ensure the management of the Children Centres
and Family Hubs is effective and sustainable.  The additional responsibilities will focus on the
management of the operational Start for Life / Early Years team who
deliver the Start for Life and Beyond offer across the borough and
support the strategic development and implementation of the offer
to Knowsley families.  This will be
aligned to the requirements of the ‘Giving Every Child the
Best Start in Life’ strategy which was released by the
Department for Education earlier this year.
 

That the Executive Director (Children's) and
the Executive Director (Resources & Partnerships) are
recommended to;

agree a monthly honorarium payment
equivalent to 50% of the difference between the substantive grade
and the bottom SCP of PMG 2, until 31 March 2027, to support the
delivery of the Start for Life and Beyond Offer, and;
agree to the extension of the
existing honorarium arrangement that is in place for additional
responsibilities for Sector Support until 31 March 2027.

 

If these additional responsibilities were not
awarded and the capacity was not created, there would be a risk
that the Council would not be able to deliver the requirements
outlined in the government strategy and Knowsley families and young
children would be disadvantaged. The Start for Life and Beyond team
does not currently have sufficient senior management capacity to
effectively manage the operational and strategic responsibilities
needed to drive the transformation of the offer.
topline: The Executive Director Children & Young People and Executive Director Resources & Partnerships have decided to approve an honorarium arrangement to reflect additional responsibilities for the management of Children Centres and Family Hubs in Knowsley.

content:
The purpose of this report is
to seek permission, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule
9.2.2(e)for an exemption from Contract Procedure Rule 6to direct
award a contract without competition to John Moores University
Services for drug and alcohol monitoring systems.
 
This exemption is justified as
the requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2(e) are met as
follows:
 
e.        Any other
exceptional circumstances. The following circumstances are
considered exceptional justifying the awarding of a contract
without competition.
 
This exemption is
justified under CPR 9.2.2(e) due to exceptional circumstances. The
proposed drug and alcohol monitoring system is the only solution
that integrates directly with the existing JMUS case?management
infrastructure. Switching suppliers would require bespoke
interfaces, disrupt statutory safeguarding functions, and introduce
unacceptable risk to chain?of?custody evidence and active casework.
The service is time?critical, and any disruption would compromise
the Council’s statutory duties.
 

By Executive
Director (Resources and Partnerships):
 
(i)       That an exemption
from Contract Procedure Rule6 be granted, in accordance with
Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e), to permit the direct award of a
contract without competition for provision of Drug and Alcohol
monitoring systems.
 
By Executive
Director (Health and Social Care):
 
(ii)       That a contract be
direct awarded without competition to John Moores University
Services for the provision of drug and alcohol monitoring systems
from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2029; and
 
(iii)      That the Procurement Team
be authorised to make the necessary arrangements for the issue of
the relevant contract documentation.
 

This option was considered and rejected due to
the importance of having relevant data provision required to
support a reduction in drug and alcohol harms. This would also
impact on the flow of intelligence between local authorities with
regards to drug and alcohol treatment. The system enables
collaboration and sharing of information between providers, support
services, and those responsible for commissioning services. Not
commissioning these key monitoring systems risks increasing the
numbers of drug and alcohol related deaths in Knowsley.
 

Deliver in house:

 
This option was considered and rejected as the
local authority does not have access to the required integrated
monitoring and criminal justice systems or specialist knowledge of
these data functions to provide inhouse.
 

Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):

 
This option was considered and rejected on the
grounds that this would likely result in an award to JMUS as they
are the unique provider. If another provider came forward with an
offer of delivery, it would not meet MAT (Most Advantageous Tender)
requirements and would require significant investment in time and
resource to achieve the same position currently offered by this
provider, which would, in the meantime, put provision (intelligence
flows, collaboration and sharing of best practice) and local people
at risk (decrease in positive treatment outcomes, disproportionate
increase in number of drug related deaths).
topline: The Executive Directors have decided to grant an exemption to direct award a contract without competition to John Moores University Services for drug and alcohol monitoring systems.

content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation72(1)(e) to modify the pricing with Merseyside Youth
Association for Short Breaks; Activities for disabled children from
1 April 2026 to 31 October 2026.
 
The modification is justified as the
following requirements of Public Contract Regulations 2015 72(1)(e)
are met in that the modification is not considered to be
substantial within the meaning of Regulation 72(8) as follows:
 
·      
It does not render the contract materially different from the one
initially concluded;
·      
It does not introduce conditions which, had they been part of the
initial procurement procedure would have allowed for the admission
of other bidders, the acceptance of another tender other than the
one originally accepted or attracted additional participants in the
original procedure;
·      
It does not change the economic balance of the contract in favour
of the contractor;
·      
It does not extend the scope of the contract considerably; and
It does not involve a new contractor replace
the original recipient of the contract award.

 
(i)       That, in accordance
with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation 72(1)(e), the
contract with Merseyside Youth Association for Short Breaks:
Activities for disabled children to be modified by increasing the
pricing by 4.5% from the original contract value (£0.041m);
and
 
          and
provided for within the existing contract at clause H1, which
allows for modification without a new procurement procedure being
required.
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and rejected due to the
statutory duty under the Children Act 1989 for the Local Authority
to provide (as part of a range of services for families) breaks
from caring for carers of disabled children; and to support them to
continue to care for their children at home and to allow them to do
so more effectively.  
It would also have negative impact on the children/young
people and families accessing the service should this cease or be
disrupted. Additionally, there would potentially be a financial and
reputational risk. 
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
A competitive exercise
at this stage would not be beneficial as the provider is delivering
the service satisfactorily. An additional seven-month extension has
been approved as of 16 February 2026 to extend the service until 31
October 2026 and therefore does not allow sufficient time to
complete a thorough competitive
tender process. In this time, the changes would need to support the
transition between providers for approximately 70 vulnerable
children and young people. Consequently, this interchangeability
between services would be time limited and the process would need
to be repeated again for the further procurement, potentially
creating confusion among families and a reputational risk to the
Council. 
 
In house provision – As there is no current
capacity within the Council to provide this service, this option
was not considered. Whilst the Council does have its own internal
respite offer, this would not provide adequate interchangeability
with the current commissioned short break service that offers term
time weekend and school holiday activity groups.

(2)      Contract Procedure Rule

Direct Payment Support  Service by
modifying the pricing from £0.120m to £0.125m to account for increases to
employers’ National Insurance contributions.
 
The modification to the term of the contract
is justified as the following requirements of Contract Procedure
Rule 9.4.2 are met as follows:
 
(1): The modification is provided for within
the existing contract at clause B1.2 in precise and clear detail
with regards to scope, nature and conditions under which the
modification may be used.
 
The modification to the pricing of the
contract is justified as the following requirements of Contract
Procedure Rule 9.4.2 are met as follows:
 
(7) Non-substantial modification – a
modification is non-substantial if all of the following criteria
are met:
 
(i) the modification does not increase the
term of the contract by more than 10% of the maximum term provided
for on award
 
(ii) the modification does not materially
change the scope of the contract
 
(iii) the modification does not materially
change the economic balance of the contract in favour of the
supplier.
 
The changes are not considered substantial for
the following reasons:
 
·      
The modification does not increase the term of the contract beyond
that allowed for in the original contract at clause B1.2
 
·      
The scope of the contract is not proposed to change in any way and
will continue to be delivered as per the original
specification.
 
·      
While the proposed modification increases the contract value, it
does not materially shift the economic balance in the
supplier’s favour. The adjustment simply prevents the
supplier from being financially disadvantaged by recent, changes to

i)        That, in

with statutory requirements, whilst protecting highway safety and
movement.

purpose:

in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation72(1)(a), to modify the call off contract with Aimes
Management Services Limited (trading as ARO) for provision of a
virtual firewall and internet breakout as provided for within the
existing call off contract at part B: clause 1.3  from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. A security
virtual firewall and secure internet breakout are important because

content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation72(1)(a), to modify the call off contract with Aimes
Management Services Limited (trading as ARO) for provision of a
virtual firewall and internet breakout as provided for within the
existing call off contract at part B: clause 1.3  from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. A security
virtual firewall and secure internet breakout are important because
together they protect cloud and network traffic, reduce latency and
cost, and enable a modern zero trust security model without relying
on a central data?centre bottleneck.
 

(i)       That, in accordance
with Public Contract Regulations 2015 Regulation 72(1)(a), the call
off contract with Aimes Management Services Limited (trading as
ARO) for the provision of provision of a virtual firewall and
internet breakout be modified by extending the contract term from
01 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, as provided within the existing
Call-Off Contract entered into under the Crown Commercial Service
G-Cloud 13 framework, as set out in the Call-Off Form under the
“Extension period” provisions and Part B Clause
1.3.
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected because the existing contract for virtual firewall and
internet breakout is due to expire on 31st March 2026. If the
contract is not extended this would result in the loss of
immediately cloud access, external communications with Microsoft
and other partners, security protections, and remote services,
effectively crippling normal business operations. This would
present a significant risk of service disruption and impact on
Council services used by users, residents and partners.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): This
option was considered and rejected on this occasion because the
existing contract includes a clear and explicit option to extend
for a further period of up to 12 months. The incumbent supplier is
performing satisfactorily with services operating as intended. The
pricing for the extension period was agreed as part of the original
procurement therefore undertaking a new competitive procurement at
this point would be disproportionate and introduce unnecessary risk
to service continuity. This could also not be completed within the
timescales required to ensure uninterrupted provision of
services.
 
There were no other viable options identified
as delivering the services in-house was considered but discounted
as the services rely on externally hosted private cloud
infrastructure and accredited data centre facilities. The current
call off contract provides the provided services and includes
contractual mechanism to extend the term.
topline: The Head of Information Technology has decided to extend the contract with Aimes Management Services Limited for provision of a virtual firewall and internet breakout.

in accordance with The Health Care Services (Provider Selection
Regime) Regulations 2023 – 13(1)(d), to modify the contract
with Diverse Active CIC for Mum’s Social Walk Service
contract by modifying the scope and terms of the contract from 1
April 2026 to 31 May 2026.
 
The modification is justified as the following
requirements of The Health Care Services (Provider Selection
Regime) Regulations 2023 – 13(1)(d) are met as follows:
 
The justification for the decision is that the
modification does not render the contract materially different in
character, and the cumulative change in the lifetime value of the

than £0.5m.

The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with The Health Care Services (Provider Selection
Regime) Regulations 2023 – 13(1)(d), to modify the contract
with Diverse Active CIC for Mum’s Social Walk Service
contract by modifying the scope and terms of the contract from 1
April 2026 to 31 May 2026.
 
The modification is justified as the following
requirements of The Health Care Services (Provider Selection
Regime) Regulations 2023 – 13(1)(d) are met as follows:
 
The justification for the decision is that the
modification does not render the contract materially different in
character, and the cumulative change in the lifetime value of the
contract or framework agreement since it was entered into is less
than £0.5m.
 
The decision is needed to enable the continued
delivery of service in line with the current contract. The provider
was recently successful as a subcontractor for the new Healthy
Knowsley Service. Significant procurement delays were experienced
during the retender process of the Healthy Knowsley Service during
2025/26 and a short extension is required to align these
contracts.
 

(i)            
That in accordance with The Health Care Services (Provider
Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 – 13 (1)(d), the contract
with Diverse Active CIC for delivery of the Mum’s Social Walk
Service be modified by extending the
term for two months from 1 April 2026 to the 31
May 2026; and 
 
(ii)           
That the Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant
contract modification documentation.
 


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected as it
would have left a gap in local provision if the service was not
extended to cover the period before the new Healthy Knowsley
Service contract to deliver the service is in force (which will
involve the incumbent provider continuing to provide the service as
a sub-contractor under that main contract). The service was
previously funded through Public Health reserves and although due
to expire on the 31 March 2026 was performing well; therefore, the
option to do nothing was rejected as it would have led to a lack of
available provision for mother’s and families in Knowsley for
an interim period. The service aims to increase physical activity
levels and contribute to improved health and wellbeing outcomes of
pregnant women, new parents and their families through a free
“Mum’s Social” programme.  
 

Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
A
tender exercise for the Healthy Knowsley has already taken place
and once that contract commences, the
Mum’s Social Walk Service will be delivered as part of
this new contract (to be effective from 1 June
2026).
topline: The Executive Director Resources & Partnerships and Executive Director Health and Social Care have decided to extend the contract with Diverse Active CIC for the Mum's Social Walk Service by two months.

decision_maker: Head of Highways and Capital Delivery (Jon Robinson)
purpose:
To seek authorisation to introduce a Temporary
Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation Notice relating to
sections of the M62 Junction 5 Eastbound Entry Slip, Roby Ward, to
facilitate essential carriageway maintenance works on behalf of
Tarmac, in accordance with statutory requirements, whilst
protecting highway safety and movement.
content:
To seek authorisation to introduce a Temporary
Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation Notice relating to
sections of the M62 Junction 5 Eastbound Entry Slip, Roby Ward, to
facilitate essential carriageway maintenance works on behalf of
Tarmac, in accordance with statutory requirements, whilst
protecting highway safety and movement.

The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery
authorises the necessary legal and administrative procedures
required to:-
 
(a) 
process a Temporary Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation
Notice, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act
1984. The sections of road identified below and shown in the
drawing numbered PT/TM/8641 shall be closed to all vehicular
traffic (except emergency services), including pedal cycles, on
29th March 2026 between the hours of 06:00 and 12:00, to such an
extent as may from time to time be indicated by the appropriate
traffic signs.
 
(i)   
M62 Junction 5 Eastbound Entry Slip, Roby Ward – In an
eastbound direction to its interface with the M62.
 
(b) 
provide exemptions in
the Notice described in the decision item (a) above to permit
reasonable access to plant or premises, so far as it is practical
without interference with the execution of the said work and for
works vehicles or any vehicles being used in connection with the
police, fire or ambulance purposes and anything done with the
permission or at the direction of a police constable in
uniform.
 

Alternative traffic management techniques were
considered however given the statutory requirements of Chapter 8 of
the Traffic Sign Manual 2009 (for traffic safety measures at road
works and other temporary situations) and in the interest of
highway and public safety, it will be necessary to conduct the
works under temporary road closure conditions.
topline: The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery has decided to introduce a Temporary Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation Notice for essential carriageway maintenance works on the M62 Junction 5 Eastbound Entry Slip.

decision_maker: Executive Director Resources & Partnerships (Stephan Van Arendsen)
purpose:
Whilst the Council actively seeks to recover
any Housing Benefit overpayments made, it is not considered good
practice to continue pursuance of debts that are deemed
irrecoverable or uneconomical to collect.
 
An ongoing review of aged Housing Benefit
overpayment debt has identified £0.168m of debt which is
deemed irrecoverable as there is no legal recourse to pursue the
debt.
 
This report seeks approval to write off this
irrecoverable debt to the Council’s bad debt provision.
content:
Whilst the Council actively seeks to recover
any Housing Benefit overpayments made, it is not considered good
practice to continue pursuance of debts that are deemed
irrecoverable or uneconomical to collect.
 
An ongoing review of aged Housing Benefit
overpayment debt has identified £0.168m of debt which is
deemed irrecoverable as there is no legal recourse to pursue the
debt.
 
This report seeks approval to write off this
irrecoverable debt to the Council’s bad debt provision.
 

The Executive Director (Resources and
Partnerships) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Resources
hereby:
 
i)              
Approves the write off of irrecoverable Housing Benefit
overpayments totalling £0.168m which cannot be recovered as
there is no legal recourse to pursue the debt.
 

Continuing to pursue irrecoverable debt was
rejected as this would divert resources away from pursuing debt
that can be recovered.
topline: The Executive Director Resources & Partnerships has decided to write off irrecoverable Housing Benefit overpayments totalling £0.168m.

decision_maker: Executive Director Place (Dale Milburn)
purpose:
To obtain delegated authority to make a Public
Path Diversion Order under Section 257 of the Town and Country
Planning Act 1990 in respect of Public Footpath KN/11/1. The
diversion is necessary to enable the implementation of planning
permission 22/00348/FUL, as the approved development footprint
directly conflicts with the existing footpath alignment. The
decision is required to ensure the development can proceed lawfully
while maintaining a safe and accessible public right of way.
Approval will allow officers to carry out the statutory procedures
and secure an indemnity agreement to recover all associated
costs.
content:
To obtain delegated authority to make a Public
Path Diversion Order under Section 257 of the Town and Country
Planning Act 1990 in respect of Public Footpath KN/11/1. The
diversion is necessary to enable the implementation of planning
permission 22/00348/FUL, as the approved development footprint
directly conflicts with the existing footpath alignment. The
decision is required to ensure the development can proceed lawfully
while maintaining a safe and accessible public right of way.
Approval will allow officers to carry out the statutory procedures
and secure an indemnity agreement to recover all associated
costs.

That the Executive Director (PLACE) in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Regeneration &
Economic Development approves:
(a)      The making of a Public
Path Diversion Order under Section 257 of the Town and Country
Planning Act 1990 to divert Public Footpath KN/11/1 as shown on the
draft Order map (Appendix A).
(b)      Authorisation for officers
to undertake all statutory procedures associated with the making,
publication, and (if unopposed) confirmation of the Order.
(c)      Authorisation for officers
to submit the Order to the Secretary of State for determination if
objections are received and not withdrawn.

Do nothing – Rejected. Without a
Section 257 Diversion Order, the approved development cannot be
constructed without unlawfully obstructing the existing footpath.
This would prevent the development from proceeding or expose the
Council and developer to legal challenge.
Process the diversion through a Definitive
Map Modification Order (Wildlife & Countryside Act 1981)
– Rejected. A DMMO cannot be used to divert a path to enable
development and would not address the obstruction created by the
approved layout. It is significantly slower, more
resource-intensive, and legally inappropriate where Section 257
TCPA applies.
Alter the approved development to retain
the existing footpath alignment – Rejected. Retaining the
current route would require substantial redesign of the scheme and
is not feasible within the approved layout. The path passes
directly through the building footprint, service yards, and access
roads.
topline: The Executive Director Place has decided to approve a Public Path Diversion Order to enable a development project, potentially sparking controversy among local stakeholders.

decision_maker: Executive Director Place (Dale Milburn)
purpose:
The purpose of this report is to seek approval
for the addition of Extra Care Allocations to the Nominations
Agreement previously approved in June 2025 (decision K1767). By
doing so, this will formalise existing procedures and informal
agreements that are already in place. It will also allow the
Council to enforce terms of the Nomination Agreement to ensure
compliance and ensure that properties are allocated to households
in greatest need and have fair access to housing.
content:
The purpose of this report is to seek approval
for the addition of Extra Care Allocations to the Nominations
Agreement previously approved in June 2025 (decision K1767). By
doing so, this will formalise existing procedures and informal
agreements that are already in place. It will also allow the
Council to enforce terms of the Nomination Agreement to ensure
compliance and ensure that properties are allocated to households
in greatest need and have fair access to housing.
 

The Executive Director
(PLACE) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Regeneration
and Economic Development is recommended to:
 
a)   
approve the addition of Extra Care Allocations to
the Nominations Agreement previously approved June 2025 (decision
K1767)
b)   
authorise the Head of Housing and Property and the
Group Manager of Housing to be the Council’s designated lead
officers for matters relating to nominations rights for their
general needs social housing and Extra Care housing and between the
Council and Registered Providers.
c)   
authorise Head of Legal Services to complete
nominations agreements between Knowsley Council and the individual
Registered Providers.
 

This option was considered and rejected
because without the inclusion of Extra Care allocations within the
Nominations Agreement, this risks the Council being unable to
enforce its right to 100% nominations for allocations to Extra Care
within the borough. This would leave the Council unaware of whether
properties are being allocated to households that are eligible for
Extra Care Housing and in greatest need.
topline: The Executive Director Place has decided to approve the addition of Extra Care Allocations to the Nominations Agreement to ensure fair access to housing for households in greatest need.

Approve the refurbishment and remodelling of 52
Derby Road Huyton in advance of it becoming the Council’s new
Workforce Development Hub;

 
2.   
Approve the allocation of £0.220m
from:

a.   
Major Development Team Capacity Funding Allocation -
£0.050m

b.   
Workforce Remodelling Reserve - £0.170m;
and

Approve the inclusion of £0.220m for the
Refurbishment and Remodelling of 52 Derby Road in the Major

Council’s Headquarters and preference for it to have a high
street location.

decision_maker: Executive Director Resources & Partnerships (Stephan Van Arendsen) & Executive Director Health and Social Care (Jenny Rollinson)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is to
seek approval in accordance with The Health Care Services (Provider
Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, Regulation 13(1)(d) to modify
the contract with
Wirral Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust for the
Knowsley Healthy Child Programme contract (Lot 1: 0-25 Public
Health Service in Knowsley) by modifying the pricing from 1
April 2026 to 31 January 2027 by £277,699.
 
This modification is justified
as the requirements of The Health Care Services (Provider Selection
Regime) Regulations 2023, Regulation 13(1)(d) are met as
follows:
 
(d)      the modification is
attributable to a decision of the relevant authority and
both of the criteria in paragraph (2)
are met.
 
The criteria in Regulation
13(2) are met as follows:
 
(a)      the modification does not
render the contract or framework agreement materially different in
character, and
(b)(ii)  the cumulative change in the lifetime value of the
contract or framework agreement since it was entered into or
concluded is less than 25% of the lifetime value of the original
contract agreement when it was entered into or
concluded.
 
The report also seeks approval of a separate one-off
payment of £333,238 to cover the provider’s additional
costs in the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
content:
The purpose of the report is to
seek approval in accordance with The Health Care Services (Provider
Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, Regulation 13(1)(d) to modify
the contract with
Wirral Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust for the
Knowsley Healthy Child Programme contract (Lot 1: 0-25 Public
Health Service in Knowsley) by modifying the pricing from 1
April 2026 to 31 January 2027 by £277,699.
 
This modification is justified
as the requirements of The Health Care Services (Provider Selection
Regime) Regulations 2023, Regulation 13(1)(d) are met as
follows:
 
(d)      the modification is
attributable to a decision of the relevant authority and
both of the criteria in paragraph (2)
are met.
 
The criteria in Regulation
13(2) are met as follows:
 
(a)      the modification does not
render the contract or framework agreement materially different in
character, and
(b)(ii)  the cumulative change in the lifetime value of the
contract or framework agreement since it was entered into or
concluded is less than 25% of the lifetime value of the original
contract agreement when it was entered into or
concluded.
 
The report also seeks approval of a separate one-off
payment of £333,238 to cover the provider’s additional
costs in the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
 

By Executive Director (Resources and
Partnerships) and Executive Director (Health and Social
Care)
 
(i)            
That, in accordance with The Health Care Services (Provider
Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, Regulation 13(1)(d), the
contract with Wirral Community Health and Care NHS Foundation
Trustfor the Knowsley Healthy Child Programme contract (Lot 1: 0-25
Public Health Service in Knowsley) be modified by amending the
pricing from 1 April 2026 to 31 January 2027 by £277,699;
 
(ii)           
That the Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant
contract modification documentation; and
 
By Executive
Director (Health and Social Care)
 
(iii)          
That a one-off payment of £333,238 be made to Wirral
Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust to reflect what they
would have been due, had their contract price been modified with
effect from 1 April 2025.
 

This option was considered and rejected
because the Knowsley Healthy Child Programme (Lot 1: 0-25 Public
Health Service in Knowsley) is a statutory service that provides a
universal offer for all children in Knowsley.  The uplift to the contract is being sought so that
the existing provider can continue to deliver the outcomes detailed
in the specification whilst upholding the NHS pay agreement terms
for staff and managing the increased costs associated with this
contract.
 

Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
This option was considered and rejected
because Wirral Community Heath and Care NHS Foundation Trust are in
the final year of the contract following the implementation of a
two-year provided-for extension from 1 February 2025 to 31 January
2027 (Key Decision K1692). The service is performing well and it would not be appropriate to tender and
award a new contract at this time.
topline: The Executive Directors have decided to modify the contract with Wirral Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust for the Knowsley Healthy Child Programme, increasing pricing and making a one-off payment to cover additional costs.

decision_maker: Head of Information Technology (John Fairclough)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015 Regulation
72(1)(a), to modify the Call off Contract with Aimes Management
Services Limited for the provision of IT compute, storage and
periphery infrastructure as provided for within the existing
call-off contract entered into under the Crown Commercial Service
G-Cloud 13 Framework agreement, as set out in the call-off order
form under the “Extension period” provisions and clause
1.3 by extending the contract term from 01 April 2026 to 31 March
2027.
content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015 Regulation
72(1)(a), to modify the Call off Contract with Aimes Management
Services Limited for the provision of IT compute, storage and
periphery infrastructure as provided for within the existing
call-off contract entered into under the Crown Commercial Service
G-Cloud 13 Framework agreement, as set out in the call-off order
form under the “Extension period” provisions and clause
1.3 by extending the contract term from 01 April 2026 to 31 March
2027.
 

 
(i)   
That, in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation 72(1)(a), the Call off Contract with Aimes Management
Services Limited (trading as ARO) for the provision of IT compute,
storage and periphery infrastructure be modified by extending the
contract term as provided for  within
the existing Call-Off Contract entered into under the Crown
Commercial Service G-Cloud 13 framework as set out in the call-off
order form under the “Extension period” provisions and
clause 1.3 from 01 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.
 

(ii)  
That the Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant
contract modification documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected because the existing contract for IT compute, storage and
periphery infrastructure is due to expire on 31st March
2026. If the contract is not extended this would result in the loss
of core infrastructure services that underpin critical council
systems including line of business applications, data storage,
backup and disaster recovery. This would present a significant risk
of service disruption and impact on Council services used by users,
residents and partners.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): This
option was considered and rejected on this occasion because the
existing contract includes a clear and explicit option to extend
for a further period of up to 12 months. The incumbent supplier is
performing satisfactorily with services operating as intended. The
pricing for the extension period was agreed as part of the original
procurement therefore undertaking a new competitive procurement at
this point would be disproportionate and introduce unnecessary risk
to service continuity. This could also not be completed within the
timescales required to ensure uninterrupted provision of
services.
 
There were no other viable options identified
as delivering the services in-house was considered but discounted
as the services rely on externally hosted private cloud
infrastructure and accredited data centre facilities. The current
call off contract provides the provided services and includes
contractual mechanism to extend the term.
topline: The Head of Information Technology has decided to extend the contract with Aimes Management Services Limited for IT infrastructure services.

purpose:
This report sets out how
Knowsley Council proposes to use its three?year Homelessness, Rough
Sleeping and Domestic Abuse grant allocation to strengthen its
homelessness prevention and accommodation services. It explains the
funding available, outlines rising service demands, and recommends
creating and securing key staffing roles to ensure the Council can
deliver effective, sustainable and high?quality support for

content:
This report sets out how
Knowsley Council proposes to use its three?year Homelessness, Rough
Sleeping and Domestic Abuse grant allocation to strengthen its
homelessness prevention and accommodation services. It explains the
funding available, outlines rising service demands, and recommends
creating and securing key staffing roles to ensure the Council can
deliver effective, sustainable and high?quality support for
residents facing housing crisis.
 

The Executive
Director (PLACE) in consultation with the Executive Director
(Resources and Partnership) is hereby approves:
 
(i) Establishment of:
 

·      
2 x FTE
permanent Temporary Accommodation Housing Officer (Grade G)
posts,

·      
1 x FTE
permanent Housing Solutions Support Officer (Grade F)
post,

·      
2 x FTE
permanent Principal Housing Delivery Officer (Grade L)
posts.

 
(ii) Conversion of:
 

·      
2 x FTE
temporary Housing Solutions Officer (Grade H) posts to permanent
posts,

·      
2 x FTE
temporary Intensive Support Worker (Grade F) posts to permanent
posts,

·      
2 x FTE
temporary Housing Solutions Support Officer (Grade F) posts to
permanent posts, and;

·      
1 x FTE
temporary Empty Homes Officer (Grade J) post to
permanent.

 

Do nothing: this was rejected because:
 

·      
the
temporary accommodation service is an essential function enabling
the council to meet its statutory homeless function. The number of
properties managed by the temporary accommodation service totals
112. It would not be feasible to effectively manage these
properties for an extended period within the existing staffing
resource.  Past
experience has demonstrated that intensive management is required
for this type of provision to adequately support occupants and to
ensure that properties are well looked after and to maintain
community cohesion.

·      
the National
Homelessness plan and the Council’s Homelessness and Rough
Sleeping strategy sets out the ambition to support and prevent
homelessness. Increasing resources in the Housing Solutions service
and Strategic Housing service is necessary to adequately respond to
service demands.

·      
Extending
fixed-term roles over a long period is not a viable option and does
not provide staff employment stability.
topline: The Executive Director (Dale Milburn) has decided to approve recommendations for strengthening homelessness prevention and accommodation services in Knowsley Council.

decision_maker: Executive Director Resources & Partnerships (Stephan Van Arendsen) and Director Corporate Support (Justin Thompson)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (3), to modify the contract with
Marshall Property Construction Limited for the refurbishment of a
vacant area of the school to create soft play area, sensory room,
children’s toilets and accessible WC at Knowsley Central
Primary School, Huyton byincreasing roof heights and replacing the
defective roof decks and external wall.
 
The modification is justified as the following requirements
of Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (3) are met as follows:
 

(3)
Unforeseeable circumstances - the circumstances giving rise
to the modification

(i)       could not reasonably
have been foreseen by the contracting authority before the award of
the contract and

(ii)       does not change the
overall nature of the contract.

 
Following strip-out and demolition, previously concealed
defects were identified in both the timber and concrete roof decks,
as well as an external timber wall with inadequate structural
integrity, none of which could be fully assessed prior to
demolition. When combined with very limited existing ceiling
heights and the spatial requirements for M&E services and soft
play equipment, the original approach of repairing and
strengthening the existing structure is no longer viable.
Increasing roof heights and replacing the defective roof decks and
external wall provides a compliant, safer, and more practical
solution, delivering minimum internal ceiling heights of 2.4m,
simplifying the structural design by removing the need for
substantial steel beams and columns, and reducing long-term
risk.
content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (3), to modify the contract with
Marshall Property Construction Limited for the refurbishment of a
vacant area of the school to create soft play area, sensory room,
children’s toilets and accessible WC at Knowsley Central
Primary School, Huyton byincreasing roof heights and replacing the
defective roof decks and external wall.
 
The modification is justified as the following requirements
of Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (3) are met as follows:
 

(3)
Unforeseeable circumstances - the circumstances giving rise
to the modification

(i)       could not reasonably
have been foreseen by the contracting authority before the award of
the contract and

(ii)       does not change the
overall nature of the contract.

 
Following strip-out and demolition, previously concealed
defects were identified in both the timber and concrete roof decks,
as well as an external timber wall with inadequate structural
integrity, none of which could be fully assessed prior to
demolition. When combined with very limited existing ceiling
heights and the spatial requirements for M&E services and soft
play equipment, the original approach of repairing and
strengthening the existing structure is no longer viable.
Increasing roof heights and replacing the defective roof decks and
external wall provides a compliant, safer, and more practical
solution, delivering minimum internal ceiling heights of 2.4m,
simplifying the structural design by removing the need for
substantial steel beams and columns, and reducing long-term
risk.
 

(i)       That, in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(3), the contract with Marshall
Property Construction Limitedfor the refurbishment of a vacant area
of the school to create soft play area, sensory room,
children’s toilets and accessible WC at Knowsley Central
Primary School, Huyton be modified by increasing the pricing by
£0.156m; and
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected because it would result in the project being unable to
progress or be completed in its intended form. The newly identified
structural defects and low ceiling heights mean the existing
structure cannot safely or compliantly accommodate the proposed
soft play area, sensory room and associated facilities. Not
modifying the contract would leave the area vacant and unusable,
deny pupils access to much-needed specialist provision, and
undermine the educational and inclusion objectives of the scheme,
while also risking ongoing health and safety and maintenance issues
for the school.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): This
option was considered and rejected as undertaking a new competitive
exercise is not appropriate at this stage of the project. Marshall
Property Construction Limited is the incumbent contractor, is
performing satisfactorily, and is already fully mobilised on site
with detailed knowledge of the building, design development, and
the unforeseen structural issues identified following strip-out.
Re-tendering would result in significant delays, additional costs
associated with remobilisation and re-survey, and potential
abortive works, adversely impacting the programme and the delivery
of essential facilities for pupils. Modifying the existing contract
therefore represents the most efficient and proportionate
approach.
 
Other options: Other options were considered
but rejected. Delivering the works in-house was not feasible due to
the specialist construction requirements, structural remediation,
and the need for coordination with M&E services and soft play
equipment installation, which exceed internal capacity and
expertise. Modifying the existing contract with a different
supplier was also not practical, as no other contractor is
currently mobilised on site or familiar with the project, meaning
this would cause delays, increased costs, and potential quality and
safety risks. Therefore, proceeding with the existing contract with
the incumbent contractor remains the most efficient and effective
option.
topline: The Executive Director Resources & Partnerships has decided to approve the modification of a contract with Marshall Property Construction Limited for the refurbishment of a school to create a soft play area, sensory room, children's toilets, and accessible WC.

& Fracture Prevention Service contract as provided for within

(i)            
That, in accordance with regulation 13(1)(a) of the Health Care
Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, the contract
with Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust for the Falls and Fracture
Prevention Service be modified by extending the term as provided
for within the existing contract at clause C1 from 1 April 2026 to
31 March 2028; and
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation including the publication, in accordance with
regulation 13(4), of the transparency notice at Appendix 1 to the
report.

Do Nothing: 
This option was considered and rejected as
this would have a negative impact on existing and future service
users. The service reduces the likelihood of falls within the local
population. Falls can have serious consequences, particularly for
frail and elderly people who may suffer from reduced mobility and
independence, as well as incurring serious injuries arising from a
fall. In addition to the costs to the individual, falls have a
significant financial cost to both NHS and social care
services.
 

Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
This option was considered and rejected as
there is provision within the existing contract to extend for 24
months from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2028. The current provision of
the Falls and Fracture Prevention Service delivered by Mersey Care
NHS Foundation Trust is good. The provider is performing well, and
this is a valued service in the borough.
 

Deliver in house:
This option was considered and rejected due to
the service needing clinical expertise, skills and resources to
deliver a Falls and Fracture Prevention service, which could not be
undertaken within Council’s existing resources.
topline: The Executive Director Resources and Partnerships has decided to extend the contract with Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust for the Falls & Fracture Prevention Service.

disabled resident would potentially result in the requirement to
provide additional care packages which would incur additional costs
to Adult Social Care. The provision of these works is likely to
reduce the need for formal paid care.  
 
Deliver in

This option was considered and rejected due to
the fact that the Local Authority do not have any direct in - house
building teams who could carry out the adaptation works
required.   
  
Retender:  
The Council could retender the works but there
is a risk that the works would cost more due to the rising costs of
goods in the construction sector.

ensuring the Council’s partners (i.e. academies) continue to
have access to appropriate support in this respect given the
limited alternate provision available in the area.

decision_maker: Director Corporate Support (Justin Thompson)
purpose:
The purpose of this report is to propose the
establishment of a PVI Workforce Development Officer role to ensure
that Private, Voluntary and Independent (PVI) sector organisations
maintain access to e-learning via the HCM system. The establishment
of this role will ensure these duties are funded as currently they
are an unfunded pressure and PVI organisations will be able to
continue to access learning via HCM as part of their contractual
arrangements through the Council.
content:
The purpose of this report is to propose the
establishment of a PVI Workforce Development Officer role to ensure
that Private, Voluntary and Independent (PVI) sector organisations
maintain access to e-learning via the HCM system. The establishment
of this role will ensure these duties are funded as currently they
are an unfunded pressure and PVI organisations will be able to
continue to access learning via HCM as part of their contractual
arrangements through the Council.
 

That the Director of Corporate Support in
consultation with the Executive Director (Health and Social Care)
and the Executive Director (Resources and Partnerships) agree to
the establishment of 1 FTE PVI Workforce Development Officer
– (Grade F) post as part of the Human Resources staffing
structure. Initially this will be established on an initial
12-month fixed term basis and then reviewed at 9 months with
potential extension following evaluation of the impact of post and
model of training delivery to PVIs.
 

The alternative option of not introducing this
role presents a risk that PVI organisations will not be able to
access learning for people within their organisations and risk us
not fulfilling our duties outlined in contracts with PVI
organisations. It could also lead to PVIs sourcing their own
learning, potentially impacting quality of learning as well as
potential increased costs of contracts as PVIs add the cost of
sourcing this learning to their contracted prices.  The approach of introducing this role for 12
months will enable us to review this role and approach to learning
across PVIs and decide between Adult Social Care and HR longer term
plans.
 

Provide within Service
Considerations have also been sought whereby
to place the role in Adult Social Care, however, due to the HCM
system set up arrangements, it’s felt best this role sits
within HR.
 

Transfer Responsibility to PVIs
This option was considered and rejected as
there would be a cost to PVI providers and that there would be an
expectation for the Council to fund these costs via Adult Socia
Care Fee Rates.  The payment by the
hour/bed rate within Adult Social Care is not considered an
efficient way to fund providers to access statutory eLearning
training in relation to safeguarding.
topline: The Director of Corporate Support has decided to establish a PVI Workforce Development Officer role to ensure access to e-learning for PVI sector organizations.

documentation.
 

Do Nothing: Regarding the extension of the
contract by 12 months; this option was considered and rejected due
to the essential software services provided to areas of the Council
via the contract; to allow it to lapse without invoking an
extension would be detrimental to council employees, residents and
businesses that rely on these services.

rejected due to some of the purchased infrastructure nearing
capacity and needing extra compute and storage to function at

extend the contract any further beyond the 12 months sought by this
report, and so a competitive exercise will be mandatory in the

rejected because the supplier fully owns the “software as a

decision_maker: Director Public Health (Sarah McNulty)
purpose:
To approve funding of £0.0475m to cover
the cost of the delivery of a targeted family benefit and income
maximisation programme to contribute to addressing child and family
poverty in the borough. The funding is to cover additional capacity
in Citizens Advice Knowsley to deliver the programme which includes
outreach activity, awareness sessions, establishment of referral
pathways and one to one support for families with children through
child and family settings.
content:
To approve funding of £0.0475m to cover
the cost of the delivery of a targeted family benefit and income
maximisation programme to contribute to addressing child and family
poverty in the borough. The funding is to cover additional capacity
in Citizens Advice Knowsley to deliver the programme which includes
outreach activity, awareness sessions, establishment of referral
pathways and one to one support for families with children through
child and family settings.

That the Director of Public Health in
consultation with the Health Cabinet Member are recommended to
agree to allocate £0.0475m to fund Citizens Advice Knowsley
for the delivery of a family benefit and income maximisation
programme.

Citizens Advice Knowsley is a specialist
provider of impartial support and advice in the community. The
programme was initially funded by the Cheshire and Merseyside
Integrated Commissioning Board as part of its commitment in local
areas to tackle health inequalities. However, funding ended
prematurely and given the positive action undertaken and links made
the decision to end the programme at such an early stage was
rejected.  Child and Family poverty is a
significant challenge in borough with evidence demonstrating that
maximisation of benefits and income is an effective approach to
mitigate impacts of poverty, so continuation of programme deemed
important to embed and enable approach to be incorporated into
practice.
topline: The Director of Public Health has decided to approve funding for a targeted family benefit and income maximisation programme to address child and family poverty in the borough.

decision_maker: Executive Director Resources & Partnerships (Stephan Van Arendsen) & Executive Director Childrens (Mark Mirfin)
purpose:
Given the end of the Household
Support Fund, the Council had planned to end the provision of
supermarket vouchers to the families of free school meals children
after the Easter Break. The vouchers have always been funded by
Household Support Fund which officially end on 31/3/26.
 
Throughout the lifetime of the
scheme, Knowsley has largely mirrored the offer in Liverpool and
Sefton due to the number of children who attend cross border
schools. This has proven an effective way to providing fair support
to our families whilst avoiding complaints from residents who would
otherwise be disadvantaged.
 
Due to a softening in recent
Government guidance, the Council now understands that both
Liverpool and Sefton will continue with the provision of vouchers
beyond Easter into the May 2026 half-term. To ensure our offer is
commensurate with our neighbours, it is therefore proposed to
extend our provision for the additional half term.
 
Knowsley has approximately
9,000 children who are eligible for free school meals and the
Council intends to continue its current offer of £15 per week
per child.
 
The Council notes that some
schools offer a two week May half-term break. Where this is the
case, families will receive two weeks’ worth of vouchers as
they will have gained the week from elsewhere in the school
calendar.
 
At this stage the May half-term
will be the final time the Council will allocate vouchers given the
end of the Household Support Fund and the Council’s ability
to fund an investment of this scale.
 
The May half-term vouchers are
funded from funding set aside for hardship support. At this point
it is estimated that they will cost the Council
£0.185m.

purpose:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval,
in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(1), to extend the
contract with Health Diagnostics Ltdfor the quality assurance of
the mandated NHS Health Checks Programme as provided for within the
existing contract particulars and clause C1.1 from the 1 April 2026
to 31 March 2028.
 
The reasons for the decision are, as required
by Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2. (1): The extension is provided
for within the existing contract particulars and clause C1.1 in
precise and clear detail with regards to scope, nature and
conditions under which the modification may be used.
 
The purpose of this report is also to seek
approval in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(7) to
modify the contract to include an increase in the
original tendered rates for the proposed extension
period.
 
The modification request to uplift the
contract is supported by the following provision
within Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (7): Non-substantial
modification – a modification is non-substantial if
all of the following criteria are
met
(i)            
the modification does not increase the term of the contract by more
than 10% of the maximum term provided for on award;
 
(ii)           
the modification does not materially change the scope of the
contract; and
 
(iii)         
the modification does not materially change the economic balance of
the contract in favour of the supplier.
 
The changes are not considered substantial as
they do not materially change the scope of the contract and it does
not materially change the economic balance of the contract in
favour of the supplier. The uplift being proposed is relatively
small (10.3%) against a low value contract.
 
The justification is that the provider has
delivered the service under the same pricing for the duration of
the current (as well as the previous contract period), with no
increases to their funding, while continuing to provide
comprehensive support and absorbing rising operational and
third?party costs during this time. Further cost increases are
projected for the service from April 2026, as such they are
requesting a contract modification to uplift the tendered rates to
account for these costs.

purpose:
The value of the contract is above The purpose of this report is to seek permission, in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e)for an exemption from
Contract Procedure Rule 7 to award a contract without competition
to SHAP Ltd for the provision of supported accommodation for young
people.
The proposed contract will
enable continuity of service provision for vulnerable young people
whilst the Council implements its plans to develop the scope and
model for young persons supported accommodation scheme based on the
foyer model, as described in the Homelessness and Rough Sleeping
Strategy 2025 – 2030.
 
This exemption is justified, as
the requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e) in relation
to exceptional circumstances are met, as follows:
 

It is the
Council’s commissioning intentions, as set out in the
Council’s Knowsley Homeless and Rough Sleeping Strategy
2025-2030, for the development of a foyer scheme in Knowsley for
young people at risk of homelessness The foyer model will create
wrap-around support for young people, including care experienced
persons.  It is important to ensure
continuity of care until the new scheme is built so that young
people at risk of homelessness can be successfully supported to
maintain their tenancies. Tendering the current service is not
considered to be beneficial at this time due to the significant
redesign in the way the service will be delivered that is required
to fit the new service model.

 

There is not yet a
commencement date for the foyer model project. However, it is
estimated to take between two to three years, which overlaps with
the proposed contract period. The duration of the proposed contract
is aligned to the service redesign work and is also expected to
give sufficient time to tender for the new service model when the
new building is built. Options to extend the proposed contract for
up to 24 months has been included to mitigate against any risk of
delays in the new build project.

 
The Council has a statutory
duty to consider the needs of young people including young people
with care experience, when planning homelessness services
(Homelessness Act 2002) and to prevent and relieve homelessness in
all cases (Housing Act 1996 (part 7). 
One way in which the Council meets this duty is to commission
supported accommodation for young people aged 16 to 24 years old at
risk of homelessness. The service provides intensive and focused
housing related support to 40 units of accommodation across three
sites in Knowsley. Approximately 10% of people accessing this
service are care experienced. 
Therefore, the Council has a corporate responsibility to these
young people. Without the continuation of such a service the
Council is unlikely to be able to fulfil its statutory duties to
prioritise addressing youth homelessness and relieving homelessness
for young people. Furthermore, the current service is delivered in
a building which is owned by the incumbent provider, SHAP Ltd,
making any new contract located in this building unattractive to
prospective bidders.

This option was considered and rejected

decision_maker: Executive Director Health and Social Care (Jenny Rollinson)
purpose:
The charging policy is reviewed every 12
months or more frequently if required.
 
On 23 March 2025, Cabinet Member with
Portfolio for Adult Social Care and the Executive Director (Health
and Social Care) approved the Adult Social Care Charging
Policy.
 
Since the approval of this policy in March
2025 there have been developments that have prompted a further
review of the current Charging Policy in Knowsley.
 
The Department of Health and Social Care
publish a local authority circular for each financial year setting
the capital limits, personal expenses allowance (PEA), minimum
income guarantee (MIG) and savings credit disregard. They have made
changes to the minimum income guarantee (MIG) rates for people
below Pension Credit age. The difference this year reflects the
policy decision to apply the higher uplift specifically to the core
working age MIG rates, with other Social Care Allowances, increased
by Consumer Price Inflation (CPI).
 
The revised Adult Social Care Charging Policy
included at Appendix A, has been updated to reflect an update to
the value of the allowances for Disability Related Expenses (DRE)
that can be considered in a financial assessment. Refreshed
guidance is produced annually by the National Association of
Financial Assessment Officers (NAFAO)
and the Adult Social Care Charging Policy has been updated to
reflect this.
 
There have been improvements made to the
Information, advice and guidance on Adult Social Care Charging that
have been implemented.
 
There will also be a change in practice to
reinstate charges for internal respite services provided by
Together We Care.

decision_maker: Head of Highways and Capital Delivery (Jon Robinson)
purpose:

maintenance works on behalf of Tarmac, in accordance with statutory
requirements, whilst protecting highway safety and movement.
content:
To seek authorisation to introduce a Temporary
One Way Traffic Regulation Notice relating to sections of Liverpool
Road, Prescot North Ward, to facilitate essential carriageway
maintenance works on behalf of Tarmac, in accordance with statutory
requirements, whilst protecting highway safety and movement.

The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery
authorises the necessary legal and administrative procedures
required to:-
 
(a) 
process a Temporary One Way Traffic
Regulation Notice, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic
Regulation Act 1984. The sections of road identified below and
shown in the drawing numbered PT/TM/8615 shall be closed to all
vehicular traffic (except emergency services), including pedal
cycles, on 15th March 2026 between the hours of 08:00 -12:30, to
such an extent as may from time to time be indicated by the
appropriate traffic signs.
 
(i)   
Liverpool Road – In a westerly direction from its junction
with Manchester Road to its interface with M57 junction 2
roundabout restricting the direction of
travel to east bound only.
 
(b) 
provide exemptions in
the Notice described in the decision item (a) above to permit
reasonable access to plant or premises, so far as it is practical
without interference with the execution of the said work and for
works vehicles or any vehicles being used in connection with the
police, fire or ambulance purposes and anything done with the
permission or at the direction of a police constable in
uniform.
 

Alternative traffic management techniques were
considered however given the statutory requirements of Chapter 8 of
the Traffic Sign Manual 2009 (for traffic safety measures at road
works and other temporary situations) and in the interest of
highway and public safety, it will be necessary to conduct the
works under temporary road closure conditions.
topline: The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery has decided to introduce a Temporary One Way Traffic Regulation Notice on sections of Liverpool Road for essential maintenance works.

up to up to £0.110m for
provision and installation of a Point of Use Hot Water System and
related carbon reduction infrastructure at Park Brow Primary
School, with no match funding requirement.  Also, to enter into a JCT contract with DfE

appointed Contractor, Dodd Group Midlands Ltd.

DECISION:  

i)            
Note the acceptance of grant funding up to the
value of up to £0.110m from
the Department for Education’s Net Zero Accelerator Programme
at Appendix B.

ii)           
That, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule
Schedule 1, 5.3.2, a contract be awarded to Dodd Group Midlands Ltd
following a compliant procurement process undertaken by Department
for Education’s (LocatED) using
the Crown Commercial Services Framework RM6313 to provide and
install a Point of Use Hot Water System by 31 March
2026.

iii)          
That the Head of Environmental Sustainability and
Communities approves the contractual (JCT) agreement between the
Department of Education’s (LocateEd’s) appointed Contractor, Dodd Group
Midlands Ltd, and the Council to install a Point of Use Hot Water
System to Park Brow Primary School, which requires both a signatory
and a witness signatory for the Council.

iv)          
That the Head of Environmental Sustainability and
Communities approves the inclusion of up
to £0.110m, on a Point of Use Hot Water System and
related infrastructure to Park Brow Primary School, to the
Environmental Sustainability Services 2025/26 Capital
Programme.
v)           
That the Head of Legal Services, in consultation
with Star Procurement, enacts the contract between the Council and
the Department for Education’s (LocatED) appointed Contractor, Dodd Group Midlands
Ltd, with the Department for Education’s (LocatED) being responsible for the entire
procurement process using Crown Commercial Services Framework
RM6313.

To not accept the funding
opportunity would go against the Council’s climate emergency
agenda, Net Zero 2040 target and clean air strategy. Park Brow
Primary School is within the Council’s most deprived ward,
Northwood, where health inequalities are at their
highest.

decision_maker: Director Corporate Support (Justin Thompson)
purpose:
PURPOSE OF THE REPORT/REASONS FOR DECISION:
 
This report proposes amending
the existing Occupational Health Assistant role to a broader HR
Assistant (Generalist) position. The post will remain at the same
grade and cost. This amendment will create a more flexible and
deployable resource that can support the operational HR function
where pressures and priorities are highest.
 
The Occupational Health
Assistant post became vacant following a member of staff leaving
the Council’s employment. Before recruiting, the HR
Operations team began a review to determine where the role was most
needed across the service, recognising evolving operational
requirements and increasing demand in generalist HR
areas.
 
Finance have
confirmed that the vacancy remains fully funded and unallocated,
providing an opportunity to reshape the role to better align with
service needs and create capacity where HR activity is
growing.
 
There is no longer the same
level of operational requirement for a dedicated Occupational
Health Assistant position. In contrast, generalist HR support needs
have significantly increased. Amending the role to a generalist HR
Assistant will:


Provide a deployable resource that can flex across HR
Operations to meet peaks and troughs in activity.
