PURPOSE OF THE REPORT/REASONS FOR DECISION:
 
This report proposes amending
the existing Occupational Health Assistant role to a broader HR
Assistant (Generalist) position. The post will remain at the same
grade and cost. This amendment will create a more flexible and
deployable resource that can support the operational HR function
where pressures and priorities are highest.
 
The Occupational Health
Assistant post became vacant following a member of staff leaving
the Council’s employment. Before recruiting, the HR
Operations team began a review to determine where the role was most
needed across the service, recognising evolving operational
requirements and increasing demand in generalist HR
areas.
 
Finance have
confirmed that the vacancy remains fully funded and unallocated,
providing an opportunity to reshape the role to better align with
service needs and create capacity where HR activity is
growing.
 
There is no longer the same
level of operational requirement for a dedicated Occupational
Health Assistant position. In contrast, generalist HR support needs
have significantly increased. Amending the role to a generalist HR
Assistant will:


Provide a deployable resource that can flex across HR
Operations to meet peaks and troughs in activity.
Strengthen support for core HR processes including employee
relations, recruitment, policy implementation and project
activity.
Enhance the team’s ability to carry out KPI
monitoring, data quality checks and performance
reporting.
Build a strong development pathway for individuals
entering HR, creating a valuable succession planning
pipeline across the service.
Improve service resilience by ensuring workload can be
redistributed effectively during high?pressure periods or temporary
staffing gaps.

The
benefits of this approach are:

Greater operational flexibility: The
postholder can be deployed wherever demand is highest, improving
responsiveness and service continuity.
Support for succession planning: A
broad generalist role creates a foundational development
opportunity, helping grow future HR Advisors and supporting
internal career progression.
Increased capacity: Provides essential
day?to?day support for HR activity, freeing specialist HR staff to
focus on higher?level casework and projects.
Enhanced data and KPI capability: More
consistent monitoring and improved data accuracy strengthen overall
service performance.
Cost-neutral approach: Uses the fully
funded vacancy with no change to grade or budget.
Better role alignment: Matches the
post to current organisational needs and supports delivery of HR
priorities.

The
new role of HR Assistant (Generalist) therefore needs to be
created. The Job Description and Person Specification, which has
been evaluated in line with the Council’s policy, is attached
at Appendix A for consideration.
There is no additional
financial impact. The change utilises an existing funded vacancy at
the same grade and cost.

The AED Corporate Support
agrees that a current funded Grade E, full time Occupational
Health Assistant Role is to be amended to a new role of HR
Assistant (Generalist), remaining within the same grade and in the
same cost centre.

Do nothing was considered,
however the demand for our services is only increasing which is
creating delayed response times to our customers.
 
Reducing the grade was
considered however reviewing the activity required, and in line
with our current structure, Grade E is the most appropriate to
remain consistent across the HR Operations function.
topline: The Director Corporate Support has decided to amend the Occupational Health Assistant role to a broader HR Assistant (Generalist) position to meet increasing demand for generalist HR support.

(ii)       the aggregate value

9.4.2.
 
The changes are not considered substantial for
the following reasons: the services provided under the extension
remain identical in nature to those delivered under the original
agreement; the extension falls within the permitted thresholds; the
extension does not introduce any economic advantage to the
supplier; the modification would not have attracted different
bidders.  In this context, the
continuity of the service is considered sufficiently important for
vulnerable children with disabilities and their families to justify
an extension for this period of
time.

2026.
 
The modification is justified as the following
requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(8) to designate it as
a below threshold modification as all of
the following criteria are met:
 
(i)       the modification
does not itself increase or decrease the estimated value of the
contract by more than 10%
 
(ii)       the aggregate value
of below threshold modifications related to this contract does not

(iii       it does not
materially change the scope of the Contract and

non-substantial modification or covered elsewhere in this rule

The changes are not considered substantial for
the following reasons: the services provided under the extension
remain identical in nature to those delivered under the original
agreement; the extension falls within the permitted thresholds; the

supplier; the modification would not have attracted different
bidders.  In this context, the
continuity of the service is considered sufficiently important for
vulnerable children with disabilities and their families to justify
an extension for this period of
time.
 

(i)       That, in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (8), the contract with Volair
Limited for Short Breaks: Swimming for disabled childrenbe modified by
extending its term for four months from 1 April 2026 to 31 July
2026; and
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and rejected due to the
statutory duty under the Children Act 1989 for the Local Authority
to provide (as part of a range of services for families) breaks
from caring for carers of disabled children; and to support them to
continue to care for their children at home and to allow them to do
so more effectively.  
It would also have negative impact on the children/young
people and families accessing the service should this cease or be
disrupted. Additionally, there would potentially be a financial and
reputational risk. 
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
A competitive exercise
at this stage would not be beneficial as due to the lack of
engagement with service users and parent carers, it has not been
possible to co-produce a service model that can adequately meet
their needs. Providers are delivering the service satisfactorily.
An additional four-month extension will allow for further
consultation with children/young people and families and
procurement process to begin.
 
In house provision – The Council would
not have the resources, skills or capacity to provide the service,
given the service requires specific swimming requirements of the
service, therefore this option was not considered. Additionally,
whilst the Council does have alternative short break arrangements,
neither offer an adequate interchangeability with the current
commissioned disabled swimming service.
 
No other options have been considered.
topline: The Interim Executive Director Childrens and Executive Director Resources have decided to extend the contract with Volair Limited for Short Breaks: Swimming for disabled children by four months.

decision_maker: Assistant Executive Director Public Health (Sarah McNulty)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is, in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule, 7.7.2 (ii)
(Schedule 1) to seek permission to award a contract to the lot 1
successful bidder where the tender proposed for approval exceeds
the agreed budget by more than £50,000
(£156,000).
 
The purpose of the report is
therefore also, in accordance with regulations 6(7) and 11 of the
Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023
to award contracts for the delivery of Knowsley’s sexual
health service to the two successful bidders for lot 1 and lot 2
respectively from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, with the option to
extend the contracts up to a maximum of three 12 month periods
(until 31 March 2034).  The report seeks
approval to issue the intent to award notice to the
winning bidders for lot 1 and lot 2.
 
The justification for this
decision, as required by relevant regulations, is that the Council is satisfied that:
 
·      
Direct award processes A or B cannot be
applied to this service.


Direct award process C or the most suitable provider
process would also not be appropriate for this service, in the
circumstances.


 
A compliant competitive process has therefore been
conducted in accordance with the relevant regulations and approval
of its outcome is now being sought.
content:
The purpose of the report is, in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule, 7.7.2 (ii)
(Schedule 1) to seek permission to award a contract to the lot 1
successful bidder where the tender proposed for approval exceeds
the agreed budget by more than £50,000
(£156,000).
 
The purpose of the report is
therefore also, in accordance with regulations 6(7) and 11 of the
Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023
to award contracts for the delivery of Knowsley’s sexual
health service to the two successful bidders for lot 1 and lot 2
respectively from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, with the option to
extend the contracts up to a maximum of three 12 month periods
(until 31 March 2034).  The report seeks
approval to issue the intent to award notice to the
winning bidders for lot 1 and lot 2.
 
The justification for this
decision, as required by relevant regulations, is that the Council is satisfied that:
 
·      
Direct award processes A or B cannot be
applied to this service.


Direct award process C or the most suitable provider
process would also not be appropriate for this service, in the
circumstances.


 
A compliant competitive process has therefore been
conducted in accordance with the relevant regulations and approval
of its outcome is now being sought.
 

By
Executive Director (Resources):
 

(i)          
That, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule,
7.7.2 (ii) (Schedule 1) permission be granted to award a contract
to the successful bidder for lot 1, where the tender proposed for
approval exceeds the agreed budget by more than £50,000
(£156,000 in this instance).
 

By Executive Director (Resources) and the Executive
Director (Health and Social Care):
 

(ii)        
That, in accordance with regulations 6(7) and 11 of the Health Care
Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023, two
separate contracts be awarded to the successful bidders for lot 1
and lot 2 respectively of Knowsley’s Sexual Health Service
(under the Competitive Process), as identified in Appendix A to the
report;
 

(iii)       
That, in accordance with regulation 6(7) and 11 of the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations
2023, and subject to this decision not being called-in
within three working days of being published, an Intent to Award
Notice , as set out in Appendix A to the report, be issued for
publication on the UK e-notification service, indicating the
Council’s proposed award of the contracts to the two
successful bidders for lot 1 and lot 2 respectively, for the period
1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 with the option to extend the
contracts up to a maximum of three 12 month periods (until 31 March
2034); and
 
 
 

(iv)       
That, subject to the subsequent standstill period
concluding without an unresolved challenge, the contracts be
awarded, and the Procurement Team authorised to issue the relevant
contract award documentation, including publishing a contract award
notice, based on the information already set out in the draft
intent to award notice (Appendix A)  on
the UK e-notification service. 
 


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and
rejected because the current contracts for both the Integrated
Sexual Health Service and the HIV Advice and Support Service are
due to expire and therefore doing nothing would lead to a gap in
sexual health support and services. The Integrated Sexual Health
Service is a mandatory Public Health service, and therefore
provision must be made available to residents to support their
sexual health and wellbeing needs. The HIV Advice and Support
Service, whilst not a mandatory Public Health Service, provides
valuable non-clinical based support to residents living with or
affected by HIV. It is therefore essential that there is no gap in
provision to ensure that the health and wellbeing needs of
residents living with or affected by HIV in Knowsley are
supported.
  

Deliver in house:
This option was rejected as
sexual health services are specialist services, providing clinical
and non-clinical support to residents, therefore it would not be
possible to deliver in-house. 
    
Alternative Provider Selection Regime Processes:
Direct Award Process
A – This was
rejected as the existing providers are not the only providers that
can deliver the services.
 
Direct Award
Process B – This was rejected as patients are not offered a choice of
provider and team when accessing these services within the borough,
and the number of providers is restricted by the
Council.
 
Direct Award
Process C - This was
rejected as there have been considerable changes to the
specification / contracting arrangements and the lifetime value of
the proposed new contract is more than 25% / £0.5m higher
than the value of the current contract when originally
awarded.
 
Most Suitable
Provider Process -This was rejected as the Council did not have sufficient
information about likely providers to determine which would be the
most suitable. The market for sexual health services is varied, and
a competitive tender had not been carried out for several years, so
there was little knowledge on potential providers.
topline: The Assistant Executive Director Public Health has decided to award contracts for Knowsley's sexual health service to successful bidders, potentially impacting residents' access to essential support.

purpose:

72(1)(b) to modify the contract with Beebot AI for Family Hub Programme -

Interoperability and technical continuity. Introducing a different

dismantling or reconfiguring substantial technical components,
risking system instability and performance degradation.
Additionally, any re-procurement would require the Council to
invest substantial additional funds.

the overall nature of the contract and is proportionate to the
functional and technical requirements now identified and the
modification’s value is less than 50% of the original

content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation
72(1)(b) to modify the contract with Beebot AI for Family Hub Programme -
Digital Family Hub toinclude the ongoing maintenance and
licensing costs of the digital youth hub for the remaining contract
period, including the optional extension period.
 
This additional provision, which was not
included in the original procurement has become necessary to
provide a comparative experience for young people resident in
Knowsley that mirrors and integrates with the digital family hub;
ensuring the Local Youth Offer is visible and
accessible.  It is also considered that
a change of contractor cannot be made because of the need for
Interoperability and technical continuity. Introducing a different
contractor to provide the additional services would require
dismantling or reconfiguring substantial technical components,
risking system instability and performance degradation.
Additionally, any re-procurement would require the Council to
invest substantial additional funds.
 
The scope of the modification does not alter
the overall nature of the contract and is proportionate to the
functional and technical requirements now identified and the
modification’s value is less than 50% of the original
contract value.
 

(i)       That, in accordance
with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation 72(1)(b), the
contract with Beebot AI for
Family Hub Programme - Digital Family Hub be
modified by amending the pricing and scope to include the ongoing
maintenance and licensing costs of the digital youth hub for the
remaining contract period, including the optional extension period;
and
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected because this would leave the digital youth hub service
currently provided through a contract awarded from 15 December
2025 to 31 March 2026, without the appropriate ongoing
maintenance and licensing support to sustain the service beyond its
contract expiry, with no further options to extend.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): A
competitive exercise is not desirable on this occasion, due to the
need for interoperability and technical continuity. Introducing a
different contractor to provide the additional services would
require dismantling or reconfiguring substantial technical
components, risking system instability and performance degradation.
Additionally, any re-procurement would require the Council to
invest substantial additional funds.
 
Modify the existing digital youth hub
contract: The digital youth hub contract was awarded from 15
December 2025 to 31 March 2026, to progress the development of the
digital youth hub and in line with the Department of Cultural,
Media and Sport (DCMS) grant conditions. As this was a finite
budget, a single contract was awarded to ensure the development and
build of the service. The contract had no provided-for option to
extend and given that the value of a non-provided for modification
would have exceeded 50% of the original contract value, this option
was rejected as non-compliant with Contract Procedure Rule
9.4.2.
 
No other options were considered.
topline: The Interim Executive Director Childrens and Executive Director Resources have decided to approve modifications to the contract with Beebot AI for ongoing maintenance and licensing costs of the digital youth hub in Knowsley.

Engagement Facilitation and Support Service contract with Knowsley Healthwatch
CIC:

modifying the terms of the contract originally
agreed (where such a modification was not provided for in the
contract) having not sought prior approval in accordance with
contract procedure rules in operation at that time (2024/2025
municipal year), which, in this instance, was Contract Procedure
Rule 9.3.1(b).
 
The Healthwatch
Knowsley, Knowsley Older People’s Involvement Programme and
Partnership Public Engagement Facilitation and Support
Service contract was modified in
May 2023 to enable the delivery of a
population health programme in Northwood (Kirkby) between 17 May
2023 to 9 August 2024. Although the Council explored options at the
time to modify the contract to extend the delivery of the programme
for the period 10 August 2024 to 4 August 2025 it was not completed
before the agreed period the programme ended due to uncertainty on
the continuation of funding until close to the original
modification period ending. There was also uncertainty on the most
appropriate option to continue to purchase the service which led to
further delays. During the period 10 August 2024 to 4 August 2025
the monthly payments continued to be made to the provider to enable
continuity of service to ensure outcomes of the population health
programme achieved for the community were maintained.  This represented a de facto continuation of the
previous modification.

Knowsley Healthwatch CICfor Healthwatch Knowsley, Knowsley Older
People’s Involvement Programme and Partnership Public
Engagement Facilitation and Support Service to continue to lead the
population health programme in Northwood (Kirkby) on behalf of NHS
Cheshire and Merseyside, ensuring that the contract terms between
the Council and Knowsley Healthwatch CIC for the relevant period
have been clarified.

purpose:

in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation72(1)(b) to modify the contracts with Merseyside Youth
Association and Endorphins Group for Short Breaks; Activities for
disabled children by seven months from 1 April 2026 to 31 October

The modification is justified as the following

(b) for additional works, services or supplies

cannot be made for economic or
technical reasons such as requirements of interchangeability or

content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation72(1)(b) to modify the contracts with Merseyside Youth
Association and Endorphins Group for Short Breaks; Activities for
disabled children by seven months from 1 April 2026 to 31 October
2026.
 
The modification is justified as the following
requirements of Public Contract Regulations 2015 72(1)(b) are
met:
 
(b) for additional works, services or supplies
by the original contractor that have become necessary and were not
included in the initial procurement, where a change of
contractor—
 

cannot be made for economic or
technical reasons such as requirements of interchangeability or
interoperability with existing equipment, services or installations
procured under the initial procurement, and
would cause significant
inconvenience or substantial duplication of costs for the
contracting authority,

 
provided that any increase in price does not
exceed 50% of the value of the original contract.
 

(i)       That, in accordance
with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation 72(1)(b), the
contracts with Merseyside Youth Association and Endorphins Group
for Short Breaks: Activities for disabled children be modified by
extending their respective terms by seven months from 1 April 2026
to 31 October 2026 and
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and rejected due to the
statutory duty under the Children Act 1989 for the Local Authority
to provide (as part of a range of services for families) breaks
from caring for carers of disabled children; and to support them to
continue to care for their children at home and to allow them to do
so more effectively.  
It would also have negative impact on the children/young
people and families accessing the service should this cease or be
disrupted. Additionally, there would potentially be a financial and
reputational risk. 
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
A competitive exercise
at this stage would not be beneficial as due to the lack of
engagement with service users and parent carers, it has not been
possible to co-produce a service model that can adequately meet
their needs. Providers are delivering the service satisfactorily.
An additional seven-month extension will allow for further
consultation with children/young people and families. Additionally,
a competitive tender process would have needed to commence,
mobilise and begin delivery to cover the 7 month period. In this
time, the changes would need to support the transition between
providers for approximately 130 vulnerable children and young
people; and communicated out to those waiting to access the
service. Consequently, this interchangeability between services
would be time limited and the process would need to be repeated
again for the further procurement, potentially creating confusion
among families and a reputational risk to the Council.
 
In house provision – As there is no
current capacity within the Council to provide this service, this
option was not considered. Whilst the Council does have its own
internal respite offer, this would not provide adequate
interchangeability with the current commissioned short break
service that offers term time weekend and school holiday activity
groups.
topline: The Interim Executive Director Childrens and Executive Director Resources have decided to extend contracts with Merseyside Youth Association and Endorphins Group for Short Breaks: Activities for disabled children by seven months.

local young people.
 
Deliver in house: This option was considered
and rejected due to insufficient internal capacity and resources.
This approach would require the recruitment of additional staff
making it unlikely that the required outcomes could be achieved
within the necessary timescales.
topline: The Interim Executive Director Children's Services has decided to award a contract to Viper Productions for a film and digital media programme showcasing young people and youth settings across the borough.

Notice, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act
1984. The sections of road identified below and shown in the
drawing numbered PT/TM/8584 shall be closed to all vehicular

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To approve the Council’s Asset Management Strategy
2025/2030.
content:
To approve the Council’s Asset Management Strategy
2025/2030.
 

           
The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive Director
(Resources), which presented the Asset
Management Strategy 2026–2031 for Cabinet consideration and
approval.

 

Councillor Mrs J Lonergan, Cabinet Member for
Resources, reported that the Strategy set out how the Council would manage one
of their most important resources of land and buildings. In this
respect, those assets shaped the experience of everyone who lived,
worked, and invested in Knowsley, and this strategy ensured they
continued to do so in a sustainable, efficient and future
focused way. 
Council Lonergan highlighted that
the Strategy had been timely, particularly as the Council faced
rising energy costs, increased pressure to reduce carbon emissions,
and changing expectations about how services should be delivered.
Councillor Lonergan indicated that the Strategy provided a clear
plan for ensuring that Council buildings had been fit for
purpose, financially sustainable, and able to support delivery
of the Council Plan and the Knowsley 2030
Strategy. 
Councillor Lonergan reported that
the Council’s asset base had been significant as the Council
owned over 800 assets, with a combined book value of
around £280 million and these ranged from schools and
libraries to parks, operational depots, community facilities,
housing units and town centre premises. In this respect,
the Strategy emphasised the importance of regularly reviewing
this portfolio to ensure the Council only retained those
assets that supported the Council’s strategic priorities and
dispose of those assets that were no longer
required. 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted that
at the heart of this Strategy, there had been a clear vision to
manage the Council’s assets efficiently and cost
effectively to promote carbon reduction, economic vibrancy,
sustainable services, and community
wellbeing. In this respect,
Councillor Lonergan reported that in order to achieve this, the
Strategy set out four aims of managing assets
corporately, ensuring assets are fit for purpose, delivering value
for money, and supporting economic growth. Councillor Lonergan
reported that the Strategy had been supported by an Action
Plan for 2026/27, which included practical steps such as
centralising statutory and reactive maintenance, improving data
systems, reviewing our office accommodation, updating our disposals
and acquisitions policy, and strengthening our community asset
transfer approach. 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted that
the Action Plan also reinforced the Council’s commitment
to decarbonisation, including delivering the Net Zero Delivery
Plan, improving energy efficiency across the estate, and working
closely with partners such as the Mersey Forest to enhance
biodiversity and tree coverage. 
In conclusion, Councillor Lonergan
reported that the Strategy strengthened governance arrangements,
establishing a Corporate Land and Buildings Working Group,
improving data through a single corporate property register, and
ensuring that decisions were made transparently and corporately. In
this respect, Councillor Lonergan highlighted that the
Strategy represented a major step forward in how the
Council planned, managed and made best use of the
Council’s assets and it would ensure that the Council’s
estate was sustainable, efficient, modern, and able to support the
services that residents rely on, while contributing directly to the
Council’s  financial
sustainability and environmental
commitments. 

           
RESOLVED – That:-

 

(i)          
the Asset Management Strategy 2026–2031 (as
detailed at Appendix A) be approved;

 

(ii)         
the requirement for updated Property Procedures for
Acquisitions and Disposals, as set out in the Strategy be noted;
and,

 

(iii)       the planned review of the
Community Asset Transfer guidance be noted.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Council's Asset Management Strategy 2026-2031.

content:
The report will approve fees and charges (over
£0.250m) and will therefore need to be a key
decision.
 


The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive
Director (Resources), which provided a full schedule of fees and
charges to be considered as part of the Cabinet’s budget
proposals.
 
The report
indicated that fees and charges were reviewed at least annually by
the relevant Executive Director in consultation with the Executive
Director (Resources) and the relevant Cabinet Member and the
proposals following the latest such review had been detailed in the
report, which might also be considered as part of developing the
Council’s 2026/27 budget.
 
The report
highlighted that a full review has been undertaken as part of the
process for setting fees and charges to ensure that they remain
appropriate and full costs would be recovered wherever possible,
although, Heads of Service also considered why this might not be
appropriate for social, policy, or market reasons.
 
The report
indicated that when setting discretionary fees and charges, there
had been a general assumption that services would recover relevant
cost inflation pressures through an equivalent inflationary
increase.  In this respect, this approach had usually been
based on the prevailing Consumer Price Index as at September each year, which was 3.8% in
September 2025.  The report also
highlighted that the Council also considered whether
the actual costs of a particular
service were subject to more specific inflation drivers, such as
energy, food, or fuel prices.
 
The report
highlighted that, based on the proposals in this report, the
majority of charges would be increased to ensure full cost recovery
and where this had not been the case the estimated income foregone
is minimal at £0.025m in total.
 
RESOLVED
– That the schedule of fees and charges
for 2026/27 as set out at Appendix A to this report be
approved.
 

(Note:  That in
accordance with the provisions of Section 28(2) of the Localism Act
2011, and the Council’s Code of Conduct for Elected and
Co-opted Members, Councillor Mrs D Arnall declared a Disclosable
Pecuniary Interest in the above item but, having received a
dispensation from the Monitoring Officer, remained in the meeting,
took part in the discussion and voted thereon.)

services by all local authorities. In this respect, Councillor

In this respect, the Council still expected to report a balanced
budget at the end of the year.
 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted that the
pressures in Social Care would  keep growing in the coming years, and the Council
needed to do all it could to reduce demand, and to reduce the
rising costs faced by the Council.

Councillor Lonergan highlighted that the Council,

The
Cabinet considered the report of the Executive Director (Resources)
which, along with the accompanying items being considered at the
meeting, provided information and financial strategy planning
assumptions for the Cabinet to consider in developing its revenue
budget proposals to the Council.
 
Councillor Mrs J Lonergan, Cabinet Member for
Resources, reported that the Council’s Growth Strategy had
boosted the Tax Base by 21% over the past 10 years and has secured
an extra £1.3m of permanent funding next year. In this
respect, Councillor Lonergan indicated that the Council needed to
increase Council Tax in line with the Government’s funding
assumptions, although it would be preferred not to. However, to not
increase Council Tax in line with the Government’s funding
assumptions, the Council would lose £4 million of funding
every year, forcing the Council to make cuts to services this year
and in future years. 
 
Councillor Lonergan reported that the forecasts
confirmed that £29m of permanent investment would be required
to sustain the Council’s services in the face of growing
demand and rising prices. In this respect, Councillor Lonergan
highlighted that this investment included £12.2m for demand
in Adult and Children’s Social Care, SEND and home to school
transport, £3.9m to boost capacity in Children’s
Services, and £4.5m to help with social care market
stability, including the Council’s continued commitment to
the Real Living Wage for care providers.
 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted that significant
risks remained for future years that required a strategic,
long?term response and the Council was facing increases in demand
and costs in Social Care, particularly Children’s Services,
which required the need to continually plan for the long?term and
beyond this 3-year period. 
 
Councillor Lonergan indicated that the
Council’s forecasts ensured that, wherever possible,
resources would be directed towards ensuring financial stability.
In this respect, the Council must ensure that its General Balances
were sufficient to meet future risks, and it was proposed to
increase General Balances to 6% of the Council’s budget and
keep those under review in future years if the Council’s
risks increased.
 
Councillor Lonergan also highlighted that the
Council would implement a Transformation Programme to focus on
demand reduction, service improvement and the reallocation of
existing resources to reduce costs and improve services for
Knowsley’s residents.
 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted that the report
confirmed that the Council had again been in a strong financial
position as a result of its commitment to financial management and
long-term decision-making. In this

content:
The Knowsley Council Plan 2025-2030 was agreed by the
Council on 5 March 2025. The ‘Plan’ includes an Annual
Delivery Plan which is monitored throughout the year, and this plan
is fully refreshed on an annual basis. The Council Plan is included
in the Council’s Policy Framework and underpins departmental
and service planning, helping to ensure that service delivery is
clearly aligned to the delivery of the Council’s priorities,
and that resources are directed to these areas as part of the
Council’s approach to budget and service planning.
 


The Cabinet considered the report of the Chief
Executive, which sought  endorsement of
the Annual Delivery Plan for 2026/27 prior to its submission for
approval at the full meeting of the Council on 4 March
2026.

 

Councillor G Morgan, Leader of the Council, stated
that:-

 

“In March 2025 we agreed the new Knowsley
Council Plan which sets out our three key priorities to be
addressed over a five-year period. 
These priorities remain relevant and therefore are unchanged. The
report before you today set out the actions that we will undertake
over the next year to deliver those priorities.
 

We will continue to deliver effective and
high-quality services, we will do all that we can to encourage
growth that benefits everyone, ensuring our communities and town
centres can flourish, and we will continue to deliver targeted
support to encourage fairness and opportunity for those residents
facing the biggest challenges. In particular, the Council remains
firmly focused on delivering actions to improve Children’s
Social Care and Special Educational Needs and Disability
services.
 

I am incredibly proud of the work that we do to
provide high quality services to our communities, and to protect
those who most need our support but as I always say we are never
complacent, we know that there is much work to be done, and the
report before you today includes actions that will provide a clear
focus for us over the next 12 months.
 

The delivery of these actions will be kept under
regular scrutiny by us as Cabinet members.”
 
Councillor
Mrs D Arnall, Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care,
stated:-
 
“As we
look forward to 2026-27, I am delighted to see that our Council
Plan report acknowledges the fantastic achievements in Adult Social
Care over the course of the last twelve months, including our
‘Good’ rating by the Care Quality
Commission.
This
plan seeks to build on our successes in order to further strengthen
our offer to Knowsley residents. 
 
In Adult
Social Care, we will continue to reduce wait times for Occupational
Therapy Services, increase the availability of nursing provision
locally, and further improve the respite offer for our
carers.
 
We will embed
our new care management service structure, which ensures that our
staff are supported to progress in their roles, helping us to
retain our valued workforce, and ensuring we can respond to demand
and provide the very best care and support possible to adults in
Knowsley when they need us most.
 
We
will also review our Community Integrated Response Services this
year to ensure we are well positioned to support the Adult Social
Care Front Door, prevent avoidable admissions to hospital,
facilitate timely and effective discharge, and contribute to the
development of integrated neighbourhood teams and integrated
intermediate care services. And finally, we will continue to work
with and support the local care market in Knowsley, to ensure that
we can continue to ensure sufficiency of good quality, diverse and
sustainable care and support services that meets the needs of our
residents.
 
Councillor
Mrs S Powell, Cabinet Member for Communities and Neighbourhoods,
stated:-
 
“I’m very proud of what we have achieved to date,
and I’ll highlight a few priorities for the future. Since the
Council's Climate Emergency declaration in January 2020, great
progress has been made on the journey to Net Zero by 2040. As
colleagues will be aware, a new Net Zero Delivery Plan for the next
five years has been approved by the Council and sets out a range of
actions covering buildings, transport, clean energy and the natural
environment.
 
The actions
in the report, including the decarbonisation of Council buildings
and services, and working with the Combined Authority to install
over 300 electric vehicle charge points across 167 locations,
clearly set out the steps the Council will take to meet its Net
Zero 2040 target and build on the success to date.
 
With regards
to waste, preparations for our new food waste service are well
underway.  We have taken delivery of 9
new food waste collection vehicles and work begins shortly to start
assembling the household caddy packs. 
These will be delivered to every household and will include all of
the information that our residents will need to participate in this
fantastic new service starting in Spring. In addition, our
residents will also be able to recycle more items in their existing
grey bin, things like yoghurt pots, aerosols, tubs and trays will
also be included in the accepted items.  To ensure that
Knowsley is prepared for the changes our Recycling Engagement team
have been out and about delivering Recycling Roadshows across the
borough, with over 60 planned roadshows everyone will have an
opportunity to learn more about how to recycle more and recycle
right. 
 
As colleagues
will be aware, our work on culture is hugely important and we have
secured £650,000 from Arts Council England to deliver an
exciting project for children and young people working with Heart of Glass,
Shakespeare North Playhouse, Kirkby Gallery, MAKE CIC and
Adlib.  The programme aims to empower young voices, grow
local talent and transform creative futures across Knowsley. The
collective aim is to grow a younger, more diverse and ambitious
cultural scene and improve pathways towards careers in the creative
industries. Our
residents can expect to see many more events and activities for
children and young people during the year. 
 
And finally,
the report sets out our commitment to community safety . We will
develop and implement a new Connecting Communities Plan and
continue to improve Domestic Abuse support including a new violence
against women and girls plan to protect women and girls.
We will continue to work with our Knowsley Better
Together partners to ensure a zero-tolerance approach to hate crime
in all its forms. Domestic abuse and
anti-social behaviour have a profound impact on individuals,
families and communities. This Council is committed to working with
our partners to provide the right support, strengthen early
intervention and ensure Knowsley remains a safe and supportive
place for everyone.
 
Councillor D
Lonergan, Cabinet Member for Children’s Services,
stated:-
 

“I’m pleased to highlight some key areas
in the Children’s Services element of the Annual Delivery
Plan for 2026/27. Our plan sets out a clear and ambitious programme
of work focused on strengthening children’s social care,
meeting national reform requirements, and continuing our
improvement journey.  This includes
ensuring risks to children are consistently identified and
addressed, raising the quality of core social work practice, and
supporting the recruitment and retention of a skilled and stable
workforce. 

 

Alongside this, we are driving forward our SEND
improvement programme, embedding a more inclusive culture across
schools, expanding specialist places, and improving outcomes
through strengthened partnership arrangements and delivery of
agreed actions.
 

We are also committed to expanding our Start for
Life offer, continuing the rollout of the Family Hubs approach so
every child has the best opportunities from birth. Finally, our
focus on educational attainment remains central, with targeted
action through the School Attendance Governance Group to improve
attendance and support better outcomes for children and young
people across the borough.
 

This delivery plan reflects our unwavering
commitment to protecting, supporting, and empowering children and
families and I am delighted that once again, Children’s
Services has been highlighted as the Council’s number one
priority.”
 
Councillor
Mrs C Bannon, Cabinet Member for Health, stated:-
 
“The
Council is looking forward to building on the successes of the past
year in tackling health inequalities, including improved
breastfeeding rates, more people accessing drugs and alcohol
support, and a reduction in the number of smokers. Over the coming
year, a range of programmes will be implemented to improve the
health of people who live and work in Knowsley, from the youngest
to the oldest.
 
These include
the ongoing development of the Knowsley Place Partnership with
Sport England to support people to be more active. This is going to
focus on healthy weight in children through active lifestyles, and
on women and girls.
 
The Healthy
Schools Programme is also going to continue to expand. The Council
will be supporting more schools to adopt the Schools Pledge and to
increase the free school meal offer. The programme will also be
extended to children’s mental health and
wellbeing.
 
In addition,
the public health team will be supporting NHS partners in the
prevention, detection and management of long-term conditions. An
example of this is the development and implementation of a new
Cardiovascular Disease Prevention Plan for the Borough.
 
Fewer people
take up the offer of screening and vaccination programmes in
Knowsley, compared with other Places in Cheshire and Merseyside.
The public health team will continue to provide leadership to the
local system to understand the barriers, and to develop and
implement initiatives which aim to improve uptake.
 
The coming
year is also going to see the ongoing implementation of  the new tobacco control strategy including the
introduction of Public Space Protection Orders.
The
Combating Drugs Partnership, led by the Council, will build upon
their success and work to further improve access to treatment for
those who need it. It will also aim to protect children and young
people from the harms of drugs and alcohol, including through
tackling ketamine use.
 
The Working
Well programme which supports employers to provide healthy
workplaces is also going to be expanded.
 
Finally,
implementation of the five-year Healthier Weight Strategy will aim
to increase the number of people in the Borough with a healthy
weight, with a particular focus on children.  From 1 April, the Early Years Award Scheme will be
introduced to ensure all early year’s settings are actively
supporting young children’s healthy eating and physical
activity.”
 
Councillor T
Brennan, Deputy Leader and Cabinet Members for Regeneration and
Economic Development, stated:-
 

“For Regeneration & Economic Development
Portfolio the focus and priorities for this coming year are very
much centred on us continuing to build on the successes we have had
to date to help drive growth and prosperity and provide our
residents with the skills and opportunities so they can maximise
their potential to thrive.
 

We will have a strong focus on supporting our
residents, especially those at risk of Homelessness to access
appropriate housing aligned to their needs, our well embedded
strategy and approach to the delivery and provision of temporary
accommodation is working well, so much so I am really pleased to be
able to report that over Christmas we did not have to rely on Hotel
or Bed and Breakfast accommodation as we were able to place
everyone who needed support into our dispersed
accommodation.  Whilst undoubtably this
was a huge achievement it is not job done and we are continuing to
see increasing pressures on the need for temporary accommodation.
Needless to say, therefore ensuring access to appropriate and good
quality temporary accommodation remains very much a priority for us
over the next 12 months and we will continue to expand our
offer.
 

Just under 4 months ago the Council approved
Knowsley’s new Economic Plan for the period through to 2030,
the delivery of our ambitions within this plan will be a key
priority for the Portfolio moving forward, in particular we will
work with our partners so as to not only raise awareness of the job
and career opportunities available but to ensure that our residents
are best equipped and supported to access such.
 

The way the Combined Authority  and City Region is now funded is changing with the
introduction of the Integrated Settlement meaning as a City Region
we have far more influence as to what funding is allocated to what
priorities, with this is mind Knowsley will play a lead role in
working with the LCR Combined Authority and colleagues from local
authorities from across the City Region to define the type, nature,
extent and funding envelope for both Business support and
Employment support moving forward so as to ensure our businesses
are best supported to prosper and create employment opportunities
whilst residents are supported to progress and develop into and in
work.
 

Over the last 10 years, the Borough’s physical
growth and development have served Knowsley well, with an improved
and varied housing offer, together with the delivery of much needed
affordable housing and a resurgence of our town centres, not to
mention new job creation and increased revenue streams to support
essential council services. It is essential that we continue in
this vein and that in doing so we ensure it’s done in a
planned and coherent manner. In this regard, 2026 will see us
embark on the development of a new local plan for Knowsley, a plan
which will shape and inform future development opportunities whilst
at the same time help us prevent inappropriate and unsustainable
development.
 

We are continuing with the delivery of our ambitions
for our town centres with a diversification of their offer, through
the developing of leisure and evening economy uses alongside
expansion of traditional retail offerings. In this regard, I am
pleased to be able to advise that earlier today, Planning
Permission was formally granted for the next phase of
Kirkby’s retail expansion, meaning that works will commence
on site in the coming weeks to deliver a new LIDL supermarket. The
Regeneration Portfolio has much to be proud of and has a clear
focus for its priorities over the coming 12 months,  priorities that will deliver real change and help
improve residents’ lives.”
 
           
Councillor Mrs J Lonergan, Cabinet Member for Resources,
stated:-
 
“I am
pleased to support the proposed key areas of work contained within
this delivery plan for the resource’s portfolio. All of our
key areas of work are aligned to the 3 key priorities outlined in
our council plan, and the services within my portfolio area play an
important role in supporting the delivery of key services across
the Council.  
 
The plan
includes key specific actions for the services under my portfolio
over the next year to improve our services and support
residents. 
 
Elsewhere on
this agenda we have the proposed budget package for 2026/27 and as
in previous years we will be working hard to return a balanced
budget position for next year.  This
won’t be easy due to the risks that we are facing but our
robust and forensic approach that has recently been recognised by
both the external auditor and the corporate peer challenge will put
us in the best place possible to achieve this
Likewise, we have already started work on developing the next
medium term financial plan that will support the development of the
two-year budget for 2027/28 and 2028/29.  We are well placed due to all our hard work in
recent years to deliver on this and support our
residents.
 
We have
reported throughout the year that the transformation of the
exchequer service continues at pace, and the results are there for
all to see.  Our collection rate is 4%
higher than this time last year and we are making it easier to
support our residents in paying their bills.  Most significantly, during the next year we will
introduce our new Council Tax Reduction Scheme that will see up to
a total of half a million pounds extra being in the pockets of
those residents who need it most.  This
scheme has been fundamentally reviewed by this council and will
make a real difference.
 
To further
increase this support to Knowsley residents we will also introduce
the government’s new crisis and resilience fund. Whilst these
measures will directly support residents who need our support the
most, we are also starting to work on a number of key areas that
that will inform how our organisation operates.
 
We have a new
asset management strategy on today’s agenda that will help us
ensure that we use our assets for the maximum benefit of residents
and that we get value for money out of them.  We are also continuing on our AI journey- we hope
that this will enable us to support residents better and respond
quicker,  and where our demand is
highest and will continue to rise, help us to meet this demand with
a reduced level of further investment.
 
All of this
work will continue at pace, but I want to reassure members that
alongside this, as with all areas of this Council our number 1
priority remains support to children’s services and the
delivery of the improvement plan. The Council is entering an
exciting new phase, and all of this activity is being brought
together in this delivery plan and our new transformation plan
within the resource’s portfolio
 
In conclusion,
Councillor G Morgan, Leader of the Council, stated:-
 
“I am
confident that, with the support of you all, this Council will
continue to deliver the ambitious plans it has for Knowsley. The
delivery plan sets out what we will do to help ensure that Knowsley
remains a place where people want to live, work and
visit.  It also sets out our commitment
to doing all that we can to reduce inequalities so that everyone
can share in the Borough’s success.
 
However, it is
important to recognise that many of these challenges will not be
achievable by the Council acting on its own, but instead through
the Authority playing its “place leader” role
effectively in partnership with other agencies, businesses, and
local communities. With that in mind, I am happy to propose the
recommendations in the report.”
 
           
RESOLVED – That:-

 

(i)         the
Annual Delivery Plan 2026/27 (as attached at Appendix A to this
report) be endorsed; and,

 

(ii)        the delivery plan be
recommended for approval at the full meeting of the Council on 4
March 2026.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for the Knowsley Council Plan 2025-2030, focusing on delivering key priorities and actions to support residents and communities.

decision_maker: Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development (Dale Milburn)
purpose:
To seek approval for the award of a Private
Rent Rescue Scheme grant to Livv Housing Group to enable the
purchase of a residential property under the scheme.  The
grant provided to enable the property purchase will allow the
existing household to continue to live at the property as a tenant
of Livv Housing Group therefore preventing risk of homelessness and
supporting the Council’s Homelessness and Rough Sleeping
Strategy 2025-30 whilst also increasing affordable housing
provision in the Borough through the investment of section 106
commuted sums designated for this purpose.
content:
To seek approval for the award of a Private
Rent Rescue Scheme grant to Livv Housing Group to enable the
purchase of a residential property under the scheme.  The
grant provided to enable the property purchase will allow the
existing household to continue to live at the property as a tenant
of Livv Housing Group therefore preventing risk of homelessness and
supporting the Council’s Homelessness and Rough Sleeping
Strategy 2025-30 whilst also increasing affordable housing
provision in the Borough through the investment of section 106
commuted sums designated for this purpose.  
 

The Executive Director (Regeneration and
Economic Development) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Regeneration and Economic Development hereby:
 
(i)            
Approves the award of a Private Rent Rescue Scheme grant detailed
in Appendix B to Livv Housing Group for the acquisition of a
residential property on the main terms and conditions referred to
in Appendix A.
 
(ii)           
Authorises the Head of Legal Services to prepare and complete the
necessary legal documentation.
 

Do not purchase the property – this was
rejected. The current owner is intent on selling the property and
has issued a Section 21 Notice seeking possession of the
property.  This means the tenants and their family are at risk
of homelessness.  Not purchasing the property would result in
the current tenants and their family becoming homeless leaving the
Council with further duties to fulfil under homelessness
legislation.  This could include the need to use temporary
accommodation and secure long term permanent accommodation at a
time when the Council is experiencing significant pressures around
homelessness and the availability of housing to meet
needs.  Not purchasing the property would also be a
missed opportunity to provide additional affordable housing in the
Borough now and for the future using Section 106 affordable housing
commuted sums secured for this purpose, whilst also levering in
investment from Registered Provider partners to support the
delivery of additional affordable housing.
topline: The Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development has decided to award a grant to Livv Housing Group to prevent risk of homelessness and increase affordable housing provision.

decision_maker: Head of Highways and Capital Delivery (Jon Robinson)
purpose:

content:
To seek authorisation to introduce a Temporary
Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation Notice relating to
sections of Nunthorpe Road, Prescot North Ward, to facilitate
essential carriageway maintenance works on behalf of Tarmac, in
accordance with statutory requirements, whilst protecting highway
safety and movement.

The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery
authorises the necessary legal and administrative procedures
required to:-
 
(a) 
process a Temporary Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation
Notice, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act
1984. The sections of road identified below and shown in the
drawing numbered PT/TM/8586 shall be closed to all vehicular
traffic (except emergency services), including pedal cycles, on
24th February 2026 between the hours of 09:30 -12:30, to such an
extent as may from time to time be indicated by the appropriate
traffic signs.
 
(i)   
Nunthorpe Road – From its junction with School Lane to its
junction with Ainsworth Lane.
 
(b) 
provide exemptions in
the Notice described in the decision item (a) above to permit
reasonable access to plant or premises, so far as it is practical
without interference with the execution of the said work and for
works vehicles or any vehicles being used in connection with the
police, fire or ambulance purposes and anything done with the
permission or at the direction of a police constable in
uniform.
 

Alternative traffic management techniques were
considered however given the statutory requirements of Chapter 8 of
the Traffic Sign Manual 2009 (for traffic safety measures at road
works and other temporary situations) and in the interest of
highway and public safety, it will be necessary to conduct the
works under temporary road closure conditions.
topline: The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery has decided to introduce a Temporary Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation Notice on sections of Nunthorpe Road for essential maintenance works.

purpose:

Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e) for an exemption from Contract
Procedure Rule 7 to award a contract to G2 Recruitment for Building
Control Surveyor Resource for 3 months from the date of appointment
in February 2026.
The exemption is justified as the requirements
of Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e) in relation to exceptional
circumstances.  The resource is required
urgently following a failure to recruit staff to the team through
normal processes and / or then identify suitably experienced,
qualified and immediately available resource via SCM Matrix or
competition.  The resource is required
to complete key tasks to support the Council in continuing to
fulfil statutory building control functions.
content:
This report seeks approval in accordance with
Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e) for an exemption from Contract
Procedure Rule 7 to award a contract to G2 Recruitment for Building
Control Surveyor Resource for 3 months from the date of appointment
in February 2026.
The exemption is justified as the requirements
of Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2 (e) in relation to exceptional
circumstances.  The resource is required
urgently following a failure to recruit staff to the team through
normal processes and / or then identify suitably experienced,
qualified and immediately available resource via SCM Matrix or
competition.  The resource is required
to complete key tasks to support the Council in continuing to
fulfil statutory building control functions.
 

That the Executive Director (Resources)
in consultation with the Executive Director
(Regeneration and Economic Development) hereby approve:
 
i) That an exemption from Contract Procedure
Rule 7 be granted, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.2.2
(e), to permit the award of a contract without competition for
Building Control Surveyor Resource.
 
ii) That the Head of Planning and Building
Control be authorised to award a contract without competition to G2
recruitment for Building Control Surveyor Resource for 3 months
from the date of appointment in February 2026.
 
iii) That the Procurement Team be authorised
to make the necessary arrangements for the issue of the relevant
contract documentation.
 

The alternative of utilising the process of
SCM Matrix has been considered but rejected given the lack of
availability of suitably qualified and experienced resources with
the specialist skills required.  SCM
Matrix had no qualified candidates required at this time.
topline: The Executive Director Resources has decided to award a contract to G2 Recruitment for Building Control Surveyor Resource for 3 months due to urgent staffing needs.

c(i)      That, in accordance with
Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(1), the contract with Gartner UK Ltd
for the provision of research services to support the internal
audit team be modified by extending the term as provided for within
the existing contract at Part B: Terms and Conditions, section
1.3from 1 April 2026 to March 2027; and
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.

This option was rejected. The Internal Audit
Team has one vacancy within the team. 
Consideration was given to filling this vacancy but as a number of
the team are already in relatively new roles, it was determined
that this would increase the current training and development
pressure on team managers.  Therefore,
instead of filling the post, continuing to procure services from
Gartner will provide additional capacity for training and
development of the team, as well as access to different types of
resources and training material, and a range of experts and users
to share documents, ideas, and best practice.  Without this additional capacity the Audit Team
would face difficulties in delivering its audit plan and further
developing the knowledge and skills of the team.
 
Deliver in house: The services are not
available in house.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
Gartner is already
providing a good service to the audit team which has been effective
in achieving the required objectives of capacity and skills
development. Tendering and awarding a new contract is therefore
considered not to be appropriate at this point.

purpose:
Updating the fees & charges applied by the
Fleet & Logistics Management Service with regards to MOT Tests
and Taxi Licensing.
 
These changes have been
necessitated due to changes in how the licensing service approve
vehicles as being fit to operate as a Private Hire Vehicle licensed
in Knowsley.
 
The changes proposed reflect
that in the future the Licensing Service currently require the
Fleet and Logistics Management Service to provide suitability
assessments for vehicles instead of the previous compliance test
that has been phased out from the end of January 2026. This has
resulted in the service having additional capacity within the
Stretton Way workshop for private MOT customers.

vehicles as being fit to operate as a Private Hire Vehicle licensed
in Knowsley.
 
The changes proposed reflect
that in the future the Licensing Service currently require the
Fleet and Logistics Management Service to provide suitability
assessments for vehicles instead of the previous compliance test
that has been phased out from the end of January 2026. This has

- £60.00

content:
The purpose of this report is
to seek approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 6.5.2
(iv) (Schedule 1), for the award of a
contract to Inspira Health Ltd for the Health Check Support Service from 1
April 2026 to 31 March 2028,
including options to
extend for an additional two twelve-month periods to a maximum of
31 March 2029.
 
The reason for the decision is
that a compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in
accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 6 and the winning bidder
has been identified as providing the most advantageous offer to the
Council.
 

 
(i)     That, in
accordance with Contract Procedure Rule Schedule 1 6.5.2 (iv), a
contract be awarded to Inspira Health Ltd for the provision of a
Health Check Support Service from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2028, including options to extend for an additional one twelve-month period to a
maximum of 31 March 2029.
 
(ii)    That the Procurement Team be
authorised to make the necessary arrangements for the issue of the
relevant contract documentation.
 


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and
rejected because the Health Check Support Service offers valuable
support to the Knowsley GP’s delivering the NHS Health
Checks. Not having a health check support service can lead to
significant negative health outcomes for Knowsley residents. As
serious health conditions such as Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes,
Heart Disease and Dementia can go undetected and undiagnosed. NHS
Health Checks also prevent underlying conditions from worsening
overtime, which could eventually lead to more complex medical
conditions and costly treatments later.
 
 
Regular health check-ups help
to assess risk and enable individuals to take preventative action
such as lifestyle change e.g. diet, exercise and quitting smoking.
A lack of standard operating procedures for NHS Health Checks could
lead to generic, unclear or inconsistent health advice, resulting
in increased patient confusion, stress and anxiety, and ultimately
leading to greater pressure on our mental health and wellbeing
services.
Knowsley’s most
vulnerable groups may also face greater barriers to accessing an
NHS Health Check, which will ultimately widen health inequalities
in Knowsley.
 

Deliver in House:
This option was considered and
rejected because setting up and delivering an in-house health check
support service can lead to significant and increased costs. Health
check support services also require specialist medical expertise,
and it could be difficult for the council to recruit and retain
accredited and experienced professionals in-house. Knowsley’s
most vulnerable groups may also face greater barriers to accessing
an NHS Health Check, which will ultimately widen health
inequalities in Knowsley. Additionally, it may be difficult for the
council to flex and scale up NHS health check delivery to meet both
local and national NHS health check delivery targets.
topline: The Assistant Executive Director Public Health has decided to award a contract to Inspira Health Ltd for the Health Check Support Service.

content:
The purpose of this report is to seek
approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(1), to
modify the contract with Open Fifth Ltd (formerly PTFS-Europe Ltd)
for the Library Management System. The modification will extend the
contract for a further two-year period, as provided for within
clause 3.2 of the existing contract.
In accordance with Contract Procedure Rule
9.4.2(5) the contract with Open Fifth Ltd (formerly PTFS-Europe
Ltd) be modified to include the addition of a new module Aspen for
2-year period to align with the above contract extension.
Aspen is an open-source discovery platform
originally developed by ByWater Solutions, who became a shareholder
of Open Fifth Ltd in 2023. Open Fifth Ltd is the sole UK based
provider of Aspen and is responsible for hosting, technical
support, system configuration, and ongoing product development.
Procuring Aspen through Open Fifth ensures full and reliable
integration with Koha therefore ensuring technical
compatibility.
 

         
That, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(1), the
contract with Open Fifth Ltd (formerly PTFS-Europe Ltd) for the
provision of the Library Management System be modified by extending
its term for a further two years, as provided for within clause 3.2
of the existing contract, from 15th March 2026 to 13th March
2028;
 
(ii)       That, in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(5), the contract with Open Fifth
Ltd (formerly PTFS-Europe Ltd) for the provision of the Library
Management System be modified by the addition of the new Aspen
module, This will enable the migration of the existing library
catalogue to a new platform and provide a single search interface
for all library e-resources, thereby improving accessibility and
the overall user experience for residents. It will also support the
implementation of the Library App (LiDA), providing an additional
digital channel for residents to engage with the Library
Service.
 
(iii)      That the Procurement Team
be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and rejected on the
grounds that the existing contract is scheduled to expire on
14th March 2026 but has the option to extend for a
further two years as part of the current contract. If the contract
expires then the Library Service will not have a Library management
system in place to deliver services to local residents. The option
to not purchase Aspen was also considered and rejected on the
grounds that it would result in the library catalogue becoming
outdated and increasingly unable to meet user expectations. Without
Aspen, the existing library catalogue could not be migrated to a
modern platform, nor would we be able to implement the Library App
(LiDA) limiting future development and integration of digital
services
 
Seek Competition (Quotation /
Tender):  The current contract continues
to perform well, and we have developed a long-standing, effective
working relationship with Open Fifth Ltd that we are keen to
maintain. Service delivery is subject to regular monitoring and
review, supported by scheduled account meetings, and Open Fifth Ltd
has consistently demonstrated a responsive and supportive approach.
Furthermore, the majority of Library Services across the Liverpool
City Region also use this Library Management System, enabling
stronger collaboration and shared best practice within the region.
At this stage, awarding a new contract is not considered
appropriate given the significant timescales required to undertake
a full tender.
 
Seeking competition for the provision of Aspen
was not considered a viable option, as Open Fifth Ltd is able to
ensure that the Aspen module is fully aligned with the existing
Koha Library Management System, particularly in relation to
security, data protection, ongoing service maintenance, and
software upgrades. Introducing an additional provider would
increase complexity and risk, offer no clear operational advantage,
and is therefore not considered advantageous.
topline: The Head of Customer Services has decided to extend the contract with Open Fifth Ltd for the Library Management System and add a new Aspen module.

rejected as the Supply of Chilled Goods contract held by Ralph
Livesey Ltd would expire and we would need to reprocure a new
contract which would compromise the ability of the service to meet
its obligation to feed children in Schools across the borough.

products there would also be increased disruption whilst an
alternative supplier was sought.

Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation Notice relating to
sections of Grahams Road, St Gabriels Ward, to facilitate essential
carriageway maintenance works on behalf of Tarmac, in accordance
with statutory requirements, whilst protecting highway safety and
movement.

The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery
authorises the necessary legal and administrative procedures
required to:-
 
(a) 
process a Temporary Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation
Notice, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act
1984. The sections of road identified below and shown in the
drawing numbered PT/TM/8561 shall be closed to all vehicular
traffic (except emergency services), including pedal cycles, on
30th January 2026 between the hours of 09:30 –
12:30, to such an extent as may from time to time be indicated by
the appropriate traffic signs.
 
(i)

(b) 
provide exemptions in
the Notice described in the decision item (a) above to permit
reasonable access to plant or premises, so far as it is practical
without interference with the execution of the said work and for
works vehicles or any vehicles being used in connection with the
police, fire or ambulance purposes and anything done with the
permission or at the direction of a police constable in
uniform.
 

Alternative traffic management techniques were
considered however given the statutory requirements of Chapter 8 of
the Traffic Sign Manual 2009 (for traffic safety measures at road
works and other temporary situations) and in the interest of
highway and public safety, it will be necessary to conduct the
works under temporary road closure conditions.

decision_maker: Executive Director Health & Social Care (Sarah Smith)
purpose:
Following an increase in the Real Living Wage
from 1 April 2025, this report seeks approval that the specialist
nursing care fee rates with Delphside
Ltd are increased as detailed in appendix 2 from 2 February 2026,
to support the continued sustainability of the service.
 
The report also seeks to make a one-off
payment of an amount equal to what they would have been paid if the
specialist nursing care fee rates had increased from 1 April
2025.
 
This modification is permitted under The
Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023,
Regulation 13(1)(a).
 
 
13. (1) Subject to paragraph (3),
a contract or framework agreement for relevant health care services
may be modified during its term without following a new procurement
process under these Regulations only where—
 
(a) 
the modification is clearly and unambiguously provided for in the
contract or framework agreement documents,
 
This provision applies to any health services
contracts even if they were originally awarded outside of the
Provider Selection Regime (PSR), as is the case in this
instance.  PSR allows for greater
flexibility in procurement processes whilst still providing for
transparency and proportionality. 
Section 12 of the existing contract clearly and unambiguously
provides for this proposed modification.
content:
Following an increase in the Real Living Wage
from 1 April 2025, this report seeks approval that the specialist
nursing care fee rates with Delphside
Ltd are increased as detailed in appendix 2 from 2 February 2026,
to support the continued sustainability of the service.
 
The report also seeks to make a one-off
payment of an amount equal to what they would have been paid if the
specialist nursing care fee rates had increased from 1 April
2025.
 
This modification is permitted under The
Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023,
Regulation 13(1)(a).
 
 
13. (1) Subject to paragraph (3),
a contract or framework agreement for relevant health care services
may be modified during its term without following a new procurement
process under these Regulations only where—
 
(a) 
the modification is clearly and unambiguously provided for in the
contract or framework agreement documents,
 
This provision applies to any health services
contracts even if they were originally awarded outside of the
Provider Selection Regime (PSR), as is the case in this
instance.  PSR allows for greater
flexibility in procurement processes whilst still providing for
transparency and proportionality. 
Section 12 of the existing contract clearly and unambiguously
provides for this proposed modification.
 

(i)       That, in accordance
with The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime)
Regulations 2023, Regulation 13(1)(a), the contract with
Delphside Ltd for the provision of
specialist nursing care be modified by increasing the fee rates, as
provided for within the existing contract at section 12, as
detailed in Appendix 2 to the report from 2 February 2026 to 31
March 2026;
 
(ii)       That a separate
one-off payment be made to Delphside
Ltd of an amount equal to what they would have been paid if the
specialist nursing care fee rates agreed in (i) had been increased
from 1 April 2025, which is when the provider started to incur the
additional costs, and;
 
(iii)      That the Procurement Team
be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation
 


Do Nothing (Freeze Rates)
This would have retained fee rates at 2024/25
levels.  This was rejected as analysis
of the providers costs identified that this is not sufficient to
sustain the service due to inflationary increase in costs across
the service and exceptional increases in Employers National
Insurance contribution and the Real Living Wage from 1 April
2025.
 

Pay the 7.53% increase in line with the standard rates
The provider rejected an increase of 7.53% so
commissioners undertook an open book accounting exercise. The open
book accounting exercise identified that an increase of 7.53% was
insufficient to sustain the service due to cost pressures unique to
this [specialist] care home.
topline: The Executive Director Health & Social Care has decided to approve an increase in specialist nursing care fee rates with Delphside Ltd to support service sustainability.

purpose:
The purpose of the report is to
seek approval for the introduction of a Second Chance Housing
Project.  The project aims to support
hard to house homeless applicants as a way of preventing the
potential of long-term future cycles of homelessness. This will
also alleviate pressure on both Adult Services and Children’s
