content:
The purpose of the report is to
seek approval for the introduction of a Second Chance Housing
Project.  The project aims to support
hard to house homeless applicants as a way of preventing the
potential of long-term future cycles of homelessness. This will
also alleviate pressure on both Adult Services and Children’s
Social Care.
 

The Executive Director (Regeneration and
Economic Development) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Regeneration and Economic Development hereby:
 
(i)            
Approves the creation of a Second Chance Housing Project aimed at
securing accommodation to support, on a discretionary basis, hard
to house households including households found to be intentionally
homeless.
(ii)           
Approves the Council supporting participating Registered Providers
of Social Housing under the terms of the Project to reduce the
financial risk to them of accepting referred households.
(iii)         
Approves the two-year variation to the Property Pool Plus
Allocation Scheme under paragraph 4.6.4 (1) of the Scheme to
support the delivery of the Second Chance Housing Project through
the use of discretion.
(iv)         
Endorses the proposal for Strategic Housing to lease homes from
Registered Providers of Social Housing to be used as temporary
accommodation for households who will be accepted onto the Project,
but additional assurance is required before granting a tenancy.
(v)          
Authorise the Head of Housing and Property and Group Manager of
Housing to approve acceptance of hard to house applicants onto the
Second Chance Housing Scheme and to approve referrals for
accommodation through the Project
(vi)         
Authorises the Head of Legal Services to prepare and complete the
necessary legal documentation.
 

Do nothing – This was
rejected because it does not enable the Council to adopt a holistic
homelessness prevention approach to those households who are deemed
to be intentionally homeless. This often results in prolonged
homelessness and leads to increased pressures for other Council
services.
topline: The Executive Director has decided to introduce a Second Chance Housing Project to support hard to house homeless applicants and prevent long-term cycles of homelessness.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
This plan sets out the short-term priorities that the
Council intends to complete by 2030 on its journey to Net
Zero.
content:
This plan sets out the short-term priorities that the
Council intends to complete by 2030 on its journey to Net
Zero.
 


             
The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive Director
(Communities and Neighbourhoods) which outlinedthe proposedactions
inthe NetZero DeliveryPlan 2026-2030 under the key pillars of
Transport, Buildings, Clean Energy andNatural
Environment.  In this respect, the Council also
recognisedthat cross-cutting actions such as Waste, Air Quality and
Health were also critical, and those pillars aligned with the
Liverpool City Region’s Climate Action Plan.

 

             
Councillor Mrs S Powell, Cabinet Member for Communities and
Neighbourhoods reported that the Council had declared a Climate
Emergency in January 2020 and committedto meetinga NetCarbon
Zero2040 targetfor emissionsfrom the Council’sestates
andservices.  In this respect. In order to maximise
theCouncil’s impacton this agenda,a ClimateEmergency
ActionPlan had
beenapproved byCabinet in November2020, anda NetZero
DeliveryPlan had also
been developedto focus on short-term priorities between 2022
to 2025.

 

             
Councillor Powell highlighted that since the Council's Climate
Emergency declaration in January 2020, progress had been made on
the Council's journey to a Net Zero 2040.  In this respect, a broad range of projects had
been undertaken over the last five years from the decarbonisation
of public sector buildings, piloting alternative and low carbon
fuel in fleet vehicles, to the creation of both the Schools Climate
Network and the Climate Education Opportunities Programme.
Councillor Powell highlighted that the Council’s commitment
to work with partner organisations to reduce carbon emissions had
been crucial, and this work with partners would
continue.

 

             
Councillor Powell reported that the delivery of those projects had
resulted in a significant reduction in carbon emissions from the
Council's internal estates and services in 2024/25 when compared to
2009/2010 level and a new Net Zero Delivery Plan covering 2026-2030
had been developed which outlined the steps to be taken to build on
this achievement.

 

             
RESOLVED – That the Net Zero Delivery Plan 2026-2030,
attached at Appendix A, be approved.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Net Zero Delivery Plan 2026-2030.

content:
The Cabinet considered the report of the Interim
Executive Director (Children’s Services) which
set out a proposed Cabinet response to the
recommendations put forward by the Children’s Services
Scrutiny Committee as a result of its Task and Finish Scrutiny
Review of Education Services.
 
Councillor D Lonergan, Cabinet Member for Children’s
Services thanked Members of the Scrutiny Committee for the thorough
and constructive way in which the review had been undertaken as the
Committee had taken a genuine cradle to career view of education in
Knowsley, engaging directly with schools, colleges, partners,
children and young people.
 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted that the review recognised the
many strengths across the Council’s education system and also
the commitment of staff, strong leadership in schools and colleges,
and the collaborative culture that supported school improvement
across the Borough. Councillor Lonergan indicated that the review
did not shy away from the challenges the Council faced and it
highlighted areas where the Council could support the most
vulnerable children, improving attendance, strengthening
transitions, and ensuring young people could access the right
post-16 pathways.
 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted that many of the actions
identified would be delivered through existing partnerships and
resources, while others would involve further modelling and
analysis to inform future decisions. In this respect, this work
would directly shape the new Education Strategy for Knowsley that
would intend to launch in September 2026 and would be subject to
full consultation and continued scrutiny involvement.
 
Councillor Lonergan reported that the Council could not ignore
the importance of education and with partners, the Council were
always looking at how to break down barriers to
opportunity, ensuring all children in Knowsley fulfil their
potential. In this respect, Councillor Lonergan commended
the report and its recommendations.
 
           
RESOLVED – That:-
 

(i)         all of
the recommendations arising from the Scrutiny Review be
agreed;
 

(ii)        the
Cabinet’s response as proposed at Appendix A to this report
be agreed and published; and,
 

(iii)       that reviews of
progress in implementing the recommendations should be reported to
the Children’s Services Cabinet Member as
follows:-

 

(a)        After six
months, to consider progress in implementation of the agreed
actions and,
 

(b)        After twelve
months, to review the impact of the agreed actions.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for improving education services in Knowsley.

purpose:

describes the approach that the Council will take to enforce

content:
The decision is for the introduction of a policy that
describes the approach that the Council will take to enforce
legislation that prohibits the supply, in the course of a business,
of single use vapes.
 
This is a key decision since businesses that will be
subject to the policy are located throughout the
Borough.
 

 
         
The Cabinet considered the report of the Assistant
Executive Director (Neighbourhoods and Commercial Services),
which:-
 
·      
sought approval of a policy that  set out the Council’s approach
to the use of civil (financial) penalties in relation to offences
associated with the supply of single use vapes; and
·      
provided detail of the aims of the Single Use Vapes Enforcement Policy
(“the Policy”) and the various options available to
officers of the Council in dealing with non-compliance.
 
Councillor Mrs S Powell, Cabinet Member for Communities and
Neighbourhoods, reported that the Policy had been
consistent with the principles of good regulation and complements
the Corporate Enforcement Policy. In this respect, all actions
would be targeted, transparent, consistent, appropriate and fair.
Councillor Powell reported that the Policy fulfils the
Council’s obligation under the Regulations, to publish
guidance about the use of civil sanctions and consult such persons
as it considers appropriate before publication.
 
Councillor Powell highlighted that a consultation exercise had
been conducted where the views of various stakeholders were sought
and the draft policy was sent to Elected Members and key internal
partners such as Legal and Public Health, in addition to external
contacts such as the Chamber of Commerce were sent a copy of the
draft policy that was also uploaded on the Council website to
enable members of the public to comment. In this respect, the
consultation period lasted for 8 weeks and ended on 26 November
2025.
 
Councillor Powell reported that as a result of the feedback
received, the environmental impact in relation to disposal of
single use vapes had been emphasised in the policy and possible
sanctions on non-compliant tenant businesses in Council owned
property discussed. Councillor Powell indicated that a number of
comments supported the approach as described in the
policy.
 
Councillor Powell indicated that if approved, Trading Standards
officers would utilise the new powers, including the issue of civil
penalties, when deemed appropriate.
 
RESOLVED – That the Single Use Vapes Enforcement Policy
which is attached at Appendix A to this report be
approved.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Single Use Vapes Enforcement Policy to enforce legislation prohibiting the supply of single use vapes in businesses throughout the Borough.

the 2025 Spending Review undertaken by Central Government it had
been confirmed that £15.6 billion would be made available
between 2027 and 2032 to provide Transport for City Regions
settlements for nine eligible mayoral strategic authorities, with
the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority being awarded
£1.581 billion. 
 

Councillor Brennan highlighted that the Transport
for City Region had been a  significant
investment in transport and infrastructure across the city region
and while the wider funding would deliver significant road, rail,
bus and sustainable transport solutions the funding had also been
for maintaining and improving the existing highways
asset.  In this respect, Councillor
Brennan indicated that the report focussed on maintaining and
improving the existing highways asset element and accepting the
funding associated with this. 
Councillor Brennan highlighted that further agreements would be
sought as the programme developed and other elements of the funding
were released.

 

Councillor Brennan reported that the Combined
Authority was allocating £32.780m of the Transport for City
Region funding to Knowsley Council for highways works associated
with non-major schemes between financial years 2027/28 and
2031/32.

The Council enter into a Grant Funding Agreement
with Liverpool City Region Combined Authority, in relation to the
Transport for City Regions funding for 2027 to 2032.
 

(ii)         
the Head of Legal Services to finalise and then

(iii)        
The Executive Director (Regeneration and Economic
Development) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for

content:
The Resources and Waste
Strategy sets out a vision for
Knowsley as it works towards zero waste and the
circular economy. It is
an item that impacts the whole borough and
as such must be considered a key decision
 

The Cabinet
considered the report of the Assistant Executive Director
(Neighbourhoods and Commercial Services), which sought approval of
the Knowsley Resources and Waste Strategy 2026-2029.
 
Councillor
Mrs S Powell, Cabinet Member for Communities and Neighbourhoods,
reported that in March 2025, Cabinet endorsed the
Liverpool City Region Zero Waste
Strategy and the Knowsley Resources and Waste Strategy had been
intended to underpin the wider LCR approach to achieving zero waste
and set out the Council’s vision and objectives for
transforming how residents and businesses think about, and deal
with, the waste they produce.  

 

Councillor Powell reported that the National and
regional strategies played a significant role in shaping the
Knowsley Resource & Waste Strategy 2026–2029 and it was
vital that the Council’s strategy not only complied with new
legislative requirements but also aligned with the Borough’s
wider environmental ambitions. In this respect, this alignment
ensured that strategic objectives were effectively translated into
operational service delivery, giving residents confidence in the
Council’s ability and resources to deliver on its
commitments.

 
Councillor
Powell highlighted that Knowsley published its Council Plan
2025-2030 that outlined how Knowsley would deliver effective,
high-quality services and support to Knowsley’s residents and
businesses and to fully meet this delivery promise Knowsley would
undertake the implementation of a new food waste recycling
collection service to all households by April 2026, the expansion
of the types of materials recycled at the kerbside, an improvement
in the amount of waste being recycled and an improved offer of
support to residents in relation to positive waste
behaviours.
 

RESOLVED – That the new Resources and Waste
Strategy 2026-2029, as attached at Appendix A to this report, be
approved.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Knowsley Resources and Waste Strategy 2026-2029, aiming towards zero waste and the circular economy.

(i)           
That, in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015 72.1 (a),

Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract
modification documentation.
 

Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected
because it is strategically relevant to the Council as it helps to
meet demand for low level daily living aids and, therefore, reduces
demand for the Council’s occupational therapy services.
Without this service waiting lists for the occupational therapy
service is likely to increase, creating longer delays to people
receiving support that prevents the need for more expensive
long-term care. 
 
Seek Competition
(Tender):
This option was considered and rejected as
there were concerns that a retender would not result in any better
value being offered. The proposed cost of the service has been
evaluated and confirmed as offering good value to the Council.
 
Deliver in
house:
This option was considered and rejected
because although the Council has the relevant skills and knowledge
to do this; it does not have capacity to deliver this service.
Furthermore, there is added value to an external organisation, such
as a Registered Provider of Social Housing, providing this type of
service in the borough which the Council would struggle to achieve
on its own.

decision_maker: Assistant Executive Director  Adult Social Care (Jenny Rollinson)
purpose:
In line with our commitment to growing our own
Social Work Workforce of the future, Adult Social Care has grown
its apprenticeship cohort year on year, with a view to retaining
these staff once qualified.
 
Adult Social Care has an Apprenticeship
Reserve to support this approach with the intention being that this
reserve would be utilised to cover the costs of these staff, and
any wider infrastructure costs.
 
In Adult Social Care we currently have 6
apprentice Social Workers across our care management
service.  These staff have a reduced
supported case load, reduced work hours to attend taught sessions
and rotate across the service to ensure they are able to fulfil the
requirements of their course.
 
To date, these staff have been aligned to
vacant posts (temp or permanent) within the care management
structure, and so we have not needed to draw down on the
Apprenticeship Reserve to the extent that we anticipated. 
However, as part of the care management restructure which was
approved in November, there will no longer be temporary posts
available, and we have been through a process to align all
permanent staff to permanent vacancies in readiness for go live,
and so there will be no suitable permanent vacant posts
either.   It is therefore now
necessary to move the cost of the apprentices to the reserve as per
the original intention.
 
To achieve this, it is necessary to establish
the 6 apprenticeship posts on HCM with unique post numbers to move
the apprentices into.
 
The costs associated with the six posts will
initially be met from the ASC Financial Strategy Reserve
(Apprenticeship Corporate Investment). As this is a one-off funding
source, the postholders will need to be transitioned into
mainstream budgets once they conclude their apprenticeships and
suitable permanent posts become available.

decision_maker: Executive Director Resources (Stephan Van Arendsen) and Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development (Dale Milburn)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
for the existing Warm Homes Scheme and its contract to deliver a
targeted project working with the IKAN falls prevention team to
assist their clients so that they can receive system checks,
necessary repairs and upgrades to their heating systems so homes
are warm and safe to reduce the risks of falls.  There is also scope to undertake other minor
electrical and plumbing works as part of this
initiative.  The Warm Homes IKAN Falls
Prevention Referral project will be funded by the reallocation of
the remaining balance of the Healthy Homes initiative from Public
Health.  The IKAN team will make
referrals to the Strategic Housing Team.  Where homes require major works, such as
replacement boilers and new heating systems, Strategic Housing will
provide advice and guidance to clients about other potential home
energy efficiency schemes.
content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
for the existing Warm Homes Scheme and its contract to deliver a
targeted project working with the IKAN falls prevention team to
assist their clients so that they can receive system checks,
necessary repairs and upgrades to their heating systems so homes
are warm and safe to reduce the risks of falls.  There is also scope to undertake other minor
electrical and plumbing works as part of this
initiative.  The Warm Homes IKAN Falls
Prevention Referral project will be funded by the reallocation of
the remaining balance of the Healthy Homes initiative from Public
Health.  The IKAN team will make
referrals to the Strategic Housing Team.  Where homes require major works, such as
replacement boilers and new heating systems, Strategic Housing will
provide advice and guidance to clients about other potential home
energy efficiency schemes.

That the Executive Director (Resources) in
consultation with the Resources Cabinet Member hereby : 
 
i)            
Approves the re-allocation of the remaining £0.026m Healthy
Homes funding to be utilised through the Council’s Warm Homes
Scheme to deliver the IKAN (Independent Knowsley Advice Network)
Falls Prevention Referral Project, to provide heating, electrical
and plumbing works to the homes of Knowsley homeowners who are
supported by the IKAN Team. 
 
That
the Executive Director (Regeneration and Economic Development)
in consultation with the Regeneration and Economic Development
Cabinet Member hereby:- 
 
ii)           
Approves the Council’s Warm Homes Scheme contract to be
utilised for the IKAN Falls and Prevention Referral Project, to
provide heating, electrical and plumbing works to the homes of
Knowsley homeowners who are supported by the IKAN Team. 
iii)          
Approves the development of a project referral process between
Strategic Housing and the IKAN Team
 

Don’t undertake the Warm
Homes IKAN Falls Prevention project – this was rejected as it
would mean that an opportunity would be missed to work in a more
targeted way to support people who are at risk of falls which may
be increased due to their homes not being warm enough, due to them
having heating systems that are not working correctly or
efficiently.  The use of the remaining
Healthy Homes budget supports the original intention of the
initiative and supports a preventative approach to falls prevention
which is relatively low cost.
topline: The Executive Director Resources and Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development have decided to reallocate funding to the Warm Homes Scheme to provide heating, electrical, and plumbing works to homes of Knowsley homeowners supported by the IKAN falls prevention team.

standstill period and call-in period.
 

This option was considered and rejected due to
the fact that the current contract for the Healthy Knowsley Service
is due to expire on the 31 March 2026. Doing nothing would,
therefore, lead to a lack of integrated health services to support
healthy weight in Knowsley. Given that Knowsley has some of the
highest rates of obesity in the country, there would be a
significant risk in not having healthy weight services in place to

outcomes for residents.

not deemed appropriate to be delivered by or a
good use of the Councils resources, e.g. skills and

content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval to modify the
contract with Morris Bakeries Ltd for Bread and Morning goods in
accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015 as
follows:
 

Regulation 72(1)(a) – by extending the
contract by 24 months from 1st February 2026 until 31 January
2028;
Regulation 72(1)(a) – by amending the
pricing of the contract from 1st February
2026.

 
This modification is justified as the
requirements of Public Contract Regulations 2015 Regulation
72(1)(a) are met as the provision for the requested modifications
are set out in the contract in clear, precise and unequivocal
terms.
 

(i)            
That, in accordance
with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation 72(1)(a), the
contract with Morris Bakeries Ltd for Bread and Morning Goods be
modified by extending the term as provided for within the existing
contract at Clause 3.1 in conjunction with the Specification from
1st February 2026 by 24 months (2 years) until 31 January
2028;
 
(ii)           
That, in accordance
with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation 72(1)(a) the pricing in the
contract with Morris Bakeries Ltd for Bread and Morning Goods be
modified from 1 February 2026 as set out in Appendix 1 as provided
for in the existing contract at clause 42.4, due to a range of
inflationary pressures affecting certain sectors of the Bread and
Morning Goods supply chain; and
 
(iii)         
That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the
relevant contract modification documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and rejected as the
Bread and Morning Goods contract held by Morris Bakeries Ltd would
expire and this would compromise the ability of the service to meet
its obligation to feed children and young people on a daily basis whilst at school.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): Ceasing the contract
and reprocuring would not be prudent at the current time due to the
volatility in food pricing, it is most likely that if we opted to
try to let a new contract for Bread and Morning Goods the
commercial terms are highly likely to be less favorable due to the
ongoing uncertainty experienced in the food service industry. As
well as being unlikely to secure better commercial terms for
comparative products there would also be increased disruption
whilst an alternative supplier was sought.
topline: The Assistant Executive Director Neighbourhoods & Commercial Services has decided to modify the contract with Morris Bakeries Ltd for Bread and Morning Goods.

content:
The purpose of this report is
to seek approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 6.5.2
(iv) (Schedule 1), for the award of a contract to the winning bidder as
identified in Appendix A for the Safe and Steady Exercise Programme
from the 1 April 2026 to 31/03/2029, including options to extend
for an additional two twelve-month periods to a maximum of 31st
March 2031.

that a compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in
accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 6 and the winning bidder
has been identified as providing the most advantageous offer to the
Council.
 

(i)           
That, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule
Schedule 1 6.5.2 (iv), a contract be awarded to the winning bidder
as identified in Appendix A for the Safe and Steady Exercise
Programme from the 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2029, including
options to extend for a maximum of two additional
twelve-month periods to 31 March 2031.
 
(ii)         
That the Procurement
Team be authorised to make the
necessary arrangements for the issue of the relevant contract
documentation.
 


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and
rejected as this would destabilise the existing postural stability
offer in Knowsley, thereby contributing to an increase in falls,
which would have a negative impact on existing and future service
users and public health outcomes.
 

Deliver in house:
The option to deliver in house
was rejected because this type of service is to be ideally provided
by a specialist organisation that can deliver a postural stability
programme to improve strength and balance in Knowsley residents,
who have had a fall or are at risk of having a fall. This type of
service is not deemed appropriate to be delivered by or a good use
of the Councils resources, e.g. skills and capacity.
topline: The Assistant Executive Director Public Health has decided to award a contract for the Safe and Steady Exercise Programme.

content:

Order relating to sections of Finch Lane, Halewood South Ward, to
facilitate essential electrical cabling works on behalf of Site
Safe Traffic Solutions, in accordance with statutory requirements,
whilst protecting highway safety and movement.

The Head of Highways and
Capital Delivery authorises the necessary legal and administrative
procedures required to:-
 

(a)  
process a Temporary Prohibition of Driving Traffic
Regulation Order, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic
Regulation Act 1984. The sections of road identified below and
shown in the drawing numbered PT/TM/8539 shall be closed to all
vehicular traffic (except emergency services), including pedal
cycles, from 2nd January 2026 to 13th February 2026, to such an
extent as may from time to time be indicated by the appropriate
traffic signs.

provide exemptions in the Order described

decision_maker: Executive Director Resources (Stephan Van Arendsen) and Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development (Dale Milburn)
purpose:
This direct award is justified under the
requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.1.7. The re-appointment
of a chairperson is required to continue the development of the
Knowsley Place Board and Ambassador programme during 2026 following
its reestablishment in the latter half of this year. The
appointment for a further 12-month period will enable the further
evaluation of the programme which is currently in its infancy,
prior to a decision being taken as to the longer-term continuation
of the programme and the recruitment of a chairperson for a
three-year period.
content:
This direct award is justified under the
requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.1.7. The re-appointment
of a chairperson is required to continue the development of the
Knowsley Place Board and Ambassador programme during 2026 following
its reestablishment in the latter half of this year. The
appointment for a further 12-month period will enable the further
evaluation of the programme which is currently in its infancy,
prior to a decision being taken as to the longer-term continuation
of the programme and the recruitment of a chairperson for a
three-year period.

By Executive Director (Resources) and
Executive Director (Regeneration and Neighbourhoods authorise:
 
(i)            
That a contract to be awarded directly, in accordance with Contract
Procedure Rule 9.1.7 for the appointment of the Chairperson of the
Knowsley Place Board and Ambassadors Programme for the period
through to 31 December 2026 to Max Steinberg CBE DL.
 
(ii)           
That the procurement team be authorised to make the necessary
arrangements for the issue of the relevant contract
documentation.

Do Nothing: Not to reappoint a Chair for a
further 12 month period would result in the Council losing the
opportunity to retain a chairperson with the reputation, calibre,
experience and gravitas to lead active and like-minded individuals
of the Place Board and Ambassadors Programme who independently help
lobby and promote the economic aspirations of Knowsley to key
stakeholders at the most senior level, alongside the simultaneous
efforts of Council Officers and Elected Members.
 
Deliver in house: This option was considered
and rejected as to be most effective the role of Chair needs to be
independent of the Council and its officers
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): As the
new Place Board has only been in place for 4 months it is
considered that a further 12-month period to under its current
stewardship is required to enable its impact to be fully assessed.
It is felt that to undertake a competitive process at this time
would significantly undermine the programme given it is in its
infancy and would potentially result in a loss of continuity, focus
and leadership, and potentially membership hence this has been
discounted at this time.
topline: The Executive Director Resources and Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development have decided to re-appoint Max Steinberg CBE DL as the chairperson of the Knowsley Place Board and Ambassadors Programme for a 12-month period.

decision_maker: Executive Director Communities and Neighbourhoods (Andrew Donaldson)
purpose:

enter into a Section 106 Agreement with St Helens Metropolitan

Rural Affairs to enable planning permission to be granted by St
Helens Council and approve the purchase of Whiston Woods from

content:
To authorise the Head of Legal Services to
enter into a Section 106 Agreement with St Helens Metropolitan
Borough Council and the Secretary of State for Environment Food and
Rural Affairs to enable planning permission to be granted by St
Helens Council and approve the purchase of Whiston Woods from
Forestry England to allow the cemetery extension works to take
place.
 

           
That the Executive Director of Communities
and Neighbourhoods in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Communities and Neighbourhoods:-
 
1)   
Authorise the Head of Legal Services to enter into a Section 106
Agreement with St Helens  Borough
Council and the Secretary of State for Environment Food and Rural
Affairs pursuant to a resolution made by St Helen’s Planning
Committee on 4 November 2025 to grant planning permission
(ref:  P/2025/0143/FUL)  and a Deed of Indemnity in relation to the section
106 agreement with the Secretary of State for Environment Food and
Rural Affairs; and
 
(2) Authorise the
Head of Legal Services to complete the necessary legal documents
and complete the purchase of the site known as Whiston Woods from
Forestry England to allow the necessary works to take place on
site.

To not enter into a legal agreement required
by St Helens Planning Committee as part of its resolution to grant
planning permission would mean that planning permission for the
proposals would not be secured and the Council would not be able to
extend the current cemetery offer to Whiston Woods.
topline: The Executive Director of Communities and Neighbourhoods has decided to approve the purchase of Whiston Woods and enter into a Section 106 Agreement for a cemetery extension in St Helens.

content:
The purpose of this report is
to seek approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 7.7.2
(i) (Schedule 1) for the award of a framework agreement to the
suppliers outlined in Appendix A for the Installation of Lifts and
Hoists in Domestic Properties Including Servicing and Maintenance
in Knowsley, Rochdale and Trafford.  The
framework agreement period is for four years. 
 
This framework is a
collaboration between three Local Authorities: Knowsley
Metropolitan Borough Council, Trafford Metropolitan Borough Council
and Rochdale Metropolitan Borough Council, with Knowsley as the
lead Local Authority.
 
To seek approval, in accordance
with Contract Procedure 5.3.2 for call off contracts to be awarded
to the suppliers outlined in Appendix A for Lifts and Hoists in
Domestic Properties Including Servicing and Maintenance in Knowsley
Lots 1, 2, 3 & 4 from 1 March 2026 to 28 February 2030 with no
further options to extend. It is permitted that after the third
year, from 1 March 2029, further call off contracts for Knowsley
can be awarded subject to the satisfactory performance of
contactors for a maximum period of four years.
 
The reason for the decision is
that a compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in
accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 7, and the winning bidders
have been identified as providing the most advantageous offers to
the Council.

i)        That, in
accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 7.7.2 (i) (Schedule 1) the
Executive Director (Health and Social Care), approves the award of
a framework agreement to the suppliers outlined in Appendix A for
the Installation of Lifts and Hoists in Domestic Properties
Including Servicing and Maintenance in Knowsley, Rochdale and
Trafford  . 
The framework agreement period is for four years from 1 January
2026 to 31 December 2029.
 
ii)        That, in
accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 5.3.2, call off contracts
be awarded to the suppliers outlined in Appendix A for Lifts and
Hoists in Domestic Properties Including Servicing and Maintenance
in Knowsley Lots 1, 2, 3 & 4 from 1 March 2026 to 28 February
2030 with no further options to extend.    
 
iii)       That in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 5.3.2, and subject to satisfactory
performance of contactors, it is permitted that after the third
year, from 1 March 2029, further call off contracts can be awarded
to the suppliers outlined in Appendix A for Lifts and Hoists in
Domestic Properties Including Servicing and Maintenance in Knowsley
Lots 1, 2, 3 & 4 for a maximum period of four years.
 
iv)       Authorise the
Procurement Team to make the necessary arrangements for the issue
of the relevant contract documentation.

Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected
because the continuation of the services supplied complies with the
Councils’ mandatory duty under the Housing Grants,
Construction and Regeneration Act 1996. 
The continuation of works through contracted suppliers will ensure
residents’ assessed needs are met and they are able to remain
living independently in their own homes.
 
Deliver in house:
This option was considered and rejected
because the requirement cannot be undertaken within each
Council’s resources, due to the skills and knowledge required
to fulfil the demands.  This work
involves the supply and installation of Installation of Lifts and
Hoists in Domestic Properties Including Servicing and Maintenance
in Domestic Properties.

content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 (2), modify the
contract with Artisan Joinery for the external repair and
restoration of 5-7 Eccleston Street, Prescot by modifying the
pricing and scope to include additional façade repair
works.
 
The modification is justified as the following
requirements of Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2 are met as
follows:
 
(2) Urgency - The modification is for the
execution of Works which are required in circumstances involving
risks to persons, property or serious disruption to Council
services. Risks to the property include the urgent requirement for
façade structural repairs, needed after unexpected
conditions were discovered during the ongoing contract works.

(i)       That, in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 9.4.2(2), the contract with Artisan
Joinery for the external repair and restoration of 5-7 Eccleston
Street, Prescot be modified by amending the pricing and scope to
include additional façade repair works required due to
unforeseen structural concerns and;
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected as this will not assist the Council in delivering its
long-term vision for Prescot Town Centre. In a do-nothing scenario,
the structural issues would likely worsen, increasing the scale and
cost of future repairs. It would also pose a significant safety
risk to any occupants, visitors or the public.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): Seeking
competition through a new tender process is not considered
feasible, as the existing contract is performing effectively and
efficiently. Initiating a separate procurement exercise would
likely result in significant delays and additional costs,
ultimately impacting project delivery and value for money.
topline: The Executive Director Resources and Assistant Executive Director Development and Infrastructure have decided to approve modifications to a contract with Artisan Joinery for additional facade repair works at 5-7 Eccleston Street, Prescot.

decision_maker: Executive Director Resources (Stephan Van Arendsen)
purpose:
In July 2025, Knowsley Foodbank announced that
it would cease trading. This meant that the five community food
banks and 10 food clubs that it operated in the Borough would close
to residents. 
 
Discussions took place with partners from the
Council’s network of community food providers to set out
plans to manage additional demand until further support was
available. 
This report recommends that the Council
provides retrospective and proactive support to our groups in
recognition of them meeting this additional demand.
content:
In July 2025, Knowsley Foodbank announced that
it would cease trading. This meant that the five community food
banks and 10 food clubs that it operated in the Borough would close
to residents. 
 
Discussions took place with partners from the
Council’s network of community food providers to set out
plans to manage additional demand until further support was
available. 
This report recommends that the Council
provides retrospective and proactive support to our groups in
recognition of them meeting this additional demand.
 

The Executive Director (Resources) in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Resources agrees:
 

Additional funding allocations be
made to the organisations listed below who have seen an increase in
demand due to the closure of the Knowsley Foodbank as follows:

 




Organisation


Allocation




TDCA


£0.002m




Incredible Edibles


£0.002m




Swanside Community
Centre


£0.002m




Northwood Together Community Group


£0.001m




Stockbridge Residents Association Food
Club


£0.002m




Prescot Community Church


£0.002m




Centre 63


£0.002m

£0.013m




 

The inclusion of
Northwood Together Community Group in the cohort of organisations
receiving direct support from Fareshare
to enable them to provide food directly to residents in their
communities at a cost of less than £0.001m in the current
financial year.

 

The sudden loss of Knowsley Foodbank created a
gap in the provision of crisis food and the delivery of food clubs
across the Borough.  The alternative was
to ask our community partners to absorb all
of this additional cost and demand they experienced at this
time.
topline: The Executive Director Resources has decided to allocate additional funding to organizations affected by the closure of Knowsley Foodbank.

sustainable food offer, to support activity following the end of
the Household Support Fund.  The fund
has been extended several times, however the Government has
confirmed that the Fund will officially end in March
2026.  This report outlines proposals
for how the reserve can be utilised to support organisations who
deliver a community food offer to enable them to provide a
sustainable and affordable food offer to residents following the
end of the Household Support Fund and in line with the
Council’s agreed approach to offer FareShare memberships to

sustainable food offer, to support activity following the end of
the Household Support Fund.  The fund

confirmed that the Fund will officially end in March
2026.  This report outlines proposals
for how the reserve can be utilised to support organisations who
deliver a community food offer to enable them to provide a
sustainable and affordable food offer to residents following the
end of the Household Support Fund and in line with the
Council’s agreed approach to offer FareShare memberships to
our community food partners.

consultation with the Cabinet Member for Resources agrees that the
Sustainable Food Reserve be utilised to provide access to items
which will enhance and strengthen the community food
offer.  This includes items providing
food storage (internal/external) and white goods

the delivery of food and essential items.  The hardship programme does not currently fund any
activity of projects which focus on the sustainability of the
organisation or their offer. The alternative is to do nothing and
not provide support with additional items, which may affect the
extent to which these organisations are able to store and
redistribute food and essential items to the community.

rejected because the Council has committed to delivering a project

capacity. Additionally, similar works on a broader scale covering

digital Youth Hub that is time limited, this option was rejected.

existing contract may require modification to include the
integration of the Digital Youth Hub and its ongoing maintenance
costs.

purpose:

approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 5.3 for the

contract for 17 places in total for pupils with Social, Emotional
and Mental Health (SEMH) through a Regional SEND AP Flexible
Purchasing System from 1st January 2026 to
31st July 2028, including options to extend for further
periods of time up to a maximum of twenty four months in aggregate,
to end of term in July 2030.
 
The reason for the decision is that a
compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 5.3  and
the winning  bidder has been identified
as providing the most advantageous offer to the Council.
content:
The purpose of this report is to seek
approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 5.3 for the
award of a contract to Progress Schools Liverpool for a block
contract for 17 places in total for pupils with Social, Emotional
and Mental Health (SEMH) through a Regional SEND AP Flexible
Purchasing System from 1st January 2026 to
31st July 2028, including options to extend for further
periods of time up to a maximum of twenty four months in aggregate,
to end of term in July 2030.
 
The reason for the decision is that a
compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 5.3  and
the winning  bidder has been identified
as providing the most advantageous offer to the Council.

(i)       That, in accordance
with CPR 5.3, a block contract be awarded for 17 places in total
for pupils with Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) through
a Regional SEND AP Flexible Purchasing System to Progress Schools
Liverpool for two years and seven months from 1st
January 2026 to 31st July 2028, including options to
extend the contract for further periods of time up to a maximum of
24 months in aggregate to 31st July 2030
 
(ii)       That it is noted
that eight pupils are already placed at the school, and therefore
the block contract represents a restructuring of existing
expenditure at a reduced rate, with guaranteed access to additional
places;
 
(iii)     
That during the contract’s term, there will be formal review
points throughout the year with break clauses in place to protect
the Council’s interest if standards are not maintained;
and
 
(iv)     
That the Procurement Team be authorised to make the necessary
arrangements for the issue of the relevant contract documentation
after conclusion of the standstill period / call-in
period.

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected as it would not secure reserved SEMH places for Knowsley
pupils and would result in higher costs over time through continued
reliance on spot-purchased independent placements. The block
contract provides better value for money by avoiding these
additional costs and giving the Council greater certainty in
managing demand.
 
Deliver in house: This option was considered
and rejected because there are not enough maintained places within
schools in the Borough to match demand and the Council has no
option but to seek alternative schools from the Non-Maintained and
Independent Special Schools sector.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): There
are no other alternative provisions who have approached the Local
Authority to consider a similar process of a block contract for
places that are within the close proximity to Knowsley.
topline: The Interim Executive Director Children's Services has decided to award a contract to Progress Schools Liverpool for 17 places for pupils with SEMH.

content:
To seek authorisation to introduce a Temporary
Prohibition of Pedestrian Traffic Regulation Notice relating to
sections of Heskin Road Footpath, Cherryfield Ward, to facilitate
essential footpath maintenance works on behalf of Scottish Power
Energy Network, in accordance with statutory requirements, whilst
protecting highway safety and movement.

The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery
authorises the necessary legal and administrative procedures
required to:-
 
(a) 
process a Temporary Prohibition of Pedestrians and Cyclists Traffic
Regulation Notice, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic
Regulation Act 1984. The sections of footpath identified below and
shown in the drawing numbered PT/TM/8524, shall be closed to all
pedestrians (except emergency services), including pedal cycles,
from 6th January 2026 to 8th January 2026, to such an extent as may
from time to time be indicated by the appropriate traffic
signs.
 
(i)

a north westerly direction for a distance of 28 metres.
 
(b) 
provide exemptions in
the Notice described in the decision item (a) above to permit
reasonable access to plant or premises, so far as it is practical
without interference with the execution of the said work and for
works vehicles or any vehicles being used in connection with the
police, fire or ambulance purposes and anything done with the
permission or at the direction of a police constable in
uniform.

considered however given the statutory requirements of Chapter 8 of
the Traffic Sign Manual 2009 (for traffic safety measures at road
works and other temporary situations) and in the interest of

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The report proposes capital expenditure over
£1m.
content:
The report proposes capital expenditure over
£1m.
 

           
The Cabinet considered the report of the Interim Executive Director
(Children’s Services) which proposed a coordinated programme
of capital schemes to increase local SEND capacity.
 
Councillor D
Lonergan, Cabinet Member for Children’s Services reported
that this had been a key step in ensuring
that Knowsley met its statutory responsibility to provide
high-quality, suitable education for children and young people with
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities.
 
Councillor
Lonergan highlighted that Knowsley had one of the highest
proportions of Education, Health and Care Plans in England and the
demand for specialist provision continued to rise sharply, with
Education, Health and Care Plans projected to more than double from
1,497 in 2020 to over 3,200 by 2026. In this respect, this growth
placed significant pressure on the Council’s local capacity
and increased reliance on costly independent placements, which also
increased transport costs.
 
Councillor
Lonergan indicated that the report recommended a coordinated
programme of capital investment to expand local SEND provision
which would create additional local capacity for children with
complex needs, including autism and learning difficulties, reduce
the reliance on expensive independent placements and associated
transport costs, support improved outcomes by enabling children to
access high-quality provision closer to home, and contribute to the
Council’s climate goals by reducing out-of-Borough
travel.
 
Councillor
Lonergan highlighted that those proposals represented an essential
first phase in the Council’s wider strategy to meet rising
demand for SEND provision and they would deliver immediate benefits
for children and families in Knowsley and help the Council manage
future financial pressures.
 
           
RESOLVED – That:-
 
(i)            
the development of Knowsley Central School,
including the removal of the existing modular building and the
construction of a new modular building be approved, and the
allocation of £2.224m from the Council’s High Needs
Provision Capital Allocation to fund the proposed scheme be
approved;
 
(ii)           
the implementation of essential car park and pupil
drop-off improvements at Knowsley Central School, at an estimated
cost of £0.140m, funded from the Council’s High Needs
Provision Capital Allocation be approved;

(iii)          
the Council’s Assets Service be authorised to
progress the required design, procurement, and contract management
processes to deliver the Knowsley Central scheme;
 
(iv)          
the commencement of negotiations to agree a Deed of
Variation to the existing Private Finance Initiative (PFI) contract
at Bluebell Park School at an estimated total cost of £0.100m
funded from the Council’s High Needs Provision Capital
Allocation be approved; and,

 
(v)           
the allocation of £0.070m from the
Council’s High Needs Provision Capital Allocation to Vantage
CE Academies Trust to support the establishment of a SEN Unit at
Willow Tree Primary School be approved.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for capital schemes to increase local SEND capacity in Knowsley.

content:
The Cabinet considered the report of the Interim Executive Director
(Children’s Services), which provided an update following the first Monitoring Visit undertaken by
Ofsted in September 2025.  The report
also set out the key improvement areas identified in the
Children’s Services Improvement Plan and highlighted those
which were being prioritised in the period to July
2026. 
 

Councillor D Lonergan, Cabinet Member for
Children’s Services, reported that the update
reflected the significant progress the
Council had made since Ofsted’s inspection in November 2024,
which identified serious challenges in Children’s Social Care
services.  Councillor Lonergan
highlighted that, whilst the journey to sustainable improvement
would not be either quick or easy, the steps taken so far
demonstrated the Council’s commitment to ensuring that every
child in Knowsley grows up happy, healthy, and safe from harm in a
nurturing environment.
 
Councillor Lonergan indicated
that, following the inspection, the Council adopted a whole-Council
and whole-system approach, supported by a comprehensive Improvement
Plan endorsed by the Department for Education and Ofsted. In this
respect, the first Ofsted Monitoring Visit in September 2025
provided encouraging feedback and Inspectors noted strengthened
leadership, robust governance, improved capacity at senior and
frontline levels, and a clear focus on the issues that mattered
most and highlighted that the pace of change had started to make a
real difference to practice.
 
Councillor Lonergan reported that
there had still been progress to make, and areas such as domestic
abuse, private fostering, safety planning, supervision, and
consistent management oversight remained priorities.  In this respect, those areas had already been
embedded in the Council’s refreshed Improvement Plan, and
progress would continue to be monitored rigorously.
 
Councillor Lonergan took the
opportunity to thank all staff across Children’s Services who
continued to work tirelessly to improve practice and also
acknowledged the strong political, corporate and partnership
support that underpinned the improvement journey. 

 

RESOLVED – That the update provided in respect
of the first Monitoring Visit and the improvement progress made to
date be noted.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the progress made in Children's Services following an Ofsted inspection.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The report will approve the allocation of resources and
will therefore need to be a key decision.
content:
The report will approve the allocation of resources and
will therefore need to be a key decision.
 

The Cabinet
considered the report of the Executive Director (Resources) which
provided the context within which the Council must develop its
financial strategy over the coming months. 

 
Councillor Mrs J Lonergan, Cabinet
Member for Resources, reported that on 20 November 2025 the
Government published a Policy Statement outlining the overall
conclusions from the Fair Funding Review and those conclusions were
summarised in the report.  In this
respect, only very early estimates could be made of the impact of
the Review on the Council’s Medium Term Financial Forecasts
and those estimates were also explained in the
report.

 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted
that the report also explained the process for developing the
financial forecasts and the 2026/27 budget options, ahead of the
Council formally setting the 2026/27 budget and Council Tax in
March 2026.  In this respect, based on
what the assumptions in this report indicated, the forecast
shortfall of £1.5m was sufficiently low for the limited
use of existing one-off resources to be used to balance the 2026/27
budget; however, permanent solutions would need to be identified as
part of the budget setting process for 2027/28 in order for such an
approach to be considered sustainable. 

 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted
that there had been very limited scope to allocate
further one-off or permanent resources to new investments, and any
significant new permanent investments would probably need to be
funded through the identification and reallocation of permanent
savings in service budgets.
 
           
RESOLVED - That:-
 
(i)            
the assumptions set out in this report which
underpin the Council’s revised medium-term financial
forecasts be endorsed;

 
(ii)           
it be noted that the revised financial forecasts
will be updated further over the coming weeks as context for the
Council’s 2026/27 budget setting strategy; and

 
(iii)          
the budget setting strategy set out in section 7 of
this report be endorsed.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for the allocation of resources in the Council's financial strategy.

content:
The report asks Cabinet to endorse the revised strategic
risk register.  This captures all the
strategic risks for the Council – it is those risks that
could have the biggest impact on the Council being able to fulfil
its most important responsibilities. 
When a risk is include the Council will put in place actions to
control the likelihood and/ or impact of those risks as far as
possible.  This may impact on one or
more wards in the borough.
 

         
The Cabinet considered the report of the Chief
Executive, which provided an update on the new approach to the
reporting of performance and risk
in relation to the delivery of the priorities set out in the
Council Plan 2025-30.
 
Councillor G Morgan, Leader of the
Council, stated that:-
 
“Following a review of the Council’s approach to
performance management and risk management, the Cabinet approved a
new approach in September 2025. The new approach and report format,
as set out before the cabinet today, is based on best practice and
follows guidance provided by the Local Government Association. It
provides an update on the progress that has been made between June
and November to deliver the priorities set out in our Council Plan
and it also includes progress against the actions identified to
manage the Council’s key strategic risks
 
In March 2025
the Council approved its new plan which guides our work over the
next five years, and the plan sets out three key priorities to
‘Deliver Effective, High-Quality Services and Support’,
‘Encourage Growth that Benefits Everyone’,
and
‘Deliver Targeted Support to Encourage Fairness and
Opportunity’. I am pleased to say that we have made good
progress over the previous six months against these priorities, and
I am sure that colleagues will want to comment on particular items
included in the report. 
 
Before I open
up the discussion to colleagues, there are just a couple of points
I would like to make. There are lots of examples of the progress
within each of your Portfolios, so I’d like to thank you all
for your efforts in guiding the Council’s work over this
period. There is lots for us to all be proud of in this report,
and, also the Council has recently been the subject of a Corporate
Peer Challenge, the outcome of which was overwhelmingly positive.
The review team commented on the positive commitment, passion,
enthusiasm and quality of everyone they spoke to and I am
incredibly proud of the work that this Council does on behalf of
our communities, but our strength is our joint working, and I would
like to take this opportunity to thank all of our officers,
members, partners and community stakeholders for their hard work
and dedication.
 
Two of our
Cabinet colleagues are unable to attend today’s Cabinet
meeting, so I will highlight on their behalf a couple of points
which I am sure they would want me to mention. 
 
Following a
rigorous inspection earlier in the year, the Care Quality
Commission, known as CQC, announced in August that they had rated
Knowsley Council as good, in all areas, based on how well we are
meeting our responsibilities to ensure people have access to adult
social care and support.  In fact, we
are currently rated in the top 4 of the 50 plus Authorities that
have been inspected to date, which is a brilliant achievement for
everyone involved. 
 
The review and
proposed restructure of our Care Management Service have now been
approved by the Council’s Employments and Appointments
Committee and the new service structure will ensure that the
service continues to respond effectively to changing demand, will
effectively support our growing cohort of apprentices and newly
qualified social workers, retain our much-valued staff and create a
sustainable workforce.
 
Our
transformation of Adult Provider Services continues with the
service recently rebranding to become ‘Together we
Care.’  The service provides Adult Day Services,
Respite, Supported Living and Shared Lives to adults with the most
complex needs in Knowsley. 
 
Since the
Council's Climate Emergency declaration in January 2020, great
progress has been made on the Council's journey to a Net Zero 2040.
A broad range of projects have been carried out over the last five
years, and delivery of these projects has resulted in a significant
reduction of 74% in carbon emissions from the Council's building
estates and services compared to 2010. 
 
Significant
progress has been made in our preparations for the new food waste
service which launches in spring 2026, with nine new food waste
vehicles and approximately 140,000 food waste caddies already
ordered and due for delivery over the coming weeks. We have created
a new Recycling Engagement team who are helping our residents to
recycle more and get ready for the new food waste service. We have
also sent out new home recycling packs to ensure that our new
residents know what to recycle and how.
 
Domestic Abuse
is a key strategic priority in the Knowsley Community Safety
Partnership Strategic Plan, and the Council has permanently
invested an additional £1m this year to strengthen domestic
abuse services, support pathways, and early intervention for
children affected. Together with our partners, we are determined to
tackle this issue and ensure victim-survivors have choice and
access to the best support.”
 
Councillor T Brennan, Deputy Leader
of the Council and Cabinet Member for Regeneration and Economic
Delivery, stated that:-
 
           
“From a Regeneration and Economic
Development Portfolio perspective, Knowsley’s economic
prosperity and growth is imperative to the future success of the
borough and our residents and our growth arising from our previous
plan was a significant contributing factor to our positive move in
the standings of the index of multiple deprivation and the 13%
reduction we have seen in unemployment over the last 12 months, the
largest such reduction in the Liverpool City Region.
 
Only recently
we have approved our latest Economic Growth Plan for the period
through to 2030 which is our most inclusive yet and is rightly
focussed on supporting our residents to gain and progress in
employment.
 
Unfortunately,
like elsewhere across the country, homelessness remains a major
challenge for us; however, I am pleased to report that over this
last quarter we have continued to increase the amount of temporary
dispersed accommodation available to us thereby reducing our
reliance on hotel and bed and breakfast accommodation which is far
from ideal for those who are homeless. Linked to this we have
continued to work in partnership with our registered providers to
acquire the properties of those within the private rented sector
who are faced with eviction through no fault of their
own.
 
Our ambitious
regeneration initiatives are continuing across the borough and
whilst funding for such schemes remains a challenge, we are
committed to working with both Government and the City Region to
access funding to ensure our ambitions and visions are
realised.”
 
Councillor Mrs C Bannon, Cabinet
Member for Health, stated that:-
 
“We have seen some successes in
the last six months which will improve the health of our
communities, and we have supported Change Grow Live to open a new
recovery facility in Kirkby Town Centre, helping to enable access
and reduce stigma experienced by people with addiction issues. The
centre combines specialist treatment rooms with spaces for group
work and support to find employment and through the drug and
alcohol programme and investment we have seen more people accessing
support and complete treatment. 

 
Similarly,
investment in our smoking cessation programmes is enabling more
people to find support to quit smoking and improve their health.
Our service providers have been working hard to reach people where
they are to help them get the support they need to quit.


 
Almost all of
our Primary Schools are now part of our Healthy Schools programme
making real changes to the food our children are eating in schools
and looking at their health more holistically and we get some great
feedback from schools involved in this programme. 

 
Our working
well programme goes from strength to strength with 250 small and
medium sized businesses benefitting from a collective £100K
in grants to improve the wellbeing of their workforce. Overall,
more than ever we are reaching into our communities, schools,
services and workplaces to support people across Knowsley improve
their health and wellbeing.”
 
Councillor D Lonergan, Cabinet
Member for Children’s Services, stated
that:-
 
           
“I am pleased that the report notes
the progress we have made against the improvement plan following
Ofsted’s ‘inadequate judgement’ of
Children’s Social Care in November 2024. During the first
Ofsted Monitoring Visit in September, Inspectors highlighted good
practice such as comprehensive child focused Plans, and that
threshold decisions in most cases are appropriate resulting in
families receiving the right level of support or intervention. We
know that there is still much for us to do to ensure our most
vulnerable young people receive the support that they need, but it
was good to hear from Ofsted that we are making progress, and that
the inspectors were impressed by the commitment of our social care
workforce.
 
The demand for
Children’s Social Care services is increasing and there has
been a significant increase in the rate of Child Protection Plans.
The number of Cared for Children has also increased, and we know
that a proportion of the increased Child Protection Cases will
translate into increased numbers of Cared for Children, creating
more demand for suitable placements. 
The increases in both are being closely monitored and the service
is working with Finance colleagues to determine the impact on
budgets, particularly for complex cases.
 
In relation to
children and young people with Special Educational Needs and
Disabilities, the numbers in Knowsley, and indeed nationally,
continue to increase.  This high number
of cases places significant demand on our services and is having an
impact in terms of performance (including Education, Health and
Care Plans rated good and timeliness of annual reviews), and on
demand for placements, particularly in independent special
schools.  This council continues to do
all that it can to address these issues, and:-
 

·      
we have established our Autism Advisory Service to
support earlier identification and intervention in mainstream
settings;

·      
the Graduated Approach, which guides how schools
assess and meet needs, is under review to ensure clarity and
consistency across schools, enabling earlier support and a more
coordinated SEND system for families; 

·      
as per the previous Agenda item, a review of options
for increasing local specialist provision and reducing
out-of-borough placements is underway. 
The first phase of the expansion at Alt Bridge School is now
complete and a SEND sufficiency review has been undertaken to
increase local special school place options, and this is the
subject of a separate report on this agenda; and,

·      
there is an NHS-led project underway to improve
inclusivity of pupils with neurodiversity in schools.  The Partnerships for Inclusion of Neurodiversity
in Schools project (PINS) offers training to schools from a range
of professionals.
 
Finally, with
regards to early years, I am very proud of our ongoing roll-out of
the Family Hubs model, which will provide effective multi-agency
support to children and families across the Borough, and is a key
catalyst to ensure Knowsley’s children have the best start in
life and go on to achieve.”
 
Councillor Mrs J Lonergan, Cabinet
Member for Resources, stated that:-
 
“In
respect of the Resources Portfolio, I am pleased to set out the
progress that is being made across a range of activities and
projects that are supporting the delivery of the council plan and
services to our residents. Financial management has always been a
strength of this council, and it is pleasing that the recent LGA
Peer review described this as being forensic and that it allows the
council to be ambitious for our residents.
 
Within the
current year, it can be seen that most services are reporting a
balanced outturn position, the main exception being
Children’s Services.  As we know,
the issue around the cost of external residential placements and
home to school transport costs are issues for all councils,
including here in Knowsley and we do have plans that have commenced
in respect of the children’s placements, and I will update
members on the financial impact of these as the work
progresses.  We have set funding aside
as a council for this, but we will also need to call on general
balances should this not be sufficient, but I want to re-assure
members that we remain in a strong and robust financial
position.
 
Our workforce
is key to us delivering our priorities and it is pleasing that the
turnover rate is below our target, demonstrating the culture of the
organisation and how we value our staff; but we need to continually
focus on the sickness level across the organisation.  This is higher than our target and focussed work
is being undertaken with each area of the council to help support
staff and prevent them going off sick where possible, and if they
do become ill support them to return as soon as practicably
possible.
 
I would also
like to highlight the work that is being undertaken in collection
of council tax.  This is an area of
intense work at present to review all of our collection processes,
and arrears, and make it easier for residents to pay.  This is progressing well and collection at the end
of October is 1.2% better than at this point last year.  We still have some way to go but all of the
current indicators are suggesting that we are moving in the right
direction.
 
Similarly, we
have just reviewed and are currently out to consultation on the
proposed changes to the council tax reduction scheme.  This has been a superb piece of work that aims to
provide more support to our residents that need it
most.  I am pleased with the outcome of
this review and the positive impact it will have for a large number
of our residents.
 
I always take
a keen interest in risk management, and we know that local
government has a wide range of risks that need to be
managed.  I welcome the revised
strategic risk register that has been developed and would like to
highlight the importance of the risk presented from a
cyber-attack.  We have seen locally the
impact of this over the summer at Jaguar Land Rover and the
experiences across the sector.  We must
not take our focus off this, and we will continue to do everything
we can to mitigate the threat posed by this
criminality.”
 
In
conclusion Councillor G Morgan, Leader of the Council, stated
that:-
 
“Today’s report shows that this Council continues to
deliver for its communities. However, as I have always said, we
will never be complacent.  There remains
much for us to be getting on with and there are major challenges to
be tackled, all clearly outlined in this report. 
 
We are
committed to delivering a whole Council approach to tackling
inequalities, including those related to education, skills, income
and health, and we will continue to work with the Knowsley
Partnership to drive forward this priority across the Borough. I am
proud of what we have achieved, and having said that, I am
delighted to move the recommendations in the
report.”
 
RESOLVED – That:-
 

(i)            
the progress in delivering against the Knowsley
Council Plan 2025-30 priorities and the performance against all
other key department performance indicators during the second
quarter of 2025/26 at Appendix A be noted;
 

(ii)           
the refreshed strategic risk register as set out at
Appendix A part 2 be endorsed and the current position in relation
to the Council’s strategic risks be noted; and
 

(iii)          
a further monitoring report be brought to the
Cabinet inJune 2026.

decision_maker: Head of Assets (Andy Lawman)
purpose:
To seek approval to the grant of a lease for
the Tower Hill Community Garden site, Ebony Way, Kirkby
content:
To seek approval to the grant of a lease for
the Tower Hill Community Garden site, Ebony Way, Kirkby
 

The Head of Assets approves the grant of a
lease for the Tower Hill Community Garden site, Ebony Way, Kirkby
whilst authorising the Head of Legal Services to prepare and
complete the necessary legal documentation.
 

·      
Do Nothing: this option was rejected as the site was
formerly utilised as a Community Garden facility and has laid
dormant since the last association that managed it ceased to
exist.  To be left as an unmanaged
vacated site would not be a positive utilisation of the space in
context of wider developments of the parkland and community
facilities surrounding it.
·      
Inclusion within Tower Hill Park: the option of removing
boundary fencing and taking the land parcel into Tower Hill Park
was considered.  However, the function
of the land as a simple amenity area within the wider parkland
would generate less direct positive outcomes for the community
compared to its potential use as a community garden facility.
·      
Delivery as a Community Garden with Dedicated Managing Body:
utilisation of the site as a dedicated community garden facility
would maximise the existing fenced space for generating positive
social outcomes for the local area. 
Short-term use of the site by Ecotherapy Garden CIC as a dedicated
managing body has demonstrated the viability of this
operation.  This would therefore be the
preferred option moving forward.
topline: The Head of Assets has decided to grant a lease for the Tower Hill Community Garden site in Kirkby.

compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in accordance

content:
The purpose of the report is to
seek approval in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation 72(1)(a), to modify the contract for Healthwatch
Knowsley, Knowsley Older People’s Involvement Programme and
Partnership Public Engagement Facilitation and Support Service as
provided for within the existing contract at clause B1.2 by
extending the term from 1 December 2025 to 31 March
2027.
 
This modification is justified
as the requirements of Public Contract Regulations 2015 72.1 (a)
are met as follows:  The modification is
provided for within the existing contract at clause B1.2 in precise
and clear detail with regards to scope, nature and conditions under
which the modification may be used.
 
 

(i)            
That, in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation 72(1)(a), the contract with Knowsley Healthwatch CIC for Healthwatch Knowsley,
Knowsley Older People’s Involvement Programme and Partnership
Public Engagement Facilitation and Support Service be modified by
extending the term as provided for within the existing contract at
clause B1.2 from 1 December 2025 to 31 March 2027;
and 
 
(ii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected.
The Council has a
statutory duty to commission a local Healthwatch. In June
2025, as part of its ‘Fit for the Future: 10 Year Health Plan
for England’, the government announced that Councils will
take on responsibility for the Healthwatch social care functions
from 2026. Due to the lack of information available at this time
regarding the exact timeline for transfer, the proposed contract
extension exceeds the outline timeline provided by the government
to ensure continuation of service throughout the whole
period. 
 
Seek Competition (Quotation /
Tender):  
This option was considered and rejected in
favour of a modification to the existing contract. Provision to
extend the existing contract for further periods of time up to 24
months in aggregate was included in the original terms of the
contract. The contract was extended in March 2025 for a period of
eight months up to 30 November 2025. This request is for a further
16 months, which equates to 24 months in aggregate, so permissible
within the original terms of contract. Healthwatch Knowsley CIC
continue to perform well.
topline: The Executive Director Health & Social Care has decided to extend the contract for Healthwatch Knowsley and related services until March 2027.

purpose:
