content:
To accept 100% grant funding of up to
£0.160m for provision and installation of photovoltaic
(solar) and related carbon reduction infrastructure at Park Brow
Primary School and Malvern Primary School, with no match funding
requirement, other than installation of data points at the Schools,
which the Schools will fund. Also, to enter into a JCT contract
with DfE (LocatED’s)/Barker
Associates appointed Contractor, Amelio Enterprises Ltd.

         
i)              
Note the acceptance of grant funding up to the value of
£0.160m from the Department for Education’s GB Energy
Solar Partnership Programme at Appendix B.
ii)             
That, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule Schedule 1, 5.3.2,
a contract be awarded to Amelio Enterprises Ltd (Amelio Solar
Energy) following a compliant procurement process undertaken by
Department for Education’s (LocatED) using the Crown Commercial Services
Framework RM6313 to provide and install solar (photovoltaic)
equipment by 28 February 2026.
iii)           
That the Head of Environmental Sustainability and Communities
approves the contractual (JCT) agreement between the Department of
Education’s (LocateEd’s)
appointed Contractor, Amelio Enterprises Ltd (Amelio Solar Energy),
and the Council to install photovoltaic (solar) equipment and
related carbon reduction infrastructure to Park Brow Primary School
and Malvern Primary School, which requires both a signatory and a
witness signatory for the Council.
iv)           
That the Head of Environmental Sustainability and Communities
approves expenditure, up to the value of £0.160m, on
photovoltaic (solar) equipment and related infrastructure to Park
Brow Primary School and Malvern Primary School.
v)            
That the Head of Legal Services, in consultation with Star
Procurement, enacts the contract between the Council and the
Department for Education’s (LocatED) appointed Contractor, Amelio Enterprises
Ltd (Amelio Solar Energy), with the Department for
Education’s (LocatED) being
responsible for the entire procurement process using Crown
Commercial Services Framework RM6313.
vi)           
That the Head of Information Communications and Technology
facilitates installation of the required data points at Park Brow
Primary School and Malvern Primary School, within the project
timelines (currently November -December 2025).
 
That
the Head of Finance agrees to resource planned and reactive
maintenance of solar photovoltaic equipment for its’ asset
life (expected 25 years), given the Council’s Net Zero 2040
commitment, with relevant school contributions from energy
savings.

To not accept the funding opportunity would go
against the Council’s climate emergency agenda, Net Zero 2040
target and clean air strategy. Park Brow Primary School is within
the Council’s most deprived ward, Northwood, where health
inequalities are at their highest. Malvern Primary School is within
Swanside ward, which as a whole is
considered to have a moderate to high level of deprivation.

content:

facilitate essential footbridge repairs, maintenance and inspection
works on behalf of Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council, in
accordance with statutory requirements, whilst protecting highway
safety and movement.

The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery
authorises the necessary legal and administrative procedures
required to:-
 
(a) 
process a Temporary Prohibition of Pedestrians and Cyclists Traffic
Regulation Order, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic
Regulation Act 1984. The sections of footbridge identified below
and shown in the drawing numbered PT/TM/8503 shall be closed to all
pedestrians and pedal cycles, from 22nd November 2025 to 14th
December 2025, to such an extent as may from time to time be
indicated by the appropriate traffic signs.
 
i)     
Unnamed Footbridge – From its interface with Pennywood Drive to its interface with Pinnington Road.
 
(b) 
provide exemptions in the Order described in the decision item (a)
above to permit reasonable access to plant or premises, so far as
it is practical without interference with the execution of the said
work and for works vehicles or any vehicles being used in
connection with the police, fire or ambulance purposes and anything
done with the permission or at the direction of a police constable
in uniform.
 

Alternative traffic management techniques were
considered however given the statutory requirements of Chapter 8 of
the Traffic Sign Manual 2009 (for traffic safety measures at road
works and other temporary situations) and in the interest of
highway and public safety, it will be necessary to conduct the
works under temporary road closure conditions.

deliver the project.

the improvements to the site and also from experiences of
collaboration in managing the site for community football use, it
is clear that the one-off purchase of equipment to allow Berkley FC
to deliver tailored playing pitch improvements to the site would be
the most appropriate model moving forward.

required to introduce an Experimental Traffic Regulation Order,
relating to no waiting at any time restrictions on Acacia Avenue,

PT/TM/8494 appended to

content:
To seek authorisation for the Head of Legal Services to
carry out the necessary legal and administrative procedures
required to introduce an Experimental Traffic Regulation Order,
relating to no waiting at any time restrictions on Acacia Avenue,
Cypress Road and Chestnut Avenue, Huyton, as per Schedules 1 and 2
appended to this report and as shown on the drawing numbered
PT/TM/8494 appended to
this report.

That the Executive Director (Regeneration and
Economic Development) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Regeneration and Economic Development: -
 
(a)      
Approve the making of an Experimental Traffic Regulation Order
under the provisions of sections 9 to 13 of the Road Traffic
Regulation Act 1984 the effect of which will be to amend the
Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council (Prohibition and Restriction
of Waiting and Loading and Parking Places) (Civil Enforcement and
Consolidation Order) 2015 on an experimental basis, in so far as it
relates to no waiting at any time restrictions on Acacia Avenue,
Cypress Road and Chestnut Avenue, Huyton, by the temporary
suspension of the Map Schedule detailed in Schedule 1 appended to
this report and the temporary addition and insertion of the Map
Schedule detailed in Schedule 2 appended to this report. The
extents of the proposals are as shown on plan number PT/TM/8494
appended to this report and as described below: -  
 
Proposed Prohibition of Waiting
(No waiting at any time)
 
·      
Acacia Avenue, Huyton (south side) from a point 12 metres west of
its junction with Cypress Road to a point 12 metres east of its
junction with Cypress Road
·      
Cypress Road, Huyton (both sides) from its junction with Acacia
Avenue for a distance of 10 metres in a
southerly direction.
 
·      
Acacia Avenue, Huyton (south side) from a point 10 metres west of
its junction with Chestnut Avenue to a point 3 metres east of its
junction with Chestnut Avenue
·      
Chestnut Avenue, Huyton (both sides) from its junction with Acacia
Avenue for a distance of 10 metres in a
southerly direction
 
(b) 
Authorise the Head of Legal Services to carry out the necessary
legal and administrative procedures required to advertise the
Traffic Regulation Order referred to in this report, pursuant to
the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 and the Traffic Management Act
2004 (and regulations made under those Acts) and to make the
provisions of this order as advertised permanent if there are no
objections which remain unwithdrawn. 
 
(c) 
Approve the undertaking of an extensive post implementation
consultation exercise on this Experimental Traffic Regulation Order
should objections be received within the first six months of its
operation.
 

Single yellow line restrictions were also
considered and subsequently discounted on the basis that the
highway code says that vehicles should never park near a junction,
whereas a single yellow line would allow parking at certain times
of the day.
 
Doing nothing was considered and rejected as
this will result in vehicles being parked in a manner that impacts
and compromises road safety for traffic and pedestrians on Acacia
Avenue at the junctions with Cypress Road and Chestnut Avenue,
Huyton.
topline: The Executive Director of Regeneration and Economic Development has decided to implement no waiting at any time restrictions on specific roads in Huyton.

homeless households owed a statutory duty.
 

The Assistant Executive Director (Corporate

(i)

in Appendix A of the report on the main terms and conditions
referred to in this report.
 
(ii)         
Authorises the Head of Legal Service to prepare and complete the
necessary legal documentation. 
 

Do not purchase the property – this was
rejected because it would mean having to rely on leasing of
dispersed accommodation to meet temporary accommodation demand
which would reduce the number of affordable rented properties that
are available for households who require them.
 
Rely on hotel accommodation to meet temporary
accommodation demand – this was rejected. It is accepted that
the Council will continue to need to use hotel provision due to its
flexibility. However, this comes at a considerable cost to the
Council and therefore it is necessary to reduce, as far as
possible, the level of reliance on this type of provision because
the cost of using it leads to significant subsidy loss to the
Council.

content:
The purpose of this report is to establish a
partnership between the Council and FareShare whereby the Council
will purchase community food memberships from FareShare on behalf
of voluntary sector agencies operating within Knowsley. This
arrangement aims to support local organisations in addressing food
insecurity, reducing food waste, and improving community
wellbeing.
 

It is hereby agreed that:
 
              
i.        
the Council (via the Assistant Executive Director (Corporate
Support)) enters into a partnership agreement with FareShare as
outlined in the Partnership Agreement provided at Appendix A to the
report.
 
a.   
The cost of the partnership will not exceed £0.120m in any
financial year (beginning in April 2026 for our community food and
essential partners).
 
b.   
The cost of the partnership will not exceed £0.026m (funded
from Household Support Fund for November 25-March 26) in any
financial year (beginning in November 2025) for former Knowsley
Foodbank Food Clubs with the cost in 2025/26 estimated at
£0.008m;
 
c.    
The Council will purchase three FareShare memberships (from the
current year’s Household Support Fund allocation of
£0.026m mentioned above) for Aid To All at a cost not
exceeding £0.007m in any one year (£0.003m in 25/26) to
provide crisis food parcels including those for individuals
receiving support from Council services.
 
d.   
That Aid To All will receive an Administration payment of
£625 (from the current year’s Household Support Fund
allocation of £0.026m mentioned above) in relation to the
support that they will provide the Council for the remainder of the
2025/26 financial year.
 

The Council has considered a range of options
to support our community partners including the continuation of
direct grant payments. However, the value and security of working
with Fare Share is deemed to be a better value and lower risk
solution than the continuation of grant payments at the previous
level.
topline: The Executive Director Resources has decided to establish a partnership with FareShare to address food insecurity and improve community wellbeing in Knowsley.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The report will approve the allocation of resources and
will therefore need to be a key decision.
content:
The report will approve the allocation of resources and
will therefore need to be a key decision.
 

           
The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive Director
(Resources), which set out the mid-year forecast of the
Council’s 2025/26 revenue budget outturn
position. 
 
Councillor Mrs
J Lonergan, Cabinet Member for Resources, reported that the
increased demand, need and costs continued to have a significant
impact on the provision of essential public services by all local
authorities. Councillor Lonergan highlighted that the forecasts
suggested that the deficit on service budgets could be as high as
£7.277m in 2025/26, which was largely due to severe increases
in demand for, and costs of, Children’s Social Care
placements and Home to School Transport provision.  In this respect, taking surpluses of £1.835m
on other Council-wide budgets into account, the overall forecast
had been a potential deficit of £5.442m at the end of
2025/26.
 
Councillor
Lonergan reported that the Council had previously set aside one-off
resources of £3.557m to help manage the unbudgeted in-year
pressure and had also implemented a range of actions to mitigate
this impact, including controls on non-essential expenditure and
continued close monitoring of service budgets. Councillor Lonergan
highlighted that it would be essential that Managers across the
Council continued to ensure robust financial management to reduce
the extent of the deficit at year-end. 
 
Councillor
Lonergan reported that the Council had also ensured that it
maintained General Balances at a level appropriate for the nature
of the financial risks facing the Council, and they would be
available to fund any further shortfall at the
year-end.  It is therefore forecast that
this approach would enable the Council to report a balanced overall position at year-end as detailed in
section 9 of the report. In this respect, the need to utilise
one-off resources in this way clearly reduced the scope to use that
money to make other investments in the continued growth and
regeneration of the Borough. 
 
Councillor
Lonergan reported that the demand, need and inflation pressures in
the current year would add significant costs to the Council’s
medium-term financial forecasts and the Council’s medium-term
forecasts were currently being updated to reflect latest
information on all expenditure and funding forecasts.  Councillor Lonergan highlighted that the position
on local government funding remained extremely uncertain, and the
Government had recently confirmed that key announcements on funding
would be delayed until November and December 2025. In this respect,
it was therefore intended to bring revised financial forecasts to
the Cabinet in December 2025.
 
Councillor
Lonergan reported that the Council’s commitment to strong
financial management had provided much-needed financial resilience
over recent years, although, the ability to sustain key services
had been increasingly difficult as demand and costs continued to
rise.  Councillor Lonergan reported that
the need to fund the identified budget monitoring pressures,
combined with potential new pressures emerging in the current year,
would significantly reduce the Council’s flexibility to
manage budget pressures, and its ability to allocate one-off
resources to new investments.
 
RESOLVED
– That:-
 

(i)           
the latest budget monitoring position for the
Council as set out in this report be noted; and

(ii)          
the allocation of one-off resources to fund the
2025/26 deficit as set out in section 9 of this report be
endorsed.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the allocation of resources to address a potential deficit in the Council's 2025/26 revenue budget outturn position.

Policy determines the way in which licensing decisions are made and
seeks to ensure that the Council satisfies its statutory duties
under The Licensing Act 2003 with regard to the licensing of
premises and persons for the sale and supply of alcohol, regulated
entertainment, and late night refreshment – all activities
that can have an impact on businesses and residents in the Borough
– whilst upholding the four licensing objectives:

·               
Prevention of Crime and Disorder;

·               
Public Safety;

·               
Prevention of Public Nuisance; and,
Protection of Children from
Harm.

The Cabinet
considered the report of the Head of Safety, Resilience and
Community Protection, which presented the draft Statement of
Licensing Policy for 2026-2030 ahead of seeking approval at the
full meeting of the Council on 21 January 2026.
 
Councillor Mrs
S Powell, Cabinet Member for Communities and Neighbourhoods
highlighted that the Licensing Act 2003 gives the Council full
responsibility for the licensing of premises and persons for the
sale and supply of alcohol, regulated entertainment, and late-night
refreshment. In this respect, when the Act was passed, the Council
had been required to publish a Statement of Licensing Policy, which
determined the way in which licensing decisions were made and
this  Policy must be reviewed and
updated every five years.

– That:-
 

(i)           
the content of the draft Statement of Licensing
Policy 2026-2030, as attached at Appendix A to this report, be
endorsed; and,
 

(ii)          
Full Council be recommended to approve the
Policy.

The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive Director
(Regeneration and Economic Development), which sought endorsement
of the findings of the review of the Merseyside and Halton Joint
Waste Local Plan and agree that the Joint Waste Local Plan remained up to date
for decision-making purposes for the remainder of the Plan period.

 
Councillor T Brennan,
Deputy Leader of the Council and Cabinet Member for Regeneration
and Economic Development, reported that the Merseyside and Halton
Joint Waste Local Plan formed part of Knowsley’s Development
Plan alongside the Local Plan Core Strategy and the Replacement
Unitary Development Plan.  In this
respect, the Joint Waste Local Plan had been adopted by Knowsley
Council and other Councils in the City Region in 2013 and the Plan
allocated sites for waste uses and contained the key policies that
the Council must consider when deciding planning applications which
propose new waste developments in Knowsley. 
 
Councillor Brennan
highlighted that as the Plan had been more than 5 years old, the
Council was required to review it to ensure that it had still been
fit for purpose and that the policies contained within the plan did
not require updating.  In this respect,
the review of the Plan found that it had still been effective for
decision making within Knowsley and Halton, Sefton, St Helens and
Wirral Councils had already accepted the findings of the
review.
 
RESOLVED –
That:-
 
(i)            
the findings of the Review of the Merseyside and
Halton Joint Waste Local Plan be noted; and
 
(ii)           
As per the findings of the review, as set out in
section 4.6 of this report, agree that the Merseyside and Halton
Joint Waste Local Plan remains up to
date for decision-making purposes for the remainder of the Plan
period.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to endorse the findings of the review of the Merseyside and Halton Joint Waste Local Plan.

decision_maker: Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development (Dale Milburn)
purpose:
To seek approval for the award of a Private
Rent Rescue Scheme grant to Livv Housing Group to enable the
purchase of a residential property under the scheme.  The
grant provided to enable the property purchase will allow the
existing household to continue to live at the property as a tenant
of Livv Housing Group therefore preventing risk of homelessness and
supporting the Council’s Homelessness and Rough Sleeping
Strategy 2025-30 whilst also increasing affordable housing
provision in the Borough through the investment of section 106
commuted sums designated for this purpose.
content:
To seek approval for the award of a Private
Rent Rescue Scheme grant to Livv Housing Group to enable the
purchase of a residential property under the scheme.  The
grant provided to enable the property purchase will allow the
existing household to continue to live at the property as a tenant
of Livv Housing Group therefore preventing risk of homelessness and
supporting the Council’s Homelessness and Rough Sleeping
Strategy 2025-30 whilst also increasing affordable housing
provision in the Borough through the investment of section 106
commuted sums designated for this purpose.  
 

The Executive Director (Regeneration and
Economic Development) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Regeneration and Economic Development hereby:
 
(i)           
Approves the award of a Private Rent Rescue Scheme grant detailed
in Appendix B to Livv Housing Group for the acquisition of a
residential property on the main terms and conditions referred to
in Appendix A.
 
(ii)         
Authorises the Head of Legal Services to prepare and complete the
necessary legal documentation.
 

Do not purchase the property – this was
rejected. The current owner is intent on selling the property and
because of this has issued a Section 21 Notice seeking possession
of the property.  This means the tenants and their family are
at risk of homelessness.  Not purchasing the property would
result in the current tenants and their family becoming homeless
leaving the Council with further duties to fulfil under
homelessness legislation.  This could include the need to use
temporary accommodation and secure long term permanent
accommodation at a time when the Council is experiencing
significant pressures around homelessness and the availability of
housing to meet housing needs.    Not purchasing the
property would also be a missed opportunity to provide additional
affordable housing in the Borough now and for the future using
Section 106 affordable housing commuted sums secured for this
purpose, whilst also levering in investment from Registered
Provider partners to support the delivery of additional affordable
housing.
topline: The Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development has decided to approve the award of a Private Rent Rescue Scheme grant to prevent homelessness and increase affordable housing provision.

purpose:
To authorise the Council to participate,
alongside Whiston Juniors FC, in the Football Foundation’s
‘Home Advantage’ Programme leading to a Community Asset
Transfer of the Windy Arbor Road Playing Fields site, including the
grant of a lease of 27 years, to Whiston Juniors FC in accordance
with the Council's established policy as outlined in this report.
In addition, to authorise the Council to accept a grant of up to

content:
To authorise the Council to participate,
alongside Whiston Juniors FC, in the Football Foundation’s
‘Home Advantage’ Programme leading to a Community Asset
Transfer of the Windy Arbor Road Playing Fields site, including the
grant of a lease of 27 years, to Whiston Juniors FC in accordance
with the Council's established policy as outlined in this report.
In addition, to authorise the Council to accept a grant of up to
£0.025m in relation to costs incurred in the Asset Transfer
process.
 

That The Executive Director
(Communities and Neighbourhoods) in consultation with The Cabinet
Member for Communities and Neighbourhoods:
 
a)   
Seek approval to explore the Community Asset Transfer of Windy
Arbor Road Playing Fields to Whiston Juniors Football Club;
 
b)   
Authorise the Council to agree to participate alongside Whiston
Juniors FC in the Football Foundation’s ‘Home
Advantage’ Programme and accept a grant of up to
£0.025m towards costs related to this; and
 
c)   
Authorise the Head of Legal Services to enter any necessary legal
agreements
 

Whiston Juniors FC have been based at the
Windy Arbor Road Playing Fields for many years, during which time
they have committed voluntary and financial resources to the
positive maintenance of the site, whilst also facilitating a
significant level of community football activity on the site.
 
The Club has been a key partner in ensuring
that the site is one of Knowsley's highest quality community
football facilities. The proposed Community Asset Transfer to
Whiston Juniors FC offers a sustainable management model to viably
ensure not only ongoing maintenance of the site but also continued
positive public benefit from the site.
 
The alternative option not exploring a
Community Asset Transfer and the Council directly managing the
facility was rejected as the Council does not have the resources to
proactively manage this sports facility. Not engaging with the Home
Advantage Programme was rejected as the programme unlocks a
significant amount of funding, which is not available from other
sources, to improve the site and cover the costs of a Community
Asset Transfer. Engagement with other potential football clubs as
managing bodies was rejected in view of the existing partnership
commitment between the Council and Whiston Juniors FC, as a result
of their longstanding and previous investment in the site.
topline: The Executive Director has decided to authorize the Council to participate in the 'Home Advantage' Programme for the Community Asset Transfer of Windy Arbor Road Playing Fields to Whiston Juniors FC.

content:
To seek authorisation to introduce a Temporary

behalf of Tarmac, in accordance with statutory requirements, whilst
protecting highway safety and movement.

authorises the necessary legal and administrative procedures
required to:-

Order, pursuant to Section 14 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act
1984. The sections of road identified below and shown in the
drawing numbered PT/TM/8496 shall be closed to all vehicular
traffic (except emergency services), including pedal cycles, from
10th November 2025 to 17th November 2025 between the
hours of 19:00-05:00, to such an extent as may from time to time be
indicated by the appropriate traffic signs.
 
i)

border with Liverpool City Council to its junction with Moorgate
Road North restricting the direction of travel to
westbound only.
 
ii)    
A580 East Lancashire Road - In a westerly direction to prohibit a
right turn into Moorgate Road North.
 
iii)  
Moorgate Road South - From its junction with A580 East Lancashire
Road to its interface with Randles Farm Interchange.
 
(b) 
provide exemptions in the Order described in the decision item (a)
above to permit reasonable access to plant or premises, so far as
it is practical without interference with the execution of the said
work and for works vehicles or any vehicles being used in
connection with the police, fire or ambulance purposes and anything
done with the permission or at the direction of a police constable
in uniform.
 

Alternative traffic management techniques were
considered however given the statutory requirements of Chapter 8 of
the Traffic Sign Manual 2009 (for traffic safety measures at road
works and other temporary situations) and in the interest of
highway and public safety, it will be necessary to conduct the
works under temporary road closure conditions.
topline: The Head of Highways and Capital Delivery has decided to introduce a Temporary Prohibition of Driving Traffic Regulation Order for essential road works in Cherryfield & Northwood Wards.

content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval to modify the
contract with Wray Bros Ltd for Supply and distribution of
Disposable Products, Kitchen Chemicals, Allergen Labelling and
Associated Products and Services in accordance with Public Contract
Regulations 2015 as follows:
 
·        
Regulation 72(1)(a)
– by extending the contract by 12 months from 1st November
2025 until 31 October 2026 and amending contract pricing from
1st November 2025
 
The reasons for the decision are, allowed by Public
Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation 72(1)(a). The modification is
provided for within the existing contract at clause (iv) in precise
and clear detail with regards to scope, nature and conditions under
which the modification may be used.

(i)           
That, in accordance
with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation 72(1)(a), the
contract with Wray Bros Ltd for Supply and
Distribution of Disposable Products, Kitchen Chemicals, Allergen
Labelling and Associated Products and Servicesbe modified by
extending the term as provided for within the existing contract at
clause (iv) from 1st November 2025 by 12 months (1 year) until 31
October 2026;
 
(ii)         
That, in accordance
with Public Contract Regulations 2015, Regulation 72(1)(a) the pricing in the
contract with Wray Bros for supply and distribution
of Disposable Products, Kitchen Chemicals, Allergen Labelling and
Associated Products and Servicesbe modified from 1 November
2025 as set out in Appendix 1 and which is provided for in the
existing contract at page 19 clause 27, due to a range of pressures
affecting different sectors of the contracts supply chain;
and
 
(iii)        
That the Procurement
Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract modification
documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and rejected as the
Supply and Distribution of Disposable Products,
Kitchen Chemicals, Allergen Labelling and Associated Products and
Services contract held by Wray Bros Ltd would expire and we
would need to reprocure a new contract which would compromise the
ability of the service to meet its obligation to keep Schools and
Council buildings clean and hygienic.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender): Ceasing the contract
and reprocuring would not be prudent at the current time due to the
volatility in pricing of the products contained within the
contract, it is most likely that if we opted to try to let a new
contract for Supply and Distribution of Disposable
Products, Kitchen Chemicals, Allergen Labelling and Associated
Products and Servicesthe commercial terms are highly likely
to be less favorable due to the ongoing uncertainty experienced in
the hygiene service industry. As well as being unlikely to secure
better commercial terms for comparative products there would also
be increased disruption whilst an alternative supplier was
sought.
topline: The Executive Director Resources has decided to extend the contract with Wray Bros Ltd for the supply and distribution of disposable products and kitchen chemicals.

content:
The purpose of this report is to seek
permission, in accordance with PSR23 Regulations 6(3) and 8 (Direct
Award Process A)to award a contract without competition for infant
feeding support for Knowsley women on the ward at the Liverpool
Women’s University Hospital and to issue an award notice.
 
The justification for this decision, as
required by the relevant regulations is that the Council is
satisfied that:
 

Liverpool Women’s NHS
Foundation Trust is the existing provider of the health care
services to which the proposed contracting arrangements
relate;
the healthcare services to which the
proposed contracting arrangements relate can only be provided by
the existing provider, due to the nature of the healthcare
services; and

the type of service means there is no
realistic alternative to the current provider.

(i)         That in
accordance with regulation 6(3) of the Health Care Services
(Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 a contract for the
provision of infant feeding support for Knowsley women on the ward
in the Liverpool Women’s University Hospital without
competition (under Direct Award Process A);
 
(ii)        That in
accordance with regulation 8 of the Health Care Services (Provider
Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 an award notice, as set in
Appendix A to the report be issued for publication on the UK
e-notification service, indicating the award to Liverpool Women’s NHS
Foundation Trust for the provision of infant feeding support
for Knowsley women on the ward at the Liverpool Women’s
University Hospital from 1 November 2025 to 31 October 2027;
and
 
(iii)       That the Procurement
Team be authorised to make the necessary arrangements for the issue
of the relevant contract documentation.
 

Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected as the
Family Hubs Delivery Plan has already been approved by National
Government, which includes the detailed plans for enhancing our
infant feeding services, part of which is the provision for
equitable support for breastfeeding across all hospitals.
 
Deliver in house:
This option was considered and rejected
because there are no appropriate staff or current services within
the local authority that can be utilised for this purpose.
 

Alternative Provider Selection Regime Processes:
Direct Award Process B –
This was rejected as due to the nature of this service, there is no
choice but to follow Direct Award Process A. In addition, this
hospital-based infant feeding service is limited to just one
provider.
 
Direct Award Process C - This
was rejected as due to the nature of this service, there is no
choice but to follow Direct Award Process A. In addition, this
hospital-based stop infant feeding service is limited to just one
provider.
 
Most Suitable Provider Process - This
was rejected as due to the nature of this service, there is no
choice but to follow Direct Award Process A. In addition,
hospital-based stop intermediate stop smoking service pharmacy
provision is limited to just one provider.
 
Competitive Process –The option
to recommission this service and go out for quotation / tender was
rejected as due to the nature of this service, there is no choice
but to follow Direct Award Process A. Women’s NHS Foundation
Trust are sole providers in a unique position due to the nature of
this specific service. This service is for ward patients in receipt
of Liverpool Women’s NHS Foundation Trust services.
topline: The Executive Director Resources and Assistant Executive Director Public Health have decided to award a contract without competition for infant feeding support at Liverpool Women’s University Hospital.

with regulations 6(3) and 7 of the Health Care Services (Provider
Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 to:

hospital based intermediate stop smoking service contract under
Direct Award Process A, to Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital NHS
Foundation Trust as the existing provider for the service and the
only provider capable of providing the service; and
 
(ii)       seek approval
to issue an award notice.
 
The justification for this decision, as
required by relevant regulations, is that the
Council is satisfied that:
 

Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital
is the existing provider of the healthcare services to which the
proposed contracting arrangements relate;
the relevant authority is satisfied
that the healthcare services to which the proposed contracting
arrangements relate can only be provided by the existing provider
(or group of providers) due to the nature of the healthcare
services; and

the type of service means there is no
realistic alternative to the current provider.

(i)   
That, in accordance with regulation
6(3) of the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime)
Regulations 2023,a contract for the
delivery of hospital based intermediate stop smoking service
be awarded without competition (under Direct Award
Process A);
 
(ii)  
That, in accordance with regulation 7 of the Health
Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023,
an award notice, as set out in Appendix A to the report, be issued
for publication on the UK e-notification service, indicating the
Council’s award of the contract to Liverpool Heart and Chest
Hospital NHS Foundation Trust for the period 31 October 2025 to 30
October 2028 with the option to extend the contract up to a maximum

This option was considered and rejected
because the current
contract is due to expire and therefore doing nothing would
leave Knowsley without an Intermediate Stop Smoking Service within
Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital. The consequences of this would
include poorer health outcomes for residents, increased pressure on
primary, secondary, and acute care services. It also risks
continuity of the service supporting delivery of The All Together
Smokefree Knowsley Strategic Action Plan 2024-2027 and access to
its associated supplementary funding. 
 

Deliver in house:
This option was considered and rejected due to
the service needing to be delivered in the Liverpool Heart and
Chest Hospital and the expertise, skills and resources needed to
deliver a Care Quality Commission compliant service, which could
not be undertaken within Council’s existing resources.

content:
The purpose of this report is
to seek approval for a change in the responsibility for utility
charge payments for dispersed accommodation from the Council to
customers. As at 7 October 2025, 62 properties have their energy
supplied by Utilita via smart meters but we have been advised by
Utilita that the product is being withdrawn and will no longer be
available to us. In light of this, we need to change the way we
manage utilities in our dispersed accommodation.
 

That the Executive Director (Regeneration and
Economic Development) in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Regeneration and Economic Development hereby approves the change
responsibility from Knowsley Council to residents of dispersed
temporary accommodation for household utility accounts (water, gas
and electric).

The option to reintroduce a
fixed rate weekly service charge covering gas, electricity and
water was considered but rejected. This option is unlikely to
result in the Council collecting the full amount of service charges
given historical collection rates figures and the fluctuating cost
of energy would make setting a charge which covers usage
exceptionally difficult. This option presents a significant risk to
the Council in terms of liability to subsidise energy costs whilst
potentially not collecting all service charges due.
topline: The Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development has decided to transfer responsibility for utility charge payments from Knowsley Council to residents of dispersed temporary accommodation.

content:
The purpose of this report is to seek
approval, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 7.7.3, for the
award of contract to the winning bidder as shown in Appendix B for
Dementia Friendly Strategy for a period of five months, including
options to extend for further periods of time up to a maximum of
three months in aggregate.
 
The reason for the decision is that a
compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 7, and the winning bidder has been
identified as providing the most advantageous offer to the
Council.
 

(i)         That, in
accordance with Contract Procedure Rule   7.7.3, a contract be awarded to the winning
bidder as shown in Appendix B for a period of five months, from 1
November 2025 to 31 March 2026 including options to extend for
further periods of time up to a maximum of three months in
aggregate.
 
(ii)        That the
Procurement Team be authorised to make the necessary arrangements
for the issue of the relevant contract documentation after
conclusion of the standstill period.
 


Do Nothing:
This option was considered and rejected
because the current dementia strategy for Knowsley has expired and
it is recognised that there is a need for a current dementia
strategy for the borough of Knowsley. 
Knowsley Health and Wellbeing Board requested the strategy be
written so it reflects and is representative of the whole borough
and not just a Council strategy. 
Therefore, having an independent organisation to complete the
strategy on behalf of the borough of Knowsley was deemed more
appropriate.
 

Deliver in house:
This option was considered and rejected
because of the capacity in the Council to create a strategy at this
time and also for the reason stated above.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The Economic Growth Plan sets
out a shared vision for Knowsley’s economic development. It
is a Policy Framework item and as such must be considered a key
decision.
content:
The Economic Growth Plan sets
out a shared vision for Knowsley’s economic development. It
is a Policy Framework item and as such must be considered a key
decision.

         
The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive
Director (Regeneration and Economic Development), which
sought endorsement from Cabinet of
Knowsley’s Economic Growth Plan 2025-2030 ahead of requesting
consideration and approval of the Plan at the full meeting of the
Council on 22 October 2025.
 
Councillor T Brennan, Cabinet Member for Regeneration and
Economic Development, reported that the Economic Growth Plan had
been a key document within the Council’s Policy Framework,
setting out a collective ambition for Knowsley’s economy,
with a clear roadmap for what the Council and its partners can do
to achieve that ambition.
 
Councillor Brennan also highlighted that in addition to setting
out the support offer for businesses, the Economic Growth Plan also
articulated a shared vision for the Borough’s
growth.  In this respect, Councillor
Brennan highlighted that the vision had been for Knowsley to have a
thriving, inclusive economy with opportunities for both people and
businesses, aligned with the broad priorities set out in the
Council Plan 2025-2030 to encourage growth that benefits everyone
as well as the vision and priorities set out in Knowsley
2030.
 
Councillor Brennan reported that the Plan had been clear that
delivering this shared vision for Knowsley involved a wide range of
partners, including Knowsley Chamber of Commerce, the Liverpool
City Region Combined Authority, One Knowsley and other community
and social organisations, and the scale of the Council’s
ambition for Knowsley required the Council to maintain and
strengthen those relationships.
 
           
RESOLVED – That:-
 

(i)            
the content of the draft Knowsley
Economic Growth Plan 2025-2030 as attached at Appendix A to this
report, be endorsed; and,
 

(ii)          
Full Council be requested to approve the
draft Economic Growth Plan 2025-2030.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to endorse Knowsley's Economic Growth Plan 2025-2030.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The report proposes capital expenditure over
£1m.
content:
The report proposes capital expenditure over
£1m.
 

           
The Cabinet considered the report of the Interim Executive Director
(Children’s Services) which sought
approval to the expansion of the nursery provision at St
Leo’s and Southmead Catholic Primary School.
 
           
Councillor D Lonergan, Cabinet Member for Children’s
Services, highlighted that the Council had a statutory duty to plan
school places effectively to ensure it delivered sufficient places
within a reasonable distance from where people live.
 
Councillor Lonergan highlighted that as part of the planning
approval process in relation to the creation of Halsnead Garden Village in Whiston, it had been
identified that 65 additional Full Time Equivalent (FTE) early
years places would be required, and through the planning process,
financial contributions had been secured from the housing
developers active on Halsnead Garden
Village to support the delivery of additional new early years
places.
 
Councillor Lonergan reported that as the Halsnead Garden Village had now been under
development with almost 300 homes completed, this report sought to
both outline the steps taken to provide early years places in the
Whiston and Cronton ward to date and
future plans to ensure continued sufficiency of early years places
within the Whiston and Cronton ward. In
this respect, the report sought approval to the expansion of the
nursery provision at St Leo’s and Southmead Catholic Primary
School, adding 15 FTE places for 2-year-olds and an additional 13
FTE places for 3-year-olds alongside its existing provision for 26
FTE places for 3-year-olds.
 
RESOLVED – That:-
 
(i)          
the capital costs associated with permanently expanding the nursery
provision at St Leo’s and Southmead Catholic Primary School,
funded by the allocation of £1.499m of Section 106 funding
specifically secured for education purposes as part of the planning
approvals granted to date for Halsnead
Garden Village, be approved. 
 
(ii)         
the Head of Legal Services be authorised to complete the necessary
associated legal documentation.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve over £1m in capital expenditure for the expansion of nursery provision at St Leo's and Southmead Catholic Primary School.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:

Borough.
content:
The Knowsley Community Fund will impact all wards of the
Borough.
 

The Cabinet considered the report of the Executive Director
(Communities and Neighbourhoods) which sought approval to award
grants totalling £0.672m to 116 voluntary, community, faith,
and social enterprise sector projects, which would be funded from
the Council’s 2025/26 Knowsley Community Fund.
 
Councillor G Morgan, Leader of the Council, reported that
in June 2025 the Cabinet approved the proposal to
consolidate several former grants programmes to better align
resources to outcomes and therefore created the new Knowsley
Community Fund.  In this respect,
Community groups needed to only submit a single application for
Council grant funding.
 
Councillor Morgan indicated that the Knowsley Community Fund had
been open for applications over the summer period and received over
160 applications, each requesting a share of the £560,000
allocation. Councillor Morgan highlighted that due to the number of
applications, the funding available had been increased in the
2025/26 financial year to £672,000.
 
Councillor Morgan reported that the applications demonstrated

decision_maker: Head of Information Technology (John Fairclough)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation72(1)(a), to modify the call off contract with e2e-assure
Ltd. for cloud protective monitoring and 24/7 Security Operations
Centre (SOC)s provided for within the existing call off contract at
clause part B 1.3 from 20th November 2025 to 19th November 2026. A
24/7 Security Operations Centre (SOC) is crucial because cyber
threats are persistent and don't adhere to a 9-to-5 schedule.
Continuous monitoring and real-time threat detection are essential
to minimise damage loss of essential services. A 24/7 SOC ensures
swift incident response, proactive threat mitigation.
 

The Public Contracts Regulations 2015 Regulation72(1)(a)
 
The proposed modification is explicitly
provided for in clear, precise and unequivocal terms at clause part
B 1.3 of this call-off contract. It would not be cost effective or
viable to recruit staff with expert technical skills to provide
24x7 detection and management services 365 days each year. The
option of migrating to a new supplier would involve a considerable
amount of effort and would not be cost effective when all
requirements are met by the incumbent supplier and the current call
off contract allows for the extension option to be taken.
content:
The purpose of the report is to seek approval
in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation72(1)(a), to modify the call off contract with e2e-assure
Ltd. for cloud protective monitoring and 24/7 Security Operations
Centre (SOC)s provided for within the existing call off contract at
clause part B 1.3 from 20th November 2025 to 19th November 2026. A
24/7 Security Operations Centre (SOC) is crucial because cyber
threats are persistent and don't adhere to a 9-to-5 schedule.
Continuous monitoring and real-time threat detection are essential
to minimise damage loss of essential services. A 24/7 SOC ensures
swift incident response, proactive threat mitigation.
 

The Public Contracts Regulations 2015 Regulation72(1)(a)
 
The proposed modification is explicitly
provided for in clear, precise and unequivocal terms at clause part
B 1.3 of this call-off contract. It would not be cost effective or
viable to recruit staff with expert technical skills to provide
24x7 detection and management services 365 days each year. The
option of migrating to a new supplier would involve a considerable
amount of effort and would not be cost effective when all
requirements are met by the incumbent supplier and the current call
off contract allows for the extension option to be taken.
 

(i)           
That, in accordance with Public Contract Regulations 2015
Regulation 72(1)(a), the call off contract with e2e-assure Ltd. for
cloud protective monitoring and 24/7 Security Operations Centre
(SOC)by extending the term as provided for within the existing call
off contract at clause part B 1.3 from 20th November 2025 to 19th
November 2026.
 
(ii)        That the
Procurement Team be authorised to issue the relevant contract
modification documentation.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected because without proper monitoring, it can take days,
weeks, or even months to detect a security breach. This delay
allows attackers to cause more damage before being discovered.
Insufficient logging and monitoring make it easier for attackers to
exploit vulnerabilities and maintain persistence within the
Council’s systems. This can lead to data theft, system
interfering, and further breaches.
 
The longer a breach goes undetected, the more
costly it becomes to remediate. This includes direct costs like
data and system recovery and indirect costs such as reputational
damage and loss of essential service. Operational downtime
disruptions in your operations, affecting service delivery and
stakeholders. Implementing comprehensive security monitoring and
logging can help mitigate risks by providing early detection,
enabling effective incident response, and ensuring compliance with
regulatory requirements.
 
Seek Competition (Quotation / Tender):
 
This option was considered and rejected
because the service provided by e2e-assure Limited has been
excellent. All the Council’s requirements and performance
targets have been met, and the contract has remained within budget
throughout. The nature of the contract means that potential
cyber-threats have been detected and averted meaning that the
Council has not suffered a cyber-attack.
 
Utilising the available provided for
modification in the contract will mean no change to the existing
service.
topline: The Head of Information Technology has decided to extend the contract with e2e-assure Ltd. for cloud protective monitoring and 24/7 Security Operations Centre (SOC) to ensure continuous monitoring and real-time threat detection.

content:
The purpose of this report is to seek approval
in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 6.5.2(i) (Schedule 1)
for the award of contract to ATB Electrical Systems Ltd for Control Room Video
Wall from 31/10/2025 to 04/11/2025 and this contract has no
extended time periods.
 
The reason for the decision is that a
compliant procurement exercise has been undertaken in accordance
with Contract Procedure Rule 6 and the most advantageous bid has
been identified.
 

That the Executive Director
Communities and Neighbourhoods:
 
(i)       In accordance with
Contract Procedure Rule 6.5.2 (i) (Schedule 1) a contract be
awarded to ATB Electrical Systems Ltd for Control Room Video Wall
from 31/10/2025 to 04/11/2025
 
(ii)       The Procurement Team be authorised
to make the necessary arrangements for the issue of the relevant
contract documentation.
 

 
Do Nothing/Not Award: This option was
considered and rejected because the video wall is now 24 years old
and had originally been fitted with CRT (cathode ray tube)
monitors. Over the years the CRT monitors failed and then CRT
monitors became obsolete, as plasma, LED (Light Emitting Diodes)
and LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) Televisions and monitors came to
the market.
 
The video wall cabinet has been adjusted a
number of times to take the various flat screen monitors, but it
has now reached the end of its working life.
 
The monitors we currently have are mainly
plasma screens and these are not energy efficient, as they use just
less than three quarters more energy than a LED monitor.
 
The current monitors are suffering from screen
burn, which leaves a shadow on the screen and interferes with the
picture clarity that is shown on the screen. As the picture quality
of the camera improve, passed HD quality, and move to 4k+ (4k is 4
times the resolution of HD), the picture quality suffers on the old
monitors and may cause eye strain to staff using the CCTV.
 
The current video wall will not be able to hold
the new monitors. Although the new CCTV monitors will be LED, they
are much heavier, and the video wall will not be able to take their
weight.
 
If the project is rejected, security staff may
to start to suffer longer periods of eye strain, staff would have
improved working conditions and the council’s Co2 footprint
will not be reduced.
 
Deliver in house: This option was considered
and rejected as this is specialised work that needs to be carried
out by an AV (Audio and Visual) engineer due to the unique and
specialist equipment that is needed to be installed and configure
to the video wall.
 
The security service has no one with the
relevant experience and knowledge to take on this project.
topline: The Executive Director Communities and Neighbourhoods has decided to award a contract to ATB Electrical Systems Ltd for a Control Room Video Wall replacement.

content:
The purpose of this report is to seek approval
for the award of contract for shop front and minor works to the
property at Newtown Gardens from September 2025 to December 2025,
including options to extend for further periods of time up to a
maximum of three months in aggregate, to March 2026.
 
A compliant procurement exercise has been
undertaken in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 6, and the
winning bidder has been identified as providing the most
advantageous offer to the Council.
 

The Assistant Executive Director Development and
Infrastructure approves, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule
6.5.2 (iv) (Schedule 1):
 
(i)       the award of a
Contract to Futurebuild UK Ltd for shop front and minor works the
property at Newtown Garden from September 2025 to December 2025,
including options to extend for further periods of time up to a
maximum of three months in aggregate, to March 2026.
 
(ii)       that the Procurement
Team make the necessary arrangements for the issue of the relevant
contract documentation after conclusion of the standstill
period.
 

Do Nothing: This option was considered and
rejected as this could result in continued vacancy of the ground
floor unit which would continue to negatively impact the visual
amenity of the Town Centre.  The Council
is committed to improving the Town Centre, diversifying the high
street offer, and tackling vacant units as part of wider
regeneration plans.
topline: The Assistant Executive Director Development and Infrastructure has decided to award a contract for shop front and minor works at Newtown Gardens.

decision_maker: Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development (Dale Milburn)
purpose:
The purpose of the report is to seek
authorisation for the Head of Legal Services to carry out the
necessary legal and administrative procedures required to advertise
the intention of introducing a Traffic Regulation Order for a
prohibition of waiting on Leather’s Lane and Beechwood Avenue
in Halewood as shown on the drawing numbered PT/TM/8403 in Appendix
B of this report.
content:
The purpose of the report is to seek
authorisation for the Head of Legal Services to carry out the
necessary legal and administrative procedures required to advertise
the intention of introducing a Traffic Regulation Order for a
prohibition of waiting on Leather’s Lane and Beechwood Avenue
in Halewood as shown on the drawing numbered PT/TM/8403 in Appendix
B of this report.






That the
Executive Director (Regeneration and Economic Development) in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Regeneration and Economic
Development is to authorise: -
 
a)   
the introduction of a Traffic Regulation Order under the
provisions of sections 1 to 5 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act
1984 the effect of which will be to make
amendment number 119 to the Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council
(Prohibition and Restriction of Waiting and Loading and Parking
Places) (Civil Enforcement and Consolidation) Order 2015, in
so far as it relates to Prohibition of Waiting At Any Time
restrictions on Leather’s Lane and Beechwood Avenue,
Halewood, by the suspension of the Map Schedule detailed in
Schedule 1 in Appendix A of this report and the addition and
insertion of the Map Schedule detailed in Schedule 2 in Appendix A
of this report. The extents of the proposals are as shown on the
plan numbered PT/TM/8403 in Appendix B of this report and as
described below:-
 
Proposed Prohibition of Waiting (No Waiting at
Any Time)
 

i)    
Leather’s Lane, Halewood (west side) from a point 52 metres
north of its junction with Beechwood Avenue for a distance of 74
metres in a southerly direction.
 

ii)   
Leather’s Lane, Halewood (east side) from a point 16 metres
north of its junction with Roseheath drive for a distance of 52
metres in a southerly direction.
 

iii)  
Beechwood Avenue, Halewood (both sides) from its junction with
Leather’s Lane for a distance of 12m in a north-westerly
direction
 
b)   
the Head of Legal Services to carry out the necessary legal and
administrative procedures required to advertise the intention of
introducing a Traffic Regulation Order in so far as it relates to
the introduction of Prohibition of Waiting, At Any Time
restrictions on lengths of Leather’s Lane and Beechwood
Avenue, Halewood as detailed on the drawing attached in Appendix B
to this report, pursuant to the provisions of sections 1 to 5 of the Road
Traffic Regulation Act 1984, and if no objections are made
within the objection period or no objections remain unwithdrawn, to
make the Order. 





 

Single yellow line restrictions were
considered and subsequently discounted on the basis that the
highway code states that vehicles should never park near a
junction, whereas a single yellow line would allow parking at
certain times of the day.
 
Doing nothing was considered and rejected as
this will result in vehicles being parked in a manner that impacts
and compromises road safety for traffic and pedestrians on
Leather’s Lane at the junctions with Beechwood Avenue,
Halewood.
topline: The Executive Director Regeneration and Economic Development has decided to introduce a Traffic Regulation Order for a prohibition of waiting on Leather's Lane and Beechwood Avenue in Halewood.

decision_maker: Interim Executive Director Childrens (Hilary Brooks) and Executive Director Resources (Stephan Van Arendsen)
purpose:
The purpose of this report is to seek approval
to establish and recruit to a new Locality Manager post (Grade O)
which will focus on the effective delivery of the Best Start for
life offer in a particular area of the borough. This post in the
Best Start for Life team will support the development and
implementation of the offer to Knowsley families, focusing
particularly on the requirements of the strategy ‘Giving
Every Child the Best Start in Life’ which was released by The
Department for Education in July this year.
content:
The purpose of this report is to seek approval
to establish and recruit to a new Locality Manager post (Grade O)
which will focus on the effective delivery of the Best Start for
life offer in a particular area of the borough. This post in the
Best Start for Life team will support the development and
implementation of the offer to Knowsley families, focusing
particularly on the requirements of the strategy ‘Giving
Every Child the Best Start in Life’ which was released by The
Department for Education in July this year.
 

That the Interim Executive Director
(Children's) and the Executive Director (Resources) are recommended
to agree the establishment of a Locality Manager at Grade O on a
fixed term two-year basis to support the delivery of the Start for
Life and Beyond Offer.
 

If this post was not created there would be a
risk that as a council we would be unable to deliver the
requirements outlined in the government strategy and Knowsley
families and young children would be disadvantaged. The Best Start
for life team does not currently have the sufficient capacity to
work with colleagues and partners to develop and deliver key
strategies and programmes, which is delaying progress, particularly
to the Best Start for Life offer.
topline: The Interim Executive Director Childrens and Executive Director Resources have decided to establish a new Locality Manager post to support the delivery of the Best Start for Life offer.
